title: Predation and stealing are counted at runtime, surfaced live, and never stored in the closure report
missing: deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[] carries no predation field. SimStats already accumulates predation_actions_attempted_total, predation_actions_transferred_total, predation_actions_rejected_total, predation_kills_total, and predation_actions_by_result; the live server copies all of them (crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:279-282, crates/v3-server/src/transport/protocol.rs:53-56, :223-226), so the plumb into the report is a copy of counters that already exist and are already read elsewhere.
evidence: grep for predation_actions_attempted_total / predation_kills_total across crates/ returns hits only in crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs and crates/v3-server/*; zero hits in crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs. Key-tree dump of docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json (321 distinct keys) contains no key matching 'predat' or 'steal'. The action is reachable by mutation: crates/v3-core/src/runtime/action_decode.rs:20 decodes code 4 as StealEnergy and crates/v3-core/src/mutation/graph/operators.rs:256 can emit WorldActionKind::StealEnergy; PredationConfig has no enable flag and defaults to steal_cost_rate 0.05 (crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:826-830).
why: Whether any evolved lineage makes a living off other creatures rather than off food cannot be answered from a stored closure report at all — not even negatively. A closure cannot state that predation was absent, because absence and non-measurement are the same reading today.
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t05-biotic-interactions-and-coevolution.md, Notes for AI Agents: "Report applied interactions, including absence; enabling the mechanism does not establish coevolution." (The note is addressed to T05.F01/F02/F06, which have not started; the point is that the reporting obligation it states cannot be met today for the StealEnergy interaction that already exists.)
proposal: Add the five existing cumulative predation counters to WorldTracking in crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs (beside typed_eats_total), so they are stored per case and, because WorldTracking is flattened into PersistenceSample, also at each 100-tick sample. No new runtime counting, no new derived quantity.
refutations: WEAK REFUTATION on LENS 2 ownership only — every factual leg of the claim verified true. FACTS CONFIRMED: (a) RUNTIME layer has all five counters, crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:300-305, each incremented from applied behavior in crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:58 (attempted), :74 and :87 (rejected), :128 (kills), :130 and :149 (transferred), :76/:89/:132/:151 (by_result) — no permanently-dead field. (c) LIVE layer copies all of them, crates/v3-server/src/transport/protocol.rs:223-227, crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:76-81. (b) STORED layer has zero: `grep -rin "predat|steal" crates/v3-cli/` returns exactly one hit, bench.rs:5201, and it is the English word "predate" in a doc comment; `grep -c "predat|steal"` on docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json returns 0. Reachability confirmed: action_decode.rs:20 decodes 4 as StealEnergy, mutation/graph/operators.rs:256 emits it, PredationConfig (config/simulation.rs:817-833) has no enable flag and defaults steal_cost_rate 0.05, and it is applied in tick.rs:990. Proposal mechanics confirmed: WorldTracking is at bench.rs:1318 with typed_eats_total at :1321, and it is `#[serde(flatten)]`ed into PersistenceSample at bench.rs:1461-1462, so the per-case and per-sample storage the finder describes is exactly how the existing fields land. REFUTED BECAUSE AN OPEN FEATURE OWNS IT: T05.F03 — Frequency-Dependent Interaction Telemetry, docs/roadmaps/t05-biotic-interactions-and-coevolution.md:26-27, "Record interaction outcomes by lineage so frequency-dependent dynamics are visible in the goal profile; observation only." StealEnergy is the only creature-on-creature interaction that exists, so goal-profile interaction telemetry is nominally T05.F03's schema. The same track claims the substrate explicitly at :41 ("Extend the existing `StealEnergy` interaction and predation accounting only where they provide sound primitives") and attaches the reporting-absence obligation to T05.F01/F02/F06 at :39. THE REFUTATION IS WEAK, AND I SAY SO EXPLICITLY: T05.F03 is UNSCHEDULED — `sed -n '45p' docs/roadmap.md` (the priority order for new starts) contains no T05 ID at all, and T05.F03 depends on T05.F01, which has not started; T05.F01 may also replace or subsume the current StealEnergy accounting, so it is arguable that no open feature owns these five aggregate totals. That uncertainty is why the verdict lands on refuted per the default-to-refuted rule, not because a scheduled owner exists. MISATTRIBUTION: the criterion the finder cites (t05:39) is addressed to features that have not started and is not binding today — the finder concedes this in its own text. None of the seven Final Success Criteria in docs/roadmap.md requires predation or interaction reporting. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: the underlying (a)+(c)-not-(b) gap is real, cheap, and satisfies the hard constraints (applied behavior, no derived score, no RNG consumption); it is blocked only by an unscheduled nominal owner, not by a criterion or a cost objection.
corrections: Narrower, corrected framing (the gap itself stands): (1) The cited criterion is prospective, not binding. docs/roadmaps/t05-biotic-interactions-and-coevolution.md:39 ("Report applied interactions, including absence") obligates T05.F01/F02/F06, all still unchecked at :22/:24/:32. No current closure criterion requires predation in the stored report, so this proposal is justified by the absence-vs-non-measurement argument alone, not by an existing obligation. (2) "Whether any evolved lineage makes a living off other creatures" overstates what these counters answer: they are population-wide cumulative totals with no lineage, generation, or per-creature attribution. A nonzero predation_actions_transferred_total establishes that stealing occurred at all, not that any lineage subsists on it; per-lineage attribution is T08.F02 / T04.F01 territory. The defensible claim is the narrow one: a closure report today cannot state that predation was absent, because zero and unmeasured are the same reading. (3) Implementation notes for whoever picks this up: predation_actions_by_result is keyed by an enum, so storing it needs PredationActionResult::as_key() stringification (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:26-36), the same conversion protocol.rs:57 already performs; and kill_complexity_bonus_multiplier defaults to 0.0 (config/simulation.rs:829), so the only payoff from a kill is the stolen energy minus the 5% attempt cost — a low stored kill count should be read as "unbonused," not as "predation is unrewarding by design."

Five predation counters (attempted, transferred, rejected, kills, by_result) exist as applied simulation behavior in SimStats and are surfaced live by v3-server, but are never stored in the closure report, so a closure cannot state predation's absence; the fix is a copy of existing counters into WorldTracking. However, no scheduled feature and no Final Success Criterion requires this reading today, and the criterion the finder cites is addressed to unstarted T05.F01/F02/F06; T05.F03 (Frequency-Dependent Interaction Telemetry) nominally owns goal-profile interaction telemetry but is unscheduled — absent from roadmap.md's priority order — and blocked by unstarted T05.F01.

Narrower claim: the five existing predation counters are absent from the stored closure report, and plumbing them into WorldTracking (bench.rs:1357) is a near-zero-cost way to record whether the already-live StealEnergy interaction fired at all, and at what volume, in each baseline case. Four narrowings: (1) The cited T05 note is real but binds T05.F01/F02/F06, all unstarted; no Final Success Criterion (roadmap.md:34-40) and no checked track item requires predation reporting today, so this is an opportunistic cheap plumb, not a criterion-blocking gap. The same note licenses it ("Extend the existing StealEnergy interaction and predation accounting only where they provide sound primitives"), so it is compatible with, not a substitute for, the eventual owner. (2) "Whether any evolved lineage makes a living off other creatures" overstates what aggregate counters deliver: they answer population-level presence/absence and volume only; per-lineage attribution ("who eats whom") is T05.F03, which depends on unstarted T05.F01. (3) The live server's copy is split, not uniform: the status path carries four scalars (state.rs:279-282) and only the health path carries predation_actions_by_result (state.rs:575-580). (4) predation_actions_by_result is keyed by the PredationActionResult enum (stats.rs:305), so it needs a small serializable conversion like the existing by_reader_state helper rather than a literal field copy. Also note founders do not emit StealEnergy (cgp.rs:573 is a serde roundtrip test, not the founder profile), so the stored values may read zero on current baselines; that is the absence-recording value of the change, not evidence against it.

title: Per-food-type occupied-cell count is computed every tick and discarded before it reaches SimStats
missing: FoodTypeTelemetry carries both occupied_cells and total_density, and the growth pass fills both every tick (crates/v3-core/src/kernel/ordinary_food/ecology.rs:36-42, :544-553). SimStats::record_food_growth_summary keeps only total_density and drops occupied_cells (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:394-397: last_tick_food_total_density_by_type.extend(summary.per_type.iter().map(|entry| entry.total_density))). So the stored food_density_total is the only standing-food reading, and food area is unrecoverable.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/kernel/ordinary_food/ecology.rs:36-42 (struct FoodTypeTelemetry) and :544-553 (telemetry.occupied_cells += 1 per cell with density > 0.0); crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:394-397 (only total_density retained); crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1393 (food_density_total reads last_tick_food_total_density_by_type). The only 'occupied' key in the stored goal JSON is moves_blocked_total_by_cause.occupied.
why: A single total density cannot distinguish food spread thin over the whole map from food concentrated in surviving patches, and patch structure is what sets regrowth: grazed cells regrow only from dense neighbors. From the stored report you cannot say whether Orchards' sixty meadows persisted as patches or the grass was smeared out to a uniform film at the same total density.
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t12-world-composition-and-baseline-worlds.md, Amendment 2026-09-09: "Orchards in grassland keeps grass as the founders' food, diffuse and very slowly regrowing except in sixty meadows" — the meadow structure the recipe is built around has no stored reading.
proposal: Add last_tick_food_occupied_cells_by_type to SimStats, filled from the occupied_cells already present in FoodGrowthSummary, and carry it into WorldTracking beside food_density_total in crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs. Two lines of plumbing; no new computation in the tick loop.
corrections: Four narrowings. (1) Line cite: `FoodTypeTelemetry` is ecology.rs:17-22 with `occupied_cells` at :20; the finder's ":36-42" points at `DepletionTickSummary` (ecology.rs:34-38), a different struct whose `occupied_cells` counts creature-occupied cells. The ":544-553" and stats.rs cites are correct. (2) Overstated payoff: `occupied_cells` plus `total_density` yields area and mean density per occupied cell, which does distinguish food spread thin over the map from food concentrated at the same total — but it measures neither patch count nor contiguity, so it cannot answer "did Orchards' sixty meadows persist as patches." The defensible claim is that post-run food area and mean intensity are unmeasured, not that patch structure would become readable. (3) "Unrecoverable" applies to post-run standing food only; tick-zero coverage is recoverable from the pinned recipe and `config_digest` in the stored profile. (4) The proposal is sound and constraint-compliant: the kernel already computes the count over applied food state (no new tick-loop work, no RNG, no composite score), and a `last_tick_food_occupied_cells_by_type` field carried into `WorldTracking` would inherit exactly the last-tick-snapshot semantics `food_density_total` already has — which should be stated, since like `food_density_total` it is a final-tick snapshot, not a cumulative or time-averaged reading.

Three overstatements to narrow. (1) Line cites: `ecology.rs:36-42` is `DepletionTickSummary`, not `FoodTypeTelemetry` — the struct is `:18-22` and the increment `:549`. (2) The "criterion cited" is not a criterion. The quoted sentence is verbatim, but it sits in the descriptive Amendment 2026-09-09 at docs/roadmaps/t12-world-composition-and-baseline-worlds.md:49, which records what the Orchards recipe is, not what must be measured. The nearest real track success criterion is T12 #4 (line 22), "each recipe with a stored persistence reading at production defaults, and every environmental mechanism feature closed after it records its readings on that set" — it names persistence, not food area; the closest actual sanction is line 47's "Store effective config identity, persistence, and applied pressure readings", which also does not name it. So the gap is under-covered by the track rather than mandated by it. (3) `occupied_cells` measures per-type standing-food footprint (area), not patch structure: sixty surviving meadows and one blob of equal total footprint read identically. The finder's "whether Orchards' sixty meadows persisted as patches" claims more than the field delivers — the defensible claim is that it separates food smeared thin over the map from food concentrated in a small footprint at the same total density, which is the distinction that matters because regrowth spreads only from dense neighbors. On ownership: the natural home is the next environmental-mechanism feature that reads the baseline set — T02.F05 (Natural Disturbance and Recovery) cannot measure "recolonization" from a density total alone, and T02.F04 (Grazing Recovery and Overuse) has the same need — so this can either land as the two-line plumbing now or be folded into whichever of those closes first, rather than becoming a standalone feature.

Two refinements, both narrowing rather than undermining. (a) Layer label: the quantity is not "runtime-absent" in the sense of never being computed — it is computed every tick and dropped at the SimStats boundary (stats.rs:394-397), and the live server independently builds full per-type density planes for the frontend (`crates/v3-server/src/query/cache.rs:102`), so per-type area is derivable in the running app; the gap is specific to SimStats and everything downstream, i.e. the stored closure report. (b) The fix is stronger than "one number" but weaker than "patch structure": `WorldTracking::observe` is called inside `PersistenceAccumulator::observe` (bench.rs:1780-1787, 1883), so `food_density_total` already appears in each of the 20 persistence samples per seed per world — a new `occupied_cells` field would inherit that and give a 20-point area trajectory, and area plus total density yields mean density per occupied cell. But it is a scalar count of cells with density > 0, not a clustering statistic: it separates "thin film over most of the map" from "concentrated in fewer cells" (the finder's stated question), yet cannot distinguish sixty coherent meadows from the same number of vegetated cells scattered as speckle. State the reading as per-type vegetated area, not as a meadow-shape measure.

title: Lineage diversity is a single terminal scalar pair, so a stable diversity level cannot be told from one still collapsing
missing: surviving_founder_clade_count and shannon_entropy_nats are computed once, after the run ends, from the final creature set. PersistenceSample — taken every 100 ticks and at the final tick — carries tick, population, mean_energy, births_total and a flattened WorldTracking, and no lineage field. There is no clade count at any earlier tick, and the clade size distribution is discarded at the point it is built.
evidence: crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1901-1906 calls lineage_diversity once inside observe_goal_indicators.then(...) after the run; :1979-2003 builds counts: BTreeMap<u32,u64> and returns only counts.len() and the entropy, discarding the distribution; :1455-1462 (struct PersistenceSample) has no lineage field; :1779-1785 is the per-sample push. lineage_id is the founder index and is inherited unchanged (crates/v3-core/src/creature/identity.rs:15-22, :29, :93), so the count is bounded by the founder count and monotone non-increasing.
why: The goal-v1 baseline reads 142/144/140 surviving clades out of 10,000 founders (docs/roadmap.md:52) — a 98.6% loss with no recorded timing. If that loss lands during the tick-150 peak-and-crash, the indicator is measuring the founding lottery rather than anything a closed feature changed, and no closure can tell the difference. That is precisely T04.F01's stated pull-forward trigger, and it is not readable from the current report.
criterion: docs/roadmap.md:34: "The goal profile's ecological-diversity indicators (surviving lineage count and lineage entropy first, richer strategy measures as they are added) rise across the series of closed features relative to the goal series' first reading, and each rise survives at least one later feature." Also docs/roadmaps/t04-population-structure-and-diversification.md, Notes: T04.F01 "can be pulled forward whenever the lineage-count indicator stops being informative enough."
proposal: Add surviving_founder_clade_count and shannon_entropy_nats as direct fields on PersistenceSample (beside population and mean_energy — they are snapshots, not cumulative behavior, so they do not belong inside WorldTracking, which is documented as cumulative). Reuse the existing lineage_diversity function at each of the ~20 sample ticks; it is O(N) per sample against 2,000 ticks of simulation. Optionally add largest_clade_share, which is one line off the counts map already built.
corrections: The claim is correct; only its evidence row is stale, and the current row makes the point more sharply rather than less. The 142/144/140 clades and the tick-150 peak-and-crash are the goal-v1 figures (docs/roadmap.md:50, :52). The current series row — t13-f01, goal-worlds-v1, same 10,000 founders (bench.rs:167) — reads 22/24/14 surviving clades, a 99.8% loss, and its stored trajectory peaks at 100,000 by ticks 61-65 and is already down to 2,517/8,712/4,097 by tick 200, so the unmeasured window is the first ~200 ticks and 18 of the 20 stored samples sit after it. Two mechanical corrections to the proposal: sampling also fires at extinction, not only every 100 ticks and the last tick (bench.rs:1749-1751); and the gate report also carries `population_persistence.samples`, so a plain (non-Option) field on `PersistenceSample` would be computed inside `make check` too — cost there is one BTreeMap over ~3,000 creatures on a single sample tick per seed, negligible, but the field should either be gated on `observe_goal_indicators` (as `lineage_diversity` already is, bench.rs:1901) or declared as accepted negligible gate cost rather than "gate untouched."

The gap and the code evidence are correct; three narrowings. (1) Proposal placement: `PersistenceAccumulator` is constructed unconditionally at bench.rs:1868, NOT behind `observe_goal_indicators` (bench.rs:1898, set at :2404/:2490 by `params.name == "goal" || world_set`). Adding the fields directly to `PersistenceSample` as proposed would also compute them in the gate profile (gate_profile_params: 256 founders, 75 ticks, bench.rs:145-157 — so exactly one sample, negligible cost, but it changes the gate report shape). The feature should either gate the new fields on `observe_goal_indicators` or state that the gate report gains them. (2) "Why it matters" is overstated on responsiveness: the terminal indicator is not inert. Across stored goal reports the seed-11 count reads 142 (T01.F12) -> 118 (T11.F02) -> 180 (T11.F04) -> 214 (T11.F07) -> 137 (T11.F16) -> 161 (T11.F17) -> 142 (T11.F18). The real gap is within-run timing and attribution, not responsiveness. The concrete case is better than the hypothetical tick-150 framing: T11.F17 seed 33 read 54 clades at 0.159 nats with 11,379 creatures alive, and docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:106 records it as an open user concern alongside 12.05% of that population running to the VM step cap — a per-sample clade series would have shown whether that was an early founder-lottery loss or a late sweep by the cap-hitting bloom, and the report cannot say. (3) Do not read the newest 22/24/14 as a continuation of 142/144/140: T12.F04 replaced the goal world set, so that step is a world change, not a series decline. Also, "precisely T04.F01's stated pull-forward trigger" is loose — the trigger at t04:40 is the indicator becoming uninformative; the claim is that its informativeness cannot currently be evaluated. Related, not identical.

The gap is real, but the claim is overstated in three ways. (1) STALE EPOCH: 142/144/140 clades at entropy 2.78/2.95/2.67 is the goal-v1 row (T01.F12, three seeds on one 1600x1600 world). The current goal-worlds-v1 row, docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json, reads 22, 24 and 14 surviving clades with entropy 2.360513 / 2.625223 / 0.882285, and per_seed is now one seed per WORLD (seed 11 Orchards, 22 Canyon, 33 Confluence) rather than three replicates. Founders are still 10,000 (bench.rs:167 goal_profile_params, applied at bench.rs:284; the three recipe JSONs under experiments/worlds/ set region geometry only and do not override initial_creatures). So the live loss is ~99.8%, not 98.6%, and Confluence is near-monoculture at 0.88 nats — the timing gap is more acute than the finder states, not less. (2) THE CRITERION DOES NOT LITERALLY REQUIRE A TIME SERIES: the Final Success Criteria bullet compares terminal readings across closed features, and a terminal scalar satisfies its text. The actual need comes from two other roadmap rules — the Evidence-classes note ("a feature is judged by the mechanism it adds, and the indicator only records what that mechanism did") and T04's stated pull-forward trigger. This is an attribution defect, not a criterion the report currently fails to satisfy. (3) NO OWNING FEATURE NAMED: roadmap.md requires that any feature introducing a diversity measure wires its indicator into the goal profile as part of that same feature. Sampling the existing clade count over time is much smaller than T04.F01 (a full parent-child ancestry graph) but sits inside T04's ownership, so it needs a home — a new T04 observation-only row, or a folded-in piece of T04.F01's scope — rather than an unowned edit to PersistenceSample. The proposal's placement argument is otherwise sound: WorldTracking is documented as cumulative (bench.rs:1358), so snapshot fields do belong beside population and mean_energy.

title: A failed Eat (NoFood) is not counted at any layer, so foraging failure and attempted niche shifts are invisible
missing: execute_eat increments last_tick_eat on every attempt but increments eat_actions_applied_total_by_type only on success; on failure it sets ActionResult::NoFood, debits the failed-action penalty, and records nothing. No eat-failure counter exists in SimStats, cumulative or per-tick, and no per-creature lifetime eat counter exists either. The failure reaches only the per-creature action-log ring buffer.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:722 (last_tick_eat += 1, unconditional), :727 (eat_actions_applied_total_by_type incremented inside the succeeded branch), :731 (action_result = ActionResult::NoFood; debit_failed_action). grep for eat_actions across crates/ returns exactly three non-test hits: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:242, tick.rs:727, bench.rs:1387. grep for NoFood in v3-core returns tick.rs:731 and crates/v3-core/src/creature/action_log.rs only. crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:189-197 lists every per-creature lifetime counter: action_attempted, blocked_move, invalid_reproduce, energy_sum, energy_sample_count — no eat count.
why: Blocked moves are instrumented exhaustively (by cause, by barrier-reader state, with an avoidable-share denominator) and are the stored reading for barrier pressure; the eating analogue has no counter at all. Concretely: a lineage that mutates its Eat type parameter toward the latent fruit niche while standing in grass fails every bite, and typed_eats_total records only successes — so an attempted-but-failed niche shift, and the energy it burns through the failed-action penalty, are both invisible.
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t12-world-composition-and-baseline-worlds.md, Amendment 2026-09-09: "founders emit food type 0 in their Eat action, so a second food is edible only to a lineage that changes that parameter (Confluence's 5% fruit eat share at T12.F04 shows it can happen)." (A track note, not a checkbox criterion.)
proposal: Add eat_actions_rejected_total_by_type: HashMap<OrdinaryFoodTypeId, u64> to SimStats, incremented in the existing else branch at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:731 keyed by the requested type_idx (already in scope), and carry it into WorldTracking beside typed_eats_total. Keyed by requested type is what makes the attempted niche shift readable.
corrections: Two narrowings. (1) "Records nothing" is slightly overstated: the failure does reach `OutcomeAccumulator::record_action_result(ctx.id, false)` at tick.rs:723 (outcomes.rs:53-60), which feeds the Phase 2.5 reward-modulated plasticity pass, and the per-creature action-log entry is exposed over the server API (docs/reference/v3-server-api-protocol-spec.md:734 lists `NoFood`). Neither is a counter and neither aggregates, so the telemetry gap stands — the accurate statement is "no aggregate records it", not "nothing records it". (2) Sharper form of the harm than the finder gives: a failed eat DOES increment `lifetime_action_attempted_count` (tick.rs:721) and therefore `MutationValueTotals.action_attempted_total`, while `invalid_action_total = blocked_move_total + invalid_reproduce_total` (simulation/simulation.rs:135) excludes it. A lineage that mutates its Eat type toward the latent fruit niche and fails every bite thus inflates the denominator of `invalid_action_rate` while contributing nothing to the numerator, making its failure read as improved action quality. Also: no planned feature covers this — T03.F04 (docs/roadmaps/t03-...md:29-30, "Guts", blocked on T02.F01/T03.F01) is a digestion mechanism, not a typed-eat reading, so it is the natural downstream consumer rather than existing coverage. Spec-time detail for whoever implements: a mutated Eat parameter can name a type index beyond `food.types.len()` — such a request always fails, and the bench.rs:1384 `0..types.len()` carry pattern would silently drop exactly those events, which are the clearest attempted-niche-shift cases.

Narrower claim: a failed Eat's ATTEMPT is counted — tick.rs:722 (last_tick_eat, unconditional), tick.rs:606-612 (actions_applied_total sums last_tick_eat, so failures ride into the stored report's per_seed actions_applied), tick.rs:719 (lifetime_action_attempted_count), and outcomes.rs:53-58 (OutcomeAccumulator.actions_attempted vs actions_succeeded, feeding the ActionSuccess signal, which is applied behavior rather than telemetry). What does not exist anywhere outside the per-creature action-log ring buffer is a counter that DISTINGUISHES an eat failure from an eat success. Consequences: the untyped per-tick failure count is reconstructible online at layer (c) as last_tick_eat minus the per-tick delta of the summed eat_actions_applied_total_by_type, but that needs a differencing consumer, loses the requested type, and is stored nowhere; the requested type of a failed eat is unrecoverable at every layer; and in the stored closure report (b) the gap is total, since eat attempts are lumped into actions_applied with every other action type while typed_eats_total / typed_eat_share record successes only. So "not counted at any layer" should read "the attempt is counted but its failure is never distinguished, and the requested type of a failed eat is never recorded." Add that failed eats are also excluded from invalid_action_total (simulation.rs:135) — the blocked-move asymmetry stated concretely — though that quantity is layer (a) only and never reaches the goal JSON.

Narrower claim: no failure-specific or per-type eat-failure count exists at any layer, and the asymmetry with the exhaustively instrumented move path is real — but four narrowings apply. (1) "Records nothing" overstates. The attempt is folded into last_tick_eat and thence into cumulative actions_applied_total (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:606-613), so the stored deterministic.actions_applied already counts eat attempts rather than eat successes; the failure also feeds plasticity through OutcomeAccumulator::record_action_result (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/outcomes.rs:53-59). What is absent is a failure-specific or per-type-keyed count, not any trace of the attempt. (2) The cited line (docs/roadmaps/t12-world-composition-and-baseline-worlds.md:49) is a design note, not a checkbox criterion. None of T12's six track criteria and no master Final Success Criterion in docs/roadmap.md:34-40 requires eat-failure telemetry, and the note's own evidence (Confluence's 5% fruit eat share) is a success reading that did not ask for this counter. The justification is the move/eat instrumentation asymmetry, not an unmet criterion. (3) The proposal has no owning feature. Under the workflow, telemetry rides on the mechanism feature that reads it; the natural homes are T03.F04 (digestion specialization per type, the body side of exactly this diet-shift question) or T02.F04 (grazing recovery and overuse, where depletion-driven eat failure is the overuse signal), not a standalone counter add. (4) The proposal's keying is under-specified. crates/v3-core/src/runtime/action_decode.rs:29-35 clamps the decoded index to 0..=u16::MAX, not to the configured type count, and crates/v3-core/src/kernel/world.rs:147-150 returns 0.0 for invalid types, so out-of-range requests fail identically to depleted-cell failures. Keyed by requested type, those land under nonexistent type ids that crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1384's (0..world.food.types.len()) vector would silently drop; the reading needs an explicit out-of-range bucket. Also note the niche-shift reading only has content on the two-type goal worlds (Orchards, Confluence), never on the one-food production Plains default.

title: Standing food stock is stored but neither realized regrowth nor density consumed is accumulated anywhere
missing: The growth pass accumulates only suppressed growth (growth_suppressed_by_occupancy_depletion, growth_suppressed_by_type_inhibition); realized growth — the density actually added — is never summed. On the consumption side, execute_eat has the consumed amount in hand (food_before) and pushes it only into the per-creature action log; no density-consumed total exists. typed_eats_total counts eat events, not density, so differencing samples yields bites, not energy moved.
evidence: grep for grown|growth_total|regrow|food_eaten|amount over crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs and crates/v3-core/src/kernel/ordinary_food/ecology.rs returns only stats.rs:339 and :343, both 'suppressed' fields. crates/v3-core/src/kernel/ordinary_food/ecology.rs:558-565 (FoodGrowthSummary construction: suppressed totals only). crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:719 and :725 (food_before captured, assigned to amount, passed only to push_action_log at :735-743).
why: T12.F04 made regrowth rate and recovery rate per-type knobs; nothing records what those knobs actually delivered. Standing density at 20 checkpoints shows the stock but not whether it is a fast turnover under heavy grazing or a stagnant field nobody is eating — two ecologies with identical stored readings.
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t12-world-composition-and-baseline-worlds.md, Track Success Criteria (checked): "Food types can differ in energy per bite, coverage, regrowth, and recovery through the world config alone, production defaults unchanged, so a rich rare food and a poor abundant one can share a world."
proposal: Add two cumulative per-type totals to SimStats: food_grown_total_by_type, summed in the existing next_density write loop in crates/v3-core/src/kernel/ordinary_food/ecology.rs:544-553 and carried out on FoodGrowthSummary beside the suppressed totals; and food_eaten_density_total_by_type, summed at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:725 where amount is already computed. Carry both into WorldTracking. Both are applied simulation behavior, not derived rates.
refutations: LENS 3 (need) fails, though the runtime facts check out. (1) The cited criterion is real and quoted verbatim but is ALREADY CLOSED and is a capability criterion, not a measurement one: docs/roadmaps/t12-world-composition-and-baseline-worlds.md:19 is "- [x]" and demands the knobs work "through the world config alone, production defaults unchanged". The same track's 2026-09-09 amendment states outright "Track criteria 2 and 3 are met at T12.F04". It requires that a rich rare food and a poor abundant one CAN be configured to share a world; it does not require accounting of what the knobs delivered. (2) The program has already defined what "food pressure measured every closure" means, and it is stored. The T12.F04 amendment reads Canyon's goal line as "barrier pressure present and measured every closure (barrier-blocked move fraction and the barrier-block rate split by barrier-reader state)"; the food-side analogue shipped in the same feature as typed_eat_share / typed_eats_total / food_density_total (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:451, 1321, 1324; 71 and 63 occurrences in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json). The precedent the finder leans on is satisfied for food, not violated. (3) The natural owner exists and is scheduled: T02.F04 "Grazing Recovery and Overuse" — "A patch grazed too recently yields less and recovers slowly, so the value of a place depends on its history" — and T02 track criterion 3 ("Disturbance and recovery support measurable resilience, recolonization, and strategy turnover", T02.F05). Both are bound by the shared baseline contract to record their pressure readings at their own closure. (4) No open criterion needs it: roadmap.md Final Success Criteria (lines 34-40) cover diversity indicators, cognition indicators, compute regression, mutational neighborhood, reproducibility, progress rows, and natural analogs — none touches food turnover. Adding two flux counters now, ahead of the consuming feature, is telemetry without a consumer, against the user's standing "basic diversity/cognition tracking + perf regression only" preference and the rejected-as-overengineered precedent.
corrections:
Two narrow refinements; the gap and the layer call ("runtime-absent") both stand.

1. The finder's "20 checkpoints" is CORRECT and should not be softened — I checked, and `population_persistence.per_seed[].samples[]` does carry `food_density_total` per type alongside `typed_eats_total`, `births_total`, `mean_energy` and `population` (sample 0: tick 100, food_density_total ["254965.000000","468250.125000"], typed_eats_total [2347127, 4]). Because both are cumulative-or-standing across the 20 samples, differencing them yields net stock change and bites per interval. So the "two ecologies with identical stored readings" line is slightly overstated: a heavily grazed fast-turnover field and a stagnant one would differ in the net-change/bite-count profile. What is genuinely unrecoverable is gross flow — realized regrowth and density consumed — precisely because a bite takes the whole cell, so bites cannot be converted to mass at any known rate. Restate the "why it matters" as gross flow vs net stock rather than as indistinguishable readings.

2. The proposed insertion point needs one adjustment. ecology.rs:544-553 is the telemetry write loop and sees only final density, so it cannot sum a delta as written; but it can compute the realized increment there as `(next_density[idx] - state.food_at_type(Position::new(x, y), type_idx)).max(0.0)` immediately before the existing `set_food_type_density` call. Do not instead sum raw `spread_delta` (ecology.rs:486) and `recovery_delta` (ecology.rs:533) at the delta sites — both are clamped to `max_density` on write, so their sum overstates what was actually added.

The runtime-layer absence itself is REAL and fully verified — only the justification is misattributed, so the parent should keep the fact. Verified: realized regrowth is never accumulated (crates/v3-core/src/kernel/ordinary_food/ecology.rs:559-566 constructs FoodGrowthSummary with growth_suppressed_by_occupancy_depletion and growth_suppressed_by_type_inhibition only; the three delta sites at :426-427, :484-485, :530-532 sum suppression only; stats.rs:339 and :343 are the only matching fields). Consumed density is never accumulated: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:720 captures food_before, :725 assigns it to amount, :735 passes it only to push_action_log; and crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:71 confirms consume_food_type takes the whole cell, so food_before IS the consumed amount. eat_actions_applied_total_by_type counts events, not density, so differencing checkpoints yields bites, not energy moved. The proposal is also constraint-clean and cheap: both totals are applied simulation behavior (density actually added / actually removed), not a derived rate or composite score; no rayon appears in ecology.rs so accumulation is sequential and adds no determinism hazard beyond the existing suppressed totals. The narrower correct claim: this is a genuine but currently unconsumed runtime gap whose right home is T02.F04's (and T02.F05's) closure reading, wired in by the feature that needs it, not a T12 criterion shortfall.

Three narrowings. (1) Criterion attribution is wrong. The cited T12 criterion ("Food types can differ in energy per bite, coverage, regrowth, and recovery through the world config alone") is already checked [x] at docs/roadmaps/t12-world-composition-and-baseline-worlds.md:19, and it is about config knobs existing, not about measuring what they deliver — T12 track note line 49 explicitly records "Track criteria 2 and 3 are met at T12.F04". This gap leaves no track criterion unmet. The real hook is the shared baseline contract at docs/workflow.md:343-345, and it lands on T02.F01, not T12.F04. (2) The proposal's implementation site is right but the quantity named is wrong: summing `next_density[idx]` in the write loop at ecology.rs:544-553 yields standing stock, which is already `FoodTypeTelemetry::total_density`. Realized growth is the per-cell difference `next_density[idx] - state.food_at_type(pos, type_idx)` taken in that same loop before `set_food_type_density`, which is post-clamp and therefore applied behavior; note `next_density` is initialized to zeros (ecology.rs:392) and cells with `source <= 0.0` or barriers are skipped, so the difference must be floored at zero to avoid counting skipped cells as negative growth. The alternative is the three delta sites (~428, ~486, ~534), where the accumulator must sum the post-clamp applied change, not `local_delta`/`spread_delta`/`recovery_delta` as computed, since each write clamps at `max_density`. (3) "Energy moved" is loose: the proposed counter measures density removed from the world, and energy actually credited differs by the per-type `energy_per_unit` and the `max_energy` clamp (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:72-84). Density is the correct applied quantity for the turnover-vs-stagnant question, so the proposal is sound; only the phrasing overreaches. Minor layer clarification: the existing suppressed-growth fields are `last_tick_*` (layer c, per-tick), not cumulative, so neither realized nor suppressed growth accumulates in SimStats.

title: Every behavioral reading is a world total, so two lineages making a living in different ways cannot be distinguished
missing: WorldTracking::observe reads only global SimStats maps: typed_eats_total, moves_attempted_total, the blocked-move breakdowns, and the reader-state splits are all world-wide. Nothing in the stored report attributes any action to a lineage, and no per-creature counter exists that a terminal group-by could use: the creature carries only lifetime_action_attempted_count, lifetime_blocked_move_count, lifetime_invalid_reproduce_count, and energy sums. typed_eat_share is per-world, confirmed.
evidence: crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1358-1408 (WorldTracking::observe — every field sourced from sim.stats.*, no creature iteration); :1417-1430 (fractions() divides world totals by world totals); crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:189-197 (full list of per-creature lifetime counters; no eat, no move, no steal). The only per-creature iteration in the goal path is crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1901-1906, which reads lineage_id alone.
why: The Final Success Criteria call for ecological-diversity indicators that get richer, and strategy_count / strategy_causal_distinctness sit in the report as permanently Undefined placeholders. Today nothing in the stored report could distinguish a population where every clade forages identically from one where clades have split into distinct ways of feeding — the two produce the same typed_eat_share.
criterion: NONE
proposal: Add per-creature u32 counters for applied eats (by type) and applied moves at the sites that already increment last_tick_eat / last_tick_move (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:722, :765), inherited as zero at birth, then at the terminal observation group them by lineage_id — reusing the pass that already collects lineage_id — and store per-lineage eat/move counts for the largest few clades. Flagged as overlapping owned work: T05.F03 owns per-lineage interaction outcomes (blocked on T05.F01) and T01.F04 owns behavioral strategy descriptors (deferred proof phase); the foraging-mix half currently has no owner and no criterion, so this belongs in a lower bucket.
refutations: Factual layer verified and correct: WorldTracking::observe (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1358-1408) sources every field from sim.stats.* world totals, fractions() divides world totals by world totals (:1417-1440), and CreatureState (crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:189-197) carries only lifetime_action_attempted_count, lifetime_blocked_move_count, lifetime_invalid_reproduce_count and the energy sums — no per-creature eat or move counter. The gap is real. REFUTED on Lens 3 (program need), on three grounds. (1) The finder's core justification — "the foraging-mix half currently has no owner and no criterion" — is false. T01.F06 (docs/roadmaps/t01-experimental-science-and-causal-evaluation.md:37-38) is literally "Strategy count and causal distinctness measured from resource and interaction use, replacing the lineage-count tripwire," and T01.F04 (:33-34) is "Describe what a creature does from its actions and resource use so strategies can be compared without reading genomes." Both are marked "Deferred proof phase," and docs/roadmap.md:54 states T01.F01 through T01.F10 "stay on the roadmap as a later phase, no mechanism feature depends on them, and none is planned until the user asks for that phase." The strategy_count / strategy_causal_distinctness placeholders at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:490-491 (set to UNDEFINED at :2458-2459) are those owned features' keys, Undefined by design, not orphaned slots. This is exactly the confirmatory apparatus the user has explicitly deferred. (2) The proposed grouping key fails by an explicit roadmap ruling: docs/roadmaps/t04-population-structure-and-diversification.md:40 — "Petri's founder lineage_id is stable clade identity, not a complete parent-child ancestry graph and not evidence of an ecotype. T04.F01 adds the ancestry graph; ... can be pulled forward whenever the lineage-count indicator stops being informative enough" (echoed in the T01.F12 note at docs/roadmaps/t01-...:  "lineage is founder clade identity, not ecotype, so this is a collapse tripwire and trend, not a strategy count"). With 140-144 surviving clades descended from 10,000 identical founders (docs/roadmap.md:52), per-clade eat mix would track spatial position and clade size, not heritable foraging strategy — so the stated payoff ("clades split into distinct ways of feeding") is not what the proposed reading would deliver. T04.F01 (Ancestry Graph and Ecotype Observation, observation-only, depends only on the closed T01.F12) is the non-deferred owner of that question. (3) No criterion is cited, and the nearest one does not mandate this: docs/roadmap.md:34 requires the ecological-diversity indicators ("surviving lineage count and lineage entropy first, richer strategy measures as they are added") to rise — conditional on owning features shipping those measures, not a standing requirement to add per-lineage action attribution now. No HARD CONSTRAINT is violated by the mechanics themselves (applied-behavior counters, no RNG consumption, no composite score), but the need is not established.

REFUTED on Lens 2 (weak form — every owner is unscheduled/deferred, not in the pipeline). Three open features already own this telemetry: (1) T01.F04 "Behavioral Strategy Descriptors" (docs/roadmaps/t01-experimental-science-and-causal-evaluation.md:33-34) — "Describe what a creature does from its actions and resource use so strategies can be compared without reading genomes" is verbatim the foraging-mix half the finder claims "has no owner"; DEFERRED proof phase, depends on T01.F03 (also deferred). (2) T01.F06 "Ecological Diversity and Persistence Measures" (t01:37-38) — "Strategy count and causal distinctness measured from resource and interaction use, replacing the lineage-count tripwire" owns by name the two Undefined placeholders the finder cites; DEFERRED. (3) T05.F03 "Frequency-Dependent Interaction Telemetry" (docs/roadmaps/t05-biotic-interactions-and-coevolution.md:26-27) — "Record interaction outcomes by lineage so frequency-dependent dynamics are visible in the goal profile; observation only"; UNSCHEDULED (absent from roadmap.md:45's priority list) and dependency-blocked, T05.F01 unchecked at t05:22 and itself waiting on T03.F01. Scheduling caveat the consumer must read: T01.F04/F06 fall under roadmap.md:54, "none is planned until the user asks for that phase" — the deferred causal-proof apparatus the user explicitly deprioritized — so this is refutation by paper ownership, not by anything in flight. Also refuting the finder's "criterion cited: NONE": roadmap.md:34 is the governing Final Success Criterion and anticipates this exact extension ("surviving lineage count and lineage entropy first, richer strategy measures as they are added"); T01.F06 is that criterion's owner. The finder's runtime facts are confirmed exactly as cited: WorldTracking::observe (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1358-1408) sources every field from sim.stats.* world totals, fractions() (:1417-1430) divides world totals by world totals, CreatureState (crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:187-197) carries only offspring_spawned_count, lifetime_action_attempted_count, lifetime_blocked_move_count, lifetime_invalid_reproduce_count and the energy sums — no eat or move counter — and tick.rs:718-724/762-767 are indeed the last_tick_eat/last_tick_move increment sites next to lifetime_action_attempted_count. One near-counterexample that does NOT weaken the layer claim: the stored T13.F01 goal report does contain per-lineage rows (drift_depth.recruitment.lineages[], 50 synthetic drift-walk lineages with created/present/dispatched/contributing module counts, plus route_varying_lineages), but those are offline observation-harness walks, not population clades, and they carry module recruitment, not actions — the finder wrote "attributes any action to a lineage," which is precisely true. Finally, the refutation is about ownership, not feasibility: the proposed per-creature u32 eat-by-type/move counters grouped by lineage_id at terminal observation derive from applied behavior, add no composite score, consume no production RNG, and reuse the existing lineage_id pass (bench.rs:1901-1906), so nothing in the hard constraints blocks it if the user ever wants it pulled ahead of T01.F04/F06.
corrections: Two corrections, neither overturning the claim. (1) The finder's evidence line "The only per-creature iteration in the goal path is crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1901-1906, which reads lineage_id alone" is factually wrong. Two other per-creature iterations already run in that same goal path: bench.rs:1893-1897 walks `sim.creatures.values()` computing functional_complexity, and bench.rs:1900 calls `observe_final_actions(&sim)` (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:263-292), which returns, for every living creature, `FinalActionObservation { creature_id, intact: Vec<WorldAction>, zeroed, scrambled }` — the actual selected action queue at the terminal tick. It is already computed, documented as RNG-free and non-mutating (tick.rs:256-262), and joinable to `creature.identity.lineage_id` with no runtime change. Today it is consumed only as the world-wide memory_sensitivity fraction. (2) The layer tag must be split. "runtime-absent" is correct for *accumulated* per-creature applied eats/moves — the lifetime-counter reading the finder's proposal builds, which genuinely requires new runtime fields. But a *terminal-tick per-lineage action mix* is only stored-report-absent (layer b), not runtime-absent: the per-creature selected action and the lineage_id both already exist in the goal path, so grouping them is a bench.rs-only change with no v3-core edit, no new runtime state, and no added simulation cost. That cheaper variant should be flagged distinctly and considered before the lifetime-counter version, since it satisfies the applied-behavior constraint (a selected action queue is executed behavior, not a derived score) at near-zero closure budget; the lifetime-counter proposal remains the right shape if a cumulative foraging mix rather than a one-tick snapshot is what the indicator needs.

Per-lineage behavioral attribution is genuinely runtime-absent (verified at bench.rs:1358-1408 and creature/state.rs:189-197), but it is owned work, not an unowned gap: T01.F04 and T01.F06 own strategy descriptors and strategy count from resource use and are in the user-deferred proof phase, and lineage_id is the wrong key per docs/roadmaps/t04-population-structure-and-diversification.md:40 — T04.F01's ancestry graph is the non-deferred path if the ecotype question is ever wanted.

title: Nothing records where creatures are; the only spatial reading in the report describes rock at tick zero
missing: The report has no occupancy, dispersal, clustering, or per-region reading of the population. tick_zero_connectivity is computed from barriers alone, before any creature acts, and reports total/passable cells, passable fraction, largest component size and its fraction. bench.rs never reads a creature position.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/kernel/world.rs:24-32 (PassableConnectivity: five barrier-only fields) and :35-40 ("Observe barriers only, ignoring temporary creature occupancy"); crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1866 computes it before the run. grep for region|spatial|cluster|dispersal|position|centroid in crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs returns a single hit, a comment at line 222. The stored goal JSON key dump has no key matching 'region' or 'position'.
why: T12 built Canyon (about 47% barrier, 98% of passable cells in one component) and Confluence (fragmentation with corridors and straits) specifically to create spatial pressure, and later features are directed to read those worlds' connectivity fields — but those fields describe the terrain, not whether the population spread across the components, occupied one corner, or clustered in the meadows. Whether the spatial structure did anything to the population is not readable.
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t12-world-composition-and-baseline-worlds.md, Notes: "features that expected an isolated fragmentation or scarcity world read the composite and attribute against the plains and the persistence reading's connectivity fields."
proposal: At each persistence sample, label creatures by the passable component they stand in — reusing the flood fill in WorldState::passable_connectivity, extended to retain component labels rather than only sizes — and store population per component for the largest few components. Rank last: it is the only proposal here needing new machinery rather than plumbing, and T04.F03 (habitat patch and connectivity model) is its natural owner.
refutations:
REFUTED on Lens 3, though two refute triggers do NOT fire — state that clearly. NOT grounds for refusal: (1) hard constraints pass — creature position is applied simulation state, component labels derive from barriers, the read is read-only and consumes no production RNG, and it is neither a composite score nor a dashboard; (2) cost passes — barriers are tick-zero fixed, so one flood fill per case plus O(pop) labeling folded into the `sim.creatures.values()` iteration that already runs at every persistence sample (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1879) is not disproportionate; (3) the criterion is real and quoted verbatim (docs/roadmaps/t12-world-composition-and-baseline-worlds.md:48). The factual absence is also confirmed: `grep -nE "region|spatial|cluster|dispersal|position|centroid" crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs` returns exactly one hit, the comment at line 222; PassableConnectivity (crates/v3-core/src/kernel/world.rs:24-32) is five barrier-only fields, documented at :35 as "Observe barriers only, ignoring temporary creature occupancy", and bench.rs:1866 computes it before the tick loop.

What DOES refute, three points. FIRST, the cited criterion prescribes a different method that already exists. Its words are "read the composite and attribute against the plains and the persistence reading's connectivity fields" — a between-world attribution using connectivity as a terrain covariate, not a within-world spatial reading. That is readable today: goal_indicators.population_persistence.per_seed carries seeds 11/22/33, which map 1:1 to cases Orchards (seed 11), Canyon (22), Confluence (33), each with final/peak/minimum/plateau population, mean_energy, extinction_tick and 20 samples. The finder's "whether the spatial structure did anything to the population is not readable" is false; it is readable by the mechanism the criterion names, just not the one the finder searched for. The criterion does not require population-per-component.

SECOND, the proposal is degenerate on the checked-in baseline worlds. Measured largest_component_fraction_of_passable in the newest closure report (docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json): Orchards 1.0 (passable_fraction 1.0, no barriers at all), Canyon 0.9806, Confluence 0.9954 — under the 8-way flood fill (crates/v3-core/src/contracts/direction.rs:16, Direction::ALL) that matches actual movement topology, so these are true traversability components, not an artifact of 4-way counting. Residual off-largest passable area is ~26,236 cells in Canyon and ~9,111 in Confluence, spread across many fragments, each far below the 128x128 = 16,384-cell world that went extinct on every seed (docs/roadmaps/t04-population-structure-and-diversification.md:42). "Population per component for the largest few components" would therefore read ~100% in component 0 and transient zeros elsewhere on all three baselines. Confluence — the world the finder cites as built for fragmentation with corridors and straits — is in fact LESS isolated than Canyon; its fragmentation produces a tortuous single component, not separated ones.

THIRD, the proposal does not answer its own motivation. "occupied one corner, or clustered in the meadows" is a within-component distribution question; per-component labeling cannot see it, so even granting the machinery, the stated need goes unmet.

Residual worth carrying forward, not actionable now: the absence of any spatial reading of life is genuine, but it becomes a required indicator only once T04.F03 (Habitat Patch and Connectivity Model) makes connectivity a knob that actually yields isolated patches — and the roadmap rule that a feature introducing a diversity measure wires its indicator into the goal profile in the same feature already forces T04.F03 to carry it. It is not a current closure-report gap, and adding it against today's worlds would store a near-constant field.
corrections: Two narrowings. (1) "Nothing records where creatures are" overreaches: positions exist as live sim state, and the sim computes a per-creature local spatial summary every tick — `reduce_occupancy` (crates/v3-core/src/sensors/reducers.rs:217-242) builds neighbor count ratio, a local centroid (center_x/center_y sums), crowding, and nearest-neighbor offset within the observer's vision radius, exposed as `area_occupancy: [f32; 7]` (sensors/perception.rs:86) via `WorldInputKey::AreaOccupancySummary` (perception.rs:180) and echoed into the single-creature trace payload (v3-server/src/transport/sample_protocol.rs:55). That is a brain sensor input for one observer, not telemetry and not a population reading; it is never aggregated and never stored. So the finder's "needs new machinery" ranking is right in substance, but a flood fill is not the only spatial code in the tree. (2) The stored report does carry two location-free crowding proxies derived from live creature adjacency: `moves_blocked_total_by_cause.occupied` at case level (4.26M and 4.35M on the two cases) and inside every `population_persistence.per_seed[].samples[]` entry, plus the per-tick `last_tick_food_occupancy_depletion_occupied_cells` in layer (c). Corrected claim: no reading in any layer locates the population or distributes it across the world or its passable components; `tick_zero_connectivity` is barrier-only and pre-run by design, and the only occupancy-derived signals that reach the stored report are aggregate counts with no location.

Narrower claim: the stored goal report has no reading of the population's spatial DISTRIBUTION — which passable component or region it occupies, whether it spread or clustered — even though T12.F04 built Canyon and Confluence for spatial pressure and the T12 track directs later features to read "the persistence reading's connectivity fields", which describe terrain only (crates/v3-core/src/kernel/world.rs:22-31). Three overstatements to drop. (1) "Nothing records where creatures are" is too strong: cases[].moves_blocked_total_by_cause.occupied is stored per world case and derives from creature positions; the closed T12.F04 spec explicitly uses it as "a crowding reading" and notes "Occupancy blocks outnumber barrier blocks in every world" (docs/specs/roadmap/t12-f04-baseline-world-set.md:309-310). Crowding is readable; location is not. (2) "Whether the spatial structure did anything to the population is not readable" is wrong as stated: the T12.F04 amendment designates blocked_move_fraction and barrier_blocked_fraction_by_reader_state as exactly the reading of Canyon's barrier pressure on the population, and it was read at closure (58.5% vs 51.7% Canyon, 52.7% vs 54.8% Confluence; spec lines 304-309). What is unreadable is where the population sits, not whether barriers act on it. (3) The layer label "runtime-absent" holds for SimStats aggregates but not for the underlying data: the runtime holds every position in WorldState.creature_at: Grid<Option<CreatureId>> (crates/v3-core/src/kernel/world.rs:19) and already counts creature-occupied cells per tick as last_tick_food_occupancy_depletion_occupied_cells (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:338, layer (c), a global scalar, food-depletion-scoped, unstored). The gap is aggregation and storage, not missing data, so the cost is lower than "new machinery" implies — the flood fill at world.rs:35+ needs only to retain component labels it currently discards. Ownership: T04.F03 (docs/roadmaps/t04-...:26) is the natural owner and is UNSCHEDULED; the first scheduled features that will want the reading are T02.F03 and T02.F05, neither of which currently claims it.

title: No death-cause attribution: T03.F10's lethality claim was closed on a vm_steps proxy
missing: A per-cause death tally. `SimStats` has no death field of any kind; `Simulation::remove_creature` is the single funnel every death passes through (both the Phase 0 bulk removal and the Phase 2 `remove_creature_if_dead`) and increments no counter. Nothing records WHICH energy sink took a creature to <= 0.0: lifecycle charge (decay + genome carry), brain compute (VM dispatch settlement incl. the T03.F10 step ramp, priority bid, graph pass, plasticity, reward learning), action cost, reproduction transfer, or predation victim.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:86-109 — the whole of `remove_creature`; it builds a `MutationOutcomeObservation`, gates it on `!creature.birth_mutation_operators.is_empty()` (line 93), and increments no death counter. `grep -rniE 'death|mortality|deceased' crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs` returns exactly one hit, the doc comment at stats.rs:174. `grep -niE '\b(death|deaths|mortality)\b' crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs` returns nothing. T03.F10 spec docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f10-activity-ramped-compute-cost.md:33-35 (Non-Goals): "No new work counter, telemetry field, inspector annotation, or sensor. A cap-hit counter was considered and is not added: the goal profile's `vm_steps` reading is the instrument". Its Measured table (same file, ~line 385) closes the feature on `Goal vm_steps per creature-tick | 146.184594 | Down | 22.566373 (-84.563098%) | Met`, with population and clade readings the spec itself calls confounded ("the populations behind the three samples are different populations"). Energy-subtraction sites enumerated: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:162 (lifecycle), tick.rs:655 (failed-action penalty), tick.rs:1060 (reward learning), crates/v3-core/src/runtime/vm.rs:445 and :548 (bid, dispatch settlement incl. ramp), crates/v3-core/src/runtime/cgp/execute.rs:119 and :235 (graph pass, plasticity), crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:56/83/116 (action costs), actions/reproduction.rs:161/195, actions/predation.rs:67/100. IMPORTANT SCOPING FACT I verified so this is not overclaimed: the death COUNT is already derivable from the stored report — `deterministic.goal_indicators.population_persistence.per_seed[].samples[]` carries both `births_total` and `population` at 20 checkpoints (verified in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json), and with no immigration deaths-in-window = Δbirths − Δpopulation exactly. The absence is cause, not count. Also verified: a compute-exhausted creature is NOT removed in Phase 1 — it enters Phase 2 with the `decisions` vector (no zero-energy pre-filter at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:948-955), executes its NoOp, is floored to 0.0 at tick.rs:996-998 and removed at tick.rs:1000 — the same site as action-cost deaths, so a two-site (Phase 0 / Phase 2) split would NOT isolate compute deaths.
why: Whether T03.F10 actually made runaway computation lethal cannot be answered. The feature's stated mechanism is a causal chain — ramp charge -> energy exhaustion -> death removes the looper — and only the first link (vm_steps fell) and a confounded population reading were measured. `vm_steps` falling is equally consistent with loopers dying, with loopers never arising in the changed ecology, or with seed 33's bloom disappearing for unrelated reasons; the spec's own Measured section concedes the populations are not comparable. The same blindness applies to T03.F08: a carrying cost that is supposed to make junk 'pay for itself' can only be shown to bite through slower growth, never through a creature that died carrying too much. Every future energy-cost feature inherits the same proxy.
criterion: docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f10-activity-ramped-compute-cost.md:12-15 (Goal): "a run to the `max_vm_steps` cap costs a lethal fraction of a creature's energy, and the existing exhausted-energy path (queue discarded, `NoOp`, death at zero energy) removes the looping creature"
proposal: Add `death_cause: Option<DeathCause>` to `CreatureState`, set once at the first energy subtraction that takes the creature to <= 0.0 (five variants: `Lifecycle`, `BrainCompute`, `ActionCost`, `ReproductionTransfer`, `Predation`), and in `Simulation::remove_creature` increment `SimStats::deaths_total` and `SimStats::deaths_total_by_cause`. Store the per-seed map in the goal report beside `births`. This is applied behavior — it records which charge the simulation actually applied when the creature crossed zero, not a score. It is NOT the cap-hit counter T03.F10 rejected: that counter would have tallied dispatch outcomes (how many dispatches reached max_vm_steps), whereas this tallies removals, which is the link the closure could not read. Flag the tension with that non-goal for the user rather than assuming it is settled.
corrections: Three narrowings. (1) LAYER IS SPLIT, not uniformly "runtime-absent". Predation deaths ARE already counted at runtime: `predation_kills_total` at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:303, incremented at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:128 (alongside `last_tick_predation_kills` and `PredationActionResult::TransferredAndKilled`). It is consumed by v3-server (state.rs:282,578) but appears nowhere in the stored closure report — zero predation keys in either the goal or gate JSON. So the Predation cause is a cheap layer-(b) storage gap (surface an existing counter), while Lifecycle/genome-carry, BrainCompute (incl. the T03.F10 ramp), ActionCost and ReproductionTransfer are the genuine runtime-absent four. PredationConfig (crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:819-833) has no enable flag, so the counter is live in all three baseline worlds, not trivially zero. (2) "`Simulation::remove_creature` is the single funnel every death passes through" is FALSE and breaks the proposal as written. `grep -rn 'creatures.remove(' crates/v3-core/src/` returns exactly two sites: simulation.rs:87 (remove_creature, reached by both Phase 0's remove_creature_from_sim and Phase 2's remove_creature_if_dead via tick/helpers.rs:5-19) and actions/predation.rs:125, which removes the victim inline (world.remove_creature + creatures.remove + action_logs.remove) and never calls remove_creature. A `DeathCause::Predation` variant hooked only in remove_creature would never fire. The proposal must hook both sites, or route predation through remove_creature — and if it takes the latter route it must flag that predation victims would newly be recorded into `mutation_outcome_summary` / `mutation_value_totals_by_operator` (which they currently bypass), a behavior change to existing runtime stats rather than a pure addition. (3) "SimStats has no death field of any kind" is overstated on a second count: `carriers_observed_total` (stats.rs:18, incremented at stats.rs:46 from inside remove_creature) is an implicit exit/death count for creatures carrying birth mutations — also never stored (no carrier/outcome/viability keys in the report). Neither predation_kills_total nor carriers_observed_total is a cause attribution, so the finder's own framing "the absence is cause, not count" stands; the blanket "no death field of any kind" does not. The T03.F10 non-goal tension the finder flagged is real and should go to the user unresolved: :33-35 rejects a cap-hit counter, and while a removal tally is a different instrument, the same line also rejects any "new work counter, telemetry field" outright.

Narrower claim: four of the five death causes are runtime-absent (layer a); the fifth is stored-report-absent only (layer b). SimStats DOES have a death counter for one cause — predation_kills_total at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:303, plus PredationActionResult::TransferredAndKilled in predation_actions_by_result — so "SimStats has no death field of any kind" is overstated. That counter is simply never written into the stored goal report ("predation" and "kill" appear 0 times in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json), which makes the Predation slice a cheap layer-(b) plumbing fix rather than a runtime gap. Genuinely runtime-absent are the other four: Lifecycle (decay + genome carry), BrainCompute (incl. the T03.F10 ramp), ActionCost, and ReproductionTransfer. Separately, the proposal's implementation premise is wrong and would silently produce a zero: Simulation::remove_creature is NOT the single funnel every death passes through. Predation kills bypass it entirely — crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:124-126 removes the victim with sim.world.remove_creature(victim_pos); sim.creatures.remove(victim_id); sim.action_logs.remove(victim_id), never calling Simulation::remove_creature. A counter placed only in remove_creature would tally zero Predation deaths, and the total would undercount every predation kill. Any implementation needs a second increment site at predation.rs:124; note the trap that rerouting predation victims THROUGH remove_creature instead would newly record mutation_outcome_summary and mutation_value_totals_by_operator observations for those victims (simulation.rs:88-104), changing existing stored mutation-outcome readings — a design constraint, not a reason to drop the gap. Finally, the tension the finder flagged is real but not disqualifying: T03.F10's "no new telemetry field" Non-Goal at spec:33-35 is scoped to that closed feature, not a program-level ban, so it does not pre-empt a new feature; surface it to the user as stated.

Narrow it on two points. (1) Do not frame this as an unread gap in T03.F10's closure. That spec's Non-Goals (t03-f10 spec:33-37) reject "No new work counter, telemetry field, inspector annotation, or sensor", name `vm_steps` as the instrument, and name the T11.F17 probe method as the sanctioned one-off diagnosis; the user closed the feature on that basis (23f230af). The proposal's "removal tally, not a cap-hit counter" distinction is thin — the non-goal excludes any telemetry field, not one counter shape. So T03.F10 closed on a proxy by design, and this is a request to reverse a settled scoping decision on a closed feature, which the workflow does not reopen. (2) The live program need is prospective, not retrospective: the open T03 track criteria at docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:16 ("Every body trait changes applied simulation behavior and has an observable ecological cost or tradeoff") and :17 ("exposes its applied outcomes through the goal-profile report"), both unchecked, cover the seven open cost/tradeoff features T03.F01-F07, and docs/roadmap.md:57 requires every new capacity to carry an applied cost. A feature carrying this must argue why a permanent per-cause counter beats the already-sanctioned one-off probe for those seven features — that is the KISS question, and it is unanswered by the current framing. Two placement/shape corrections: this is an observation reading, not a diversity or cognition indicator, so the roadmap.md:55 "wires its indicator into the goal profile" rule does not apply and it belongs beside `births` in `deterministic.per_seed[]`/`cases[]`, not under `goal_indicators`; and the ~12 subtraction sites include two in hot dispatch/graph loops, so the binding budget is the gate wall-clock flag at +25%, not the goal-run minutes budget. Drop the stale-cause worry: every compute exhaustion path returns `NodeResult::exhausted()` and mesh.rs:345 forces a NoOp, so no creature recovers after crossing zero.

Four narrowings. (a) FACTUAL ERROR: `Simulation::remove_creature` is NOT "the single funnel every death passes through." Predation kills bypass it entirely — crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:123-125 removes the victim from the world, the slotmap, and action_logs inline (`sim.world.remove_creature(victim_pos); sim.creatures.remove(victim_id); sim.action_logs.remove(victim_id);`) and never calls Simulation::remove_creature. The only callers of Simulation::remove_creature are simulation.rs:80 (Phase 0 bulk) and tick/helpers.rs:6 (Phase 2). Any implementation needs two increment sites, and a side effect worth noting is that predation deaths already skip the mutation-outcome observation at simulation.rs:88-104. (b) The proposal's fifth variant is redundant: `SimStats::predation_kills_total` at predation.rs:128 already counts exactly the Predation cause. The genuinely new signal is four causes — Lifecycle, BrainCompute, ActionCost, ReproductionTransfer — not five. (c) The retrospective framing is overstated: T03.F10 and T03.F08 are both closed ([x] at docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:37 and :41) on instruments their specs predeclared and the closure contract accepted. A new counter cannot re-open either closure; the value is prospective, for the eight open T03 energy-cost features. (d) The tension with T03.F10's Non-Goal (spec:32-35, "No new work counter, telemetry field, inspector annotation, or sensor. A cap-hit counter was considered and is not added") is real and must go to the user. The finder's distinction is sound — that non-goal rejected a dispatch-outcome tally and bound T03.F10's own scope — but the user, not the implementer, should settle whether a removal tally is inside the spirit of it. Layer note: this is a genuine layer-(a) runtime absence, so it is the expensive class (SimStats field plus bench.rs plumbing plus threading a cause through roughly thirteen subtraction sites), not a cheap store-what-already-exists fix.

Two claims in the finding are wrong and one defense is the wrong argument; the gap itself stands. (1) "SimStats has no death field of any kind" is overstated, and the `runtime-absent` layer label is wrong for one of the five proposed variants. `predation_kills_total` (stats.rs:303) and `last_tick_predation_kills` (stats.rs:316) already are a per-cause death counter for predation, incremented at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:128-129 on the victim's actual energy <= 0.0, and already surfaced to the live layer (crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:282, transport/protocol.rs:56). It is absent only from the stored closure report — `grep predation_kills_total crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs` returns nothing and neither t13-f01 JSON contains it. So `Predation` is a cheap layer-(b) plumbing fix, not a runtime addition; only `Lifecycle`, `BrainCompute`, `ActionCost`, and `ReproductionTransfer` are genuinely runtime-absent. (2) "`Simulation::remove_creature` is the single funnel every death passes through" is false, and this is a defect in the proposal's instrumentation site, not a nuance. Predation kills remove the victim inline at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:122-124 (`sim.world.remove_creature(victim_pos); sim.creatures.remove(victim_id); sim.action_logs.remove(victim_id);`) and never call `Simulation::remove_creature`. `grep -rn 'remove_creature' crates/v3-core/src/` confirms only three callers: paint eviction (simulation.rs:80), the Phase 0 bulk loop (tick.rs:189), and Phase 2 (tick.rs:1000). A `deaths_total` increment placed only in `remove_creature` would therefore undercount by exactly the predation deaths, and predation is not gated by any enable flag (PredationConfig at config/simulation.rs:819-833 has only `steal_cost_rate` and `kill_complexity_bonus_multiplier`), so those deaths occur under production defaults. The proposal needs a second increment site, or the predation path must be routed through the funnel. (3) The finder's defense of the T03.F10 non-goal tension is the wrong argument. "It is NOT the cap-hit counter T03.F10 rejected" does not help: the non-goal at :33-35 reads "No new work counter, telemetry field, inspector annotation, or sensor" — a general prohibition, not a cap-hit-specific one. The correct framing is that the non-goal scoped T03.F10's own delivery and does not bind later features; a death counter added by a new feature does not violate it retroactively. Flag it to the user on that basis.

Gap stands and is unowned, but two of the finder's load-bearing statements are wrong and must be fixed before this is proposed. (1) "`Simulation::remove_creature` is the single funnel every death passes through" is FALSE. Predation kills bypass it entirely: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:124-126 removes the victim directly (`sim.world.remove_creature(victim_pos); sim.creatures.remove(victim_id); sim.action_logs.remove(victim_id)`) without calling `Simulation::remove_creature`, and then increments `sim.stats.predation_kills_total` at :128. `grep -rn 'creatures\.remove('` over v3-core and v3-server returns exactly two sites: simulation.rs:87 (inside the funnel) and predation.rs:125 (the bypass). Consequences for the proposal: the `Predation` variant would never fire at the proposed increment site; predation is in fact the one cause ALREADY tallied at layer (a), and its gap is a different, cheaper one — `predation_kills_total` is absent from the stored goal report (0 hits for "predation" in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-*-goal.json). So the proposal covers four new causes, not five, and the funnel claim should read "every non-predation death passes through `Simulation::remove_creature`." Relatedly, that funnel is not death-exclusive: simulation.rs:78-80 (`apply_paint`) routes editor barrier-evictions through it, so a naive `deaths_total += 1` there would count paint evictions as deaths in v3-server; the counter must be driven by the `death_cause` field, which the proposal's own design already implies. The bypass also silently skips the mutation-outcome recording in remove_creature for every predation victim — worth flagging separately. (2) "only the first link (vm_steps fell) and a confounded population reading were measured" understates T03.F10's closure. Its Measured table at docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f10-activity-ramped-compute-cost.md:385 carries a predeclared, met, DIRECTIONAL persistence reading: seed 33 — the seed whose 12.05% cap-running tail motivated the feature — fell from 11,379 to 1,306 final (minimum 536), while seeds 11 and 22 rose, exactly as predicted. The spec does concede at :400-401 that "the populations behind the three samples are different populations", so this is still not death-cause attribution — a population drop confounds fewer births with more deaths, and cannot say the loopers specifically starved. Corrected claim: T03.F10's causal chain (ramp charge -> energy exhaustion -> death removes the looper) was closed on a vm_steps reading plus a predeclared population-collapse direction, with the terminal link — which energy sink actually took each creature to <= 0.0 — unmeasurable at every layer, and the same blindness applies to T03.F08's carrying cost. Finally, the tension the finder flags with T03.F10's Non-Goal is stronger than framed: spec :32-33 bans "No new work counter, telemetry field, inspector annotation, or sensor" as a blanket clause, not only the cap-hit counter, so this is a user decision to reopen rather than a distinction the spec leaves open.
