title: The quantity T03.F08 charges energy on is absent from every closure report
missing: Mean/median `genome_size()` and total mesh-node count over the living population at closure. The report stores `reachable_structure_size_distribution` only, so total carried structure — and therefore the junk fraction (total − reachable), which is the whole subject of the depth-dilution finding — cannot be read at any closure. `cached_genome_size` exists on every live creature and is the exact multiplicand of the per-tick charge.
evidence: `grep -o '"genome_size"' docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json | wc -l` = 0; same for `mean_genome_size`. crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:172-174 defines `cached_genome_size`; crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:162-166 charges `genome_carry_cost_per_unit * cached_genome_size` against it every tick. The helper already exists one crate away: crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:165-186 `structure_means` returns `(mean_genome_size, mean_mesh_nodes, mean_generation)` over `sim.creatures.values()`, but it is only wired to `TickSampleEvent` (lib.rs:188-198) for the `v3-cli run` path — `grep -n 'structure_means\|mean_genome_size' crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs` returns nothing. bench.rs already has the seam: `PersistenceTracker::record` (bench.rs:1753-1782) takes a lazily-evaluated `mean_energy: impl FnOnce() -> f64` closure at each of the 20 sample points, so a second closure costs the same. T03.F08 measured the quantity once, in a one-off paired sweep stored under docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/ (spec docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f08-genome-size-maintenance-cost.md:461-463: cost arm 386.535913 units vs control 1,093.835901, -64.66%), and its spec calls the TickSampleEvent fields "the only telemetry added" (line 106) — a scope statement about that feature, not a decision that closures should not store it.
why: Whether the carrying cost is still shedding structure cannot be read at any closure after T03.F08's own. The one measurement was a bespoke 12,000-tick paired sweep nobody will rerun; the standing goal profile reads only reachable size, which the cost does not target. A later feature that inflates junk (T11.F04's neutral scaffold, T11.F18's node growth, T13's recruitment repairs) would show up as a rise in reachable size or not at all, and the depth note's central quantity — 124 total mesh nodes of which 17 reachable and 4 executed — has no closure-layer counterpart.
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:38 (T03.F08 goal line): "Every unit of brain structure a creature carries costs energy each tick whether or not it ever runs, so unused structure is shed by selection and genome size has to pay for itself"
proposal: Call the existing `structure_means` (or an inlined two-line equivalent) inside `PersistenceTracker::record` at the same 20 sample points that already compute `mean_energy`, and emit `mean_genome_size` and `mean_mesh_nodes` per sample in `population_persistence.per_seed[].samples[]`. Pure counts over live creatures, no score, no new run, no measurable cost — the closure already walks the population for `mean_energy` at those ticks.
corrections: Narrower claim: mean/median `genome_size()` over the living population is absent from every stored closure report at any granularity — that part stands. But "total carried structure — and therefore the junk fraction (total − reachable) — cannot be read at any closure" is overstated. `deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].mutational_neighborhood.evolved.per_seed[].sampled_genomes[]` are drawn directly from the living population by rank over sorted `sim.creatures.keys()` (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:2174-2213), and each sample stores both `mesh_execution.total_node_count` and `mesh_execution.reachable_node_count` — 12 living genomes per case (SAMPLE_SIZE = 12, crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/sample.rs:8), 36 per closure across the three baseline worlds. In the T13.F01 goal report, case 0 (final population 8,818) reads e.g. rank 6613 total 7 / reachable 3, rank 734 total 15 / reachable 14. So the mesh-node junk fraction IS readable at closure for a rank-stratified 12-genome sample; what is missing is (a) `genome_size` — the actual multiplicand of the 1e-4 per-tick charge — in any form anywhere, and (b) any population-wide mean/median of TOTAL (as opposed to reachable) structure. The gate report carries only the founder's `total_node_count` = 2, no evolved-population totals. Minor: the proposed seam is `PersistenceTracker::observe`, not `record` (bench.rs:1756).

The claim stands; four narrowings. (a) The seam is misnamed: there is no PersistenceTracker::record. The method is `fn observe` at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1757, and its lazily-evaluated `mean_energy: impl FnOnce() -> f64` argument is real, so the seam exists as described under the correct name. (b) The finder missed the cheaper and better seam, which should be the primary proposal: crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1892-1896 ALREADY walks sim.creatures.values() at the final tick mapping to functional_complexity(&c.genome). Adding c.cached_genome_size and c.genome.nodes.len() to that same pass costs zero extra iteration and yields a total_structure_size_distribution directly comparable to reachable_structure_size_distribution — same population, same tick, same percentile shape. The 20-sample trajectory via `observe` is a separate, optional reading (it shows whether shedding is ongoing across the run, not where it landed) and should not be conflated with the minimum fix. (c) The junk-fraction subtraction is clean for genome_size units but NOT for mesh nodes. functional_complexity and genome_size() share units — crates/v3-core/src/creature/genome/tests/analysis_tests.rs:751 pins functional_complexity_equals_genome_size_fully_connected — so cached_genome_size minus functional_complexity is junk in units. But total mesh-node count has no same-population reachable counterpart in the stored report: reachable_node_count appears only inside mutational_neighborhood over sampled genomes, not over the living population, so the node-count version of "junk fraction" is still not directly readable even after the fix. The depth note's headline shape (124 total nodes, 17 reachable, 4 executed) is therefore only partly recoverable. (d) The strongest counter-argument should be met head-on rather than left implicit: the T03.F08 spec calls the TickSampleEvent fields "the only telemetry added" (docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f08-genome-size-maintenance-cost.md:106) and the T03 track note records that verification needed a bespoke long run for total node count at depth "since the drift walk has no energy and cannot show a carrying cost." That note documents the gap rather than closing it, and neither text says future closures should not store the quantity — but a proposal should cite it explicitly so the scoping question looks examined. Scope must stay at two counts over the existing final-tick pass: no mean_generation field, no derived junk ratio stored in the JSON (readers subtract), and no new or extended run.

Narrow the claim to the charged unit only. TRUE: `genome_size()` / `cached_genome_size` — the exact multiplicand of T03.F08's per-tick charge — is stored in no closure report at all, so whether the carrying cost is still shedding structure cannot be read at any closure after T03.F08's own bespoke sweep. FALSE as written: "total mesh-node count over the living population... cannot be read at any closure" and "the junk fraction (total − reachable)... cannot be read at any closure" and the depth note's 124-total/17-reachable/4-executed "has no closure-layer counterpart." The report already stores, for each of 12 living genomes per seed per case (id-sorted evenly spaced ranks, crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/sample.rs:8-23; 39 values in t13-f01-...-goal.json), `mutational_neighborhood.evolved.per_seed[].sampled_genomes[].mesh_execution.{total_node_count, reachable_node_count, executed_node_count}` (mesh-execution-v1, from T11.F14) — e.g. seed 11 totals [6,15,2,5,2,3,8,4,3,7,6,4] against reachable [6,14,2,4,2,3,7,4,3,3,5,3], so mesh-level junk is computable per sampled genome today. What is genuinely missing at the mesh layer is only a population-level aggregate and any trajectory: the reading is end-of-run and n=12 of ~8,800. Scope the proposal accordingly: the non-redundant addition is `mean_genome_size` at the existing persistence sample points (`PersistenceTracker::observe`, not `record`); `mean_mesh_nodes` is largely duplicative of the existing sample and buys only the aggregate plus the 20-point trajectory.

Narrower, corrected claim: the quantity T03.F08 charges on — `genome_size()` (junk-inclusive component count: nodes + input_refs + targets + VM instructions + constants + graph internals, genome/mod.rs:265) — has no closure-layer counterpart at all, and no SimStats counterpart either; the only recording of it in the repo is the one-off TickSampleEvent sweep at docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/*.ndjson, and even T03.F08's own closure report stores it zero times.

Two overstatements in the finder's framing:

(a) "total mesh-node count ... cannot be read at any closure" is too strong. `mutational_neighborhood.evolved.per_seed[].sampled_genomes[].mesh_execution` DOES store `total_node_count` alongside `reachable_node_count` and `executed_node_count` for real live creatures (e.g. Orchards seed 0: rank 0 = 6/6/3, rank 734 = 15/14/4), so a node-level junk fraction IS readable. The real limit is sample size, not absence: `battery.evolved_sample_size = 12` rank-strided genomes against `final_population_size = 8818`. So "total mesh-node count over the living population" should read "as a population statistic rather than a 12-genome rank-strided sample".

(b) "the report stores reachable_structure_size_distribution only" should read "reachable_structure_size_distribution is the only FULL-population structural reading". It is `functional_complexity` over every live creature (bench.rs:1893 maps sim.creatures.values()), in the same component-counting units as genome_size (mean 98.80, median 82, max 478; founder genome_size = 111 per tick/tests/phase0.rs:194) — so the missing half of "total − reachable" is specifically the total side in those units, which is exactly the unreported multiplicand.

Minor citation fixes: the seam method is `PersistenceTracker::observe`, not `record` (bench.rs:1757-1764); `cached_genome_size` is declared at state.rs:176, not 172-174; the charge site is tick.rs:161-166.

Three narrowings. (1) The "why it matters" claim that storing this would let a closure read "whether the carrying cost is still shedding structure" is wrong at goal-profile depth, and T03.F08's own spec disproves it: at generation ~48 the paired run measured 183.191 units in the cost arm versus 172.294 in the control (docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f08-genome-size-maintenance-cost.md, Rate row ~line 100) — the cost arm is higher. Shedding only appears at generation 177+ (386.535913 vs 1,093.835901 at tick 12,000, spec lines 461-463). The defensible value is narrower and still worth it: a plain closure-layer reading of the production charge's multiplicand, and a detector for junk inflation from T11.F04's neutral scaffold, T11.F18's node growth, or T13's recruitment repairs — which today would show up only as a change in reachable score, or not at all. (2) "Junk fraction (total − reachable)" is loose. `genome_size()` (crates/v3-core/src/creature/genome/mod.rs:265-285) counts every node, input_ref, target, instruction and constant; `functional_complexity` counts only reachable nodes' live-sliced instructions, consumed refs and live constants. Strike the rest of the finder's case. title: Age at death is read at the death site but discarded for ~90% of creatures
missing: A population-level lifespan reading. `creature.age` is incremented every tick and is already read as `survival_ticks` at the death funnel — but only for creatures carrying at least one applied birth-mutation operator, and only into mutation-attribution buckets. Clone births (about 90% of all births per the 2026-09-04 audit) contribute nothing, and no mean/median age at death exists for the population.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:161 `creature.age += 1` every tick for every creature. crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:150 `survival_ticks: creature.age` — the dead creature's age is literally in hand at the funnel. crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:93 gates the recording on `if !creature.birth_mutation_operators.is_empty()`, so a clone's age is computed and dropped. `grep -o '"age"' docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json | wc -l` = 0; `grep -niE 'lifespan|age_ticks' crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs` returns nothing (only `survival_ticks` at stats.rs:19/126, which is the mutation-carrier field above).
why: Age structure is the standard reading that separates a population held down by high adult mortality from one held down by low fecundity, and it is the direct signal of an energy cost biting: T03.F08's carrying charge and T03.F10's step ramp both act, if they act, by shortening lives. Today `mean_energy` and population count are the only lifecycle readings, and both are stocks. The peak-then-trough-then-recovery shape in every persistence run (peak ~35k at tick 150, trough ~4-5k by tick 700-1000) is uninterpretable without knowing whether the trough is a mortality pulse or a fecundity collapse.
criterion: NONE
proposal: In `Simulation::remove_creature`, before the existing mutation-carrier gate, add `self.stats.deaths_total += 1; self.stats.death_age_ticks_sum += creature.age;` (two u64 fields on SimStats). Store `deaths_total` and mean age at death per seed in the goal report. Both are counts of applied behavior — a creature was removed, it had lived N ticks. If a distribution is wanted later, a fixed small histogram of age buckets at the same site is still O(1); do not add one now.
refutations: REFUTED on Lens 3 (program need), on four independent grounds. (1) NO CRITERION. The finder cited none, and none exists: `grep -rniE 'mortality|lifespan|age at death|age structure|death rate|deaths' docs/roadmap.md docs/roadmaps/*.md` hits only t01-experimental-science-and-causal-evaluation.md:52/57/58 — T01.F13's neutral-shadow-model description ("same births and deaths"), which is explicitly "not in the execution order" and an optional supplement to a deferred phase, not a criterion. The Final Success Criteria at docs/roadmap.md:34-40 are: lineage-diversity indicators, cognition (memory-sensitivity) indicators, stored benchmark + no severe compute regression, mutational-neighborhood floors, cross-process determinism, one progress.md row per feature, named natural analog. None reads age at death. (2) THE HEADLINE MOTIVATION IS FACTUALLY FALSE, AND THE LAYER LABEL IS WRONG. The finder says the peak-trough-recovery shape "is uninterpretable without knowing whether the trough is a mortality pulse or a fecundity collapse." Layer (b) already answers that with zero code change: `population_persistence.per_seed[].samples[]` stores both `population` and `births_total` at 20 checkpoints, and `crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1875-1878` feeds `sim.stats.reproduction_actions_spawned_total` (spawned, not attempted) into that field, so removals = Δbirths_total − Δpopulation is EXACT population bookkeeping over applied behavior. Computed from docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json, seed 11: tick 100→200 is 36,439 births against 133,922 removals — an unambiguous mortality pulse, not a fecundity collapse; the trough interval 900→1000 is 4,158 births against 4,049 removals (balanced). So death COUNTS per interval are present in layer (b) today; only the age-at-death distribution is absent across (a)/(b)/(c), and the finder's `layer: runtime-absent` mislabels a reading that is already derivable. NOTE FOR THE PARENT: this proposal does NOT violate a hard constraint — two u64 increments are applied behavior, O(1), consume no production RNG, change no execution, and cost nothing against a minutes-scale closure budget. Second, `Simulation::remove_creature` is the single sink for starvation death (tick.rs:183-189 and tick/helpers.rs:9-19), predation kills (already counted separately as predation_kills_total), and paint eviction (simulation.rs:80-82), so a naive `deaths_total` there would conflate three different exits and would need splitting by cause to mean what the finder wants it to mean.

Predation kills bypass `Simulation::remove_creature` entirely: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:124-126 does `sim.world.remove_creature(victim_pos); sim.creatures.remove(victim_id); sim.action_logs.remove(victim_id);` inline. 2) PLACEMENT CAVEAT: `Simulation::remove_creature` also fires on non-deaths — simulation.rs:80 calls it for creatures evicted by `apply_paint_stroke`. 3) LAYER LABEL IS SPLIT, NOT UNIFORMLY "runtime-absent". Narrowed claim: the missing reading is AGE AT DEATH (mean/distribution of lifespan among creatures that died) — not a death count, and not the mortality-vs-fecundity question. (1) The proposal's deaths_total half is already derivable, time-resolved, from the stored report with no code change: population_persistence.per_seed[].samples[] carries both `population` and cumulative `births_total` at 20 checkpoints, so deaths per interval = pop[i-1] + (births[i]-births[i-1]) - pop[i]. It overcounts: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:70-82 calls the same remove_creature from apply_paint for creatures evicted under a painted barrier, which is not a death. Any lifespan counter must be placed at the two energy<=0 sites (tick.rs:184-189, tick/helpers.rs:9-15) plus the predation kill, not at remove_creature. (3) The "~90% of creatures" discard figure is stale: mutation.mutation_probability is 0.44 today (crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:785), so at least ~56% of births are clones, not 90.2%; the 90.2% is the 2026-09-04 audit at the pre-T11.F04 10% trigger (roadmap.md:64). Also note the funnel is not fully dark for clones — classify_mutation_outcome (simulation.rs:91, stats.rs:400-451) runs unconditionally and pushes every removed creature's viability_score into mutation_outcome_baseline_global, though neither that baseline nor survival_ticks_sum appears anywhere in the stored goal report.

Residual true-but-unneeded fact: SimStats genuinely has no death counter and no age-at-death distribution is derivable from stored data — but no criterion at docs/roadmap.md:34-40 requires one, and the mortality-versus-fecundity question the finder raised is already answerable exactly from the stored report's samples[].{births_total, population}.

title: An entire lifetime-outcome block exists in SimStats and reaches no consumer
missing: `SimStats::mutation_outcome_summary` and `mutation_value_totals_by_operator` — which already accumulate, at death, `carriers_observed_total`, `survival_ticks_sum`, `offspring_spawned_sum`, `survived_short_horizon_total`, `survived_long_horizon_total` and `reproduced_once_total` per mutation operator — are read by nothing. Not stored at closure, not served by v3-server.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:16-38 (MutationValueTotals fields) and :273-277 (the two aggregates); populated in crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:93-105 at every death. `grep -c 'survival_ticks_sum' crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs` = 0; same for `carriers_observed_total`, `mutation_outcome_summary`, `offspring_spawned_sum`. All four also return 0 occurrences in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json. So the simulation pays to compute these on every single removal and no layer reads them.
why: These are cohort vital rates — how long carriers of each mutation operator lived, how many reproduced at least once, how many cleared the short and long survival horizons — measured on the real population under selection, not on a synthetic battery. Every existing mutation reading in the closure report (`mutational_neighborhood`, `drift_depth`) is a battery or a drift walk: neither has an energy budget or a world. Nothing in the stored report says what mutation carriers actually did in the ecology, so 'the neighborhood changed' can never be connected to 'and it mattered'.
criterion: NONE
proposal: Store the applied-behavior subset per seed under a new `goal_indicators.mutation_carrier_outcomes`: `carriers_observed_total`, `survival_ticks_sum`, `offspring_spawned_sum`, `survived_short_horizon_total`, `survived_long_horizon_total`, `reproduced_once_total`, optionally per operator. Deliberately EXCLUDE `viability_score_sum`, `viability_score_delta_sum` and the helpful/neutral/detrimental class tallies: `viability_score` is a weighted composite built in crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:139-146 and storing it would violate the no-composite-score constraint. The excluded half is exactly the derived half; the kept half is counts of what happened.
refutations:
REFUTED on Lens 3, plus an independent factual error.

(1) NO CRITERION EXISTS. The finder cited none, and none of the seven Final Success Criteria (docs/roadmap.md:34-40) requires cohort vital rates: :34 is ecological diversity (surviving lineage count, lineage entropy), :35 is cognition (memory, learning, prediction), :37 is the mutational-neighborhood indicator. Per-operator survival/reproduction sums are none of these. This is the listed refutation ground "the criterion does not exist."

(2) THE QUESTION IS ALREADY OWNED, WITH A PRESCRIBED AND DELIBERATELY SHARED METHOD. The finder's stated motivation -- that nothing connects "the neighborhood changed" to "and it mattered" -- is verbatim the goal line of a planned feature: docs/roadmaps/t08-heredity-and-recombination.md:23-24, "T08.F02 - Lineage Mutation-Effect Attribution - Goal: Which mutations mattered. Along a surviving lineage, which heritable changes altered behavior and which were silent." The track note at :39 fixes the method: T08.F02 "attributes behavioral change along surviving lineages using the T11.F01 battery and its silent, changed, and dead classes, so that lineage readings and neighborhood readings share one definition of 'changed'." Storing operator-keyed cohort sums into the closure series now would establish a second, incompatible definition of "mattered" in the goal profile ahead of the feature that owns it and that was explicitly scoped to avoid exactly that divergence.

(3) A CORE FACTUAL CLAIM IS FALSE. "Read by nothing... not served by v3-server" is wrong. crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:379-393 maps carriers_observed_total, survival_ticks_sum and reproduced_once_total field-by-field; state.rs:511-521 populates the health payload from SimStats.mutation_value_totals_by_operator and .mutation_outcome_summary; transport/protocol.rs:78-80 and :264-265 put both on the wire. The finder asserted the server absence without grepping v3-server. frontend/src returns 0 hits, so the accurate statement is "served but not rendered," not "read by nothing."

(4) THE PROPOSED SUBSET CANNOT ANSWER ITS OWN QUESTION. simulation.rs:96 gates the summary on `!creature.birth_mutation_operators.is_empty()`, so only carriers are ever accumulated -- there is no clone/non-carrier denominator anywhere, and the audit records 90.2% of births as clones, so "it mattered" has no control arm. simulation.rs:104-109 records the identical observation into every one of a creature's birth operators, so per-operator carriers multi-count and do not partition the summary; cross-operator comparison is confounded by operator co-occurrence. And every recording path is a removal -- tick.rs:189 and tick.rs:1000 (energy <= 0.0 via tick/helpers.rs:5-19) and simulation.rs:80, which is inside `apply_paint` eviction, not an end-of-run drain -- so there is no flush for survivors and the roughly 10k creatures alive at the end of a goal run are never counted. Refuted on three independent Lens-3 grounds, plus a load-bearing factual error.

(1) NO CRITERION, AND NONE FITS. The finder cites none. The seven Final Success Criteria at docs/roadmap.md:34-40 are: lineage count + entropy (diversity), memory sensitivity (cognition), stored benchmark/no severe regression, the mutational-neighborhood indicator floors, determinism, progress.md rows, and natural analog. Mutation-carrier vital rates are none of these. The roadmap.md:55 rule the proposal leans on ("Any feature that introduces a diversity or cognition measure wires its indicator into the goal profile") obligates NEW measures to be wired; it does not obligate exporting every existing SimStats counter, and carrier lifespan/fecundity is neither a diversity nor a cognition measure.

(2) THE GAP IS ALREADY OWNED BY A PLANNED FEATURE. docs/roadmaps/t08-heredity-and-recombination.md:23-24 — "T08.F02 - Lineage Mutation-Effect Attribution - Depends on: T11.F01 - Goal: Which mutations mattered. Along a surviving lineage, which heritable changes altered behavior and which were silent." Track note :39 fixes its method (the T11.F01 battery's silent/changed/dead classes) so lineage and neighborhood readings share one definition of "changed". (3) THE KEPT HALF IS UNINTERPRETABLE ONCE THE EXCLUDED HALF IS REMOVED. crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:92-97 records the summary only `if !creature.birth_mutation_operators.is_empty()` — there is NO non-carrier vital-rate cohort anywhere in SimStats. So the proposal keeps carrier numerators and deletes the only denominator: a stored `survival_ticks_sum / carriers_observed_total` is a mean carrier lifespan against nothing, and cannot support the "and it mattered" inference it is proposed for. Separately, simulation.rs:99-105 credits a creature carrying N birth operators into all N per-operator buckets, so the optional per-operator breakdown is confounded by construction and cannot separate operator effects.

The "simulation pays to compute these and nothing reads them" motivation therefore collapses — the compute is already paid for a live consumer.

(Cost was NOT a refutation ground: serializing existing end-of-run counters is near-free and adds no runs, consumes no production RNG, and changes no execution. The proposal fails on need and interpretability, not budget.)

title: The only death-cause counter that exists reaches v3-server but not the closure report
missing: `SimStats::predation_kills_total` in the stored gate and goal reports. It is a live, always-reachable death-cause counter (Steal has no enable flag) and bench.rs never touches it.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:303 declares it; crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:128 `sim.stats.predation_kills_total += 1;` increments it; crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:282 and :578 plus crates/v3-server/src/transport/protocol.rs:56,226 carry it to the frontend. `grep -n 'predation' crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs` returns NO matches, and `grep -o 'predation' docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json | wc -l` = 0. why: It is the one death cause the runtime already counts, and the one death that transfers energy to another creature rather than to nothing. Storing it therefore yields predation-kill presence and rate per seed, not a share of population turnover and not "the cheapest half of death-cause attribution" — attribution needs a total-death counter that does not exist yet. Also note that a stored value of 0 across all baseline seeds is a valid and useful reading (predation is absent from the evolved behavior), not a failed measurement, so the proposal should predeclare that outcome rather than treat nonzero as the success case. Everything else in the claim — the layer diagnosis, the file:line evidence, the no-enable-flag finding, and the T05.F03/T05.F01 sequencing caveat — holds as written.

The layer-gap half of the claim is factually correct and survives: `predation_kills_total` is declared at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:303, incremented at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:128, carried to the frontend at crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:282 and :578 and crates/v3-server/src/transport/protocol.rs:56,226, and is absent from the stored layer — `grep -c 'predation' crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs` = 0 (also 0 for 'steal|kill'), and 'predation' appears 0 times in both docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability.json and -goal.json. There is no enable gate: PredationConfig (crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:816-833) carries only steal_cost_rate 0.05 and kill_complexity_bonus_multiplier 0.0, and StealEnergy is reachable by mutation (crates/v3-core/src/mutation/graph/operators.rs:256) and decodable as opcode 4 (crates/v3-core/src/runtime/action_decode.rs:20). What does not survive is the program-need claim: no Final Success Criterion or T05 track criterion requires a death-cause count, the signal is owned by T05.F03 which is gated behind unstarted T05.F01, and the T05 notes explicitly warn against reading kill counts as coevolution evidence. Correct framing: a real but unowned and uncriterioned observation-layer gap, to be closed by T05.F03 when its dependency chain opens, not a gap the current program needs closed now.

Two narrowings. (1) The landing-spot claim "identical in kind to `actions_applied` which is already stored" understates a real hazard: the six `PerSeed` work counters are enrolled in `COUNTER_NAMES` (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:30-37) and drive the FLAG 10% / SEVERE 50% regression comparison (bench.rs:40-42, 2865, 2997) plus per-creature-tick normalization (bench.rs:2367-2370). `predation_kills_total` must be added as a plain `PerSeed` field and explicitly NOT added to `COUNTER_NAMES` — a 0-to-3 kills delta against a reference is an unbounded percentage and would emit spurious severe flags at every closure; per-creature-tick normalization is also meaningless for a kill count. (2) "Always-reachable, live action in every goal run" means decodable and un-gated, not emitted: no founder-genome emission check exists, so the stored value may be a confirmed zero. That is still the information wanted (docs/roadmaps/t05-biotic-interactions-and-coevolution.md, Notes: report applied interactions "including absence"), but the finder's "why it matters" reads as if creature-on-creature turnover is guaranteed to have signal — it is not. Minor precision point: the counter is a lower bound on predation-caused death, since a steal leaving the victim just above zero followed by the energy filter at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:184-189 is counted as nothing. Sequencing note is accurate: T05.F03 depends on T05.F01 (and T01.F12), and T05.F01 is unchecked/unstarted in docs/roadmaps/t05-biotic-interactions-and-coevolution.md:24.

The narrow factual gap is real and should not be lost: `predation_kills_total` (declared crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:303, incremented crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:128, exported crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:282/:578) exists in layers (a) and (c) but is absent from crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs and therefore from the stored gate and goal reports, and adding it beside the existing work counters at bench.rs:1940-1944 would be roughly a one-line change that violates no hard constraint. What does not hold is the justification: no Final Success Criterion (docs/roadmap.md:34-40) or T05 track criterion requires it; T05.F03 owns interaction telemetry in the goal profile once T05.F01 exists, and T05 is absent from the priority list at docs/roadmap.md:45; StealEnergy is mutation-reachable only (founder.rs:251/256/276 emit action types 1/2/3), so it is not a "live action in every goal run" and there is no recorded evidence of a nonzero kill at closure horizons; and without any total-death counter a kill count cannot attribute population turnover. If the signal is wanted, it belongs to T05.F01/T05.F03 when that track starts, not as a standalone counter added ahead of its owning feature.

title: SURFACE CORRECTION: population generation depth IS stored, but only as median+max at the final tick
missing: Generation depth over time and its spread. What IS stored is a per-seed `{median, max}` computed at the end of the run; there is no min, no quartiles, and no trajectory, so cohort turnover rate and whether generation depth is still advancing at the end of a run cannot be read.
evidence: CORRECTION TO THE PROVIDED SURFACE, which states generation_distribution covers "only the neighborhood's SAMPLED genomes, not the population". That is wrong. crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:2230-2233 builds it as `generation_distribution(sim.creatures.values().map(|creature| creature.generation).collect())` — the WHOLE final living population. The bench test at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:4675 is literally named `evolved_depth_uses_whole_population_and_actual_sample_generation`. So the roadmap's "every closure reading is taken at 22 generations" IS readable from the stored report, and this is a weaker gap than the surface implied. The genuine absence: crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1180-1188 `generation_distribution` returns only `{median, max}`, and it is computed once, at the end of the evolved-neighborhood pass; the 20 persistence samples (bench.rs:1753-1782) carry population, births_total and mean_energy but no generation. `grep -o '"mean_generation"' docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json | wc -l` = 0, even though crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:184 already computes it for the `v3-cli run` path.
why: Whether generation depth is still climbing or has stalled at the horizon — and whether ticks-per-generation shifts within a run, which is the demographic signature of a population moving from boom to steady state — cannot be read. A terminal median alone cannot distinguish a population that reached generation 22 by tick 400 and then stopped turning over from one that was still advancing at tick 2,000, and those imply opposite things about whether 2,000 ticks is an adequate closure horizon. This is the exact question the 2026-09-07 depth research raised and only answered with an ad-hoc probe: docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:7 records the method as "a 400-genome random sample of the live population pulled from `GET /v3/simulation/creature/:id`", and line 159 states "The closure profile reads at generation 22. Every stored goal reading in `docs/progress.md` is at that depth ... nothing makes a deeper reading."
criterion: docs/roadmap.md:45 (roadmap note recording the user-driven 2026-09-07 reprioritization): "the user's 281,405-tick run (median generation 1,990) showed that every closure reading is taken at 22 generations while the substrate's mutational exposure decays to 1% of births by generation 250"
proposal: Add `mean_generation` (the third value `structure_means` already returns, crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:184) to each of the 20 persistence samples, alongside the `mean_genome_size` / `mean_mesh_nodes` of the living-structure gap — one closure over the population at ticks the report already samples. Do not add a new run, a new profile, or a deeper horizon; a 20-point generation trajectory answers the turnover question at zero extra cost. Note this proposal and the living-structure one are the same one-line change and should be specced together.
refutations:
Refuted on need, not on feasibility or facts.

1) The cited criterion does not require a new instrument. docs/roadmap.md:45 is verbatim as quoted (verified by exact-string grep), but it is a "Notes for AI Agents" rationale line recording WHY T11.F16 and T11.F17 were added. Both are closed: docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-evolvability.md:69 `- [x] T11.F16 — Drift-Depth Indicator` and :71 `- [x] T11.F17 — Executed-Biased Mutation Targeting`. Closed-feature rationale is not a standing requirement.

2) The program already answered that question with a different, deliberate instrument. The stored goal report's `drift_depth` (version `drift-depth-v3`) walks `checkpoints: [0, 22, 250, 1000, 2000]` in generation units and is floor-bearing under the 2026-09-09 re-base note (docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-evolvability.md:88). That IS a stored generation-depth trajectory, and it reads exactly the property the 2026-09-07 depth note raised.

3) The load-bearing "why it matters" claim is false against the stored report. The finder's discriminating example — "reached generation 22 by tick 400 and then stopped turning over" vs "still advancing at tick 2,000" — is readable today. `PersistenceSample` (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1455-1463) carries `births_total` AND `population` at all 20 checkpoints. On docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json seed 11, births per capita per 100-tick interval is flat at 1.52, 1.52, 1.51, 1.55, 1.73, 1.57, 1.56, 1.56, 1.54, 1.56 from tick 1,000 to 2,000 — sustained cohort turnover at the horizon, directly stored. "Cohort turnover rate cannot be read" is wrong.

4) The premise figure is stale. The finder repeats "every closure reading is taken at 22 generations"; the newest stored `generation_distribution` is `{median: 49, max: 62}` (case 0) with `sampled_genomes` at generations 47-56. The horizon depth the roadmap note worried about has already moved.

5) The proposal is also mis-costed. `structure_means` exists only in crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:165/189 (the `v3-cli run` path); bench.rs never calls it. Adding `mean_generation` requires a new `PersistenceSample` field plus an O(population) closure plumbed through `PersistenceTracker::observe` (bench.rs:1758-1785), whose own doc comment explicitly keeps O(population) passes to the predeclared cadence — small, but not "one line" and not "zero extra cost."

ACKNOWLEDGED AND CONFIRMED — amend the shared surface brief: the finder's correction is right and the brief is wrong. crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:2230-2233 builds `generation_distribution` from `sim.creatures.values().map(|creature| creature.generation)` — the whole final living population, not the neighborhood's sampled genomes — and the test at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:4675 is named `evolved_depth_uses_whole_population_and_actual_sample_generation`. Also confirmed: `generation_distribution` (bench.rs:1179-1188) returns only `{median, max}`, and `grep -o '"mean_generation"'` on the T13.F01 goal JSON returns 0.

No HARD CONSTRAINT is violated (creature.generation is applied simulation state, not a composite score or dashboard; no RNG or execution change), and the runtime cost would be negligible. The refutation is that the demographic question it claims to answer is already answerable from stored `births_total`/`population` and from `drift_depth`, and the criterion backing it is rationale for features that already shipped.
corrections: Three narrowings. (a) The "22 generations" figure the finder cites from docs/roadmap.md:45 is stale, not merely "readable": the newest stored report reads median 49 / max 62 for cases[0] and median 49 / max 59 for cases[1]. What is readable is the terminal depth, currently ~49/60; a spec must not cite 22. (b) "Cohort turnover rate cannot be read" is overstated — `births_total` is cumulative in all 20 persistence samples and `births_per_100_ticks` is already a goal indicator, so a birth-rate trajectory IS readable. The genuine, narrower absence is generation depth over time, which is what separates "births continue but the same shallow lineages keep reproducing" from "depth is still advancing at the horizon". (c) Layer precision: the terminal `{median, max}` is stored in the GOAL report only. `grep -c generation_distribution docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability.json` = 0; the gate report carries only the founder's `generation: 0`. So the gap statement is "stored in the goal report as a terminal median+max only; absent entirely from the gate report."

Narrow on two points. First, the cited text at docs/roadmap.md:45 is a "Notes for AI Agents" bullet recording the 2026-09-07 reprioritization rationale, not a Final Success Criterion or a track acceptance criterion — the gap is motivated by that note, not required by a standing criterion, so it should be specced as basic tracking rather than as satisfying a criterion. Second, the note's "every closure reading is taken at 22 generations" premise is already stale in the stored report: the newest closure records generation_distribution median 49 / max 62 (cases[0]) and median 49 / max 59 (cases[1]), so terminal depth is both readable and no longer 22. What is genuinely absent is only the spread (no min, no quartiles) and the within-run trajectory, which is a narrower gap than the "cannot be read" framing suggests. Ownership note: docs/roadmaps/t04-population-structure-and-diversification.md:23 has T04.F01 (Ancestry Graph and Ecotype Observation, observation-only) as the natural owner of ancestry-over-time; the one-field `mean_generation` addition to the existing 20 persistence samples need not wait for it, but should be recorded so T04.F01 does not re-derive it.

Three narrowings. (a) Turnover rate is largely readable today, so "cohort turnover rate ... cannot be read" overstates it: every persistence sample already carries cumulative `births_total` and `population`, so per-capita birth rate at each of the 20 sampled ticks is Δbirths_total/Δtick/population, and net deaths fall out as Δbirths_total − Δpopulation. What is genuinely absent is the generation-depth trajectory itself (a mean or median generation per sample) and the terminal spread (min/quartiles), not turnover per se. (b) The cited roadmap.md:45 phrase "every closure reading is taken at 22 generations" is a dated 2026-09-07 note written before the T12.F04 goal worlds, not a live figure: the newest stored goal report (t13-f01-...-goal.json) reads median generation 49 / 49 / 56 and max 62 / 59 / 71 across the three cases. This does not weaken the gap — it sharpens it, since the depth moved by more than 2x with only a terminal point on record to notice it — but the finder cited the 22 as current. (c) "Zero extra cost" is really near-zero: `structure_means`-style generation means are an O(population) pass at each of 20 already-sampled ticks, the same order as the `mean_energy` closure evaluated there today (bench.rs:1758-1785), and at populations of 8k-22k that is a real, small addition. Also note that mean_generation per sample fixes the trajectory half of the stated gap but not the spread half; adding min/quartiles would mean widening `GenerationDistribution` (bench.rs:1170-1173), a separate one-line change. Field additions must follow the T01.F11 serde-default precedent so stored reports still load.

The gap is real and unowned, but the finder overstates the absence on two points and the proposal only solves half of what it claims.

1. "cohort turnover rate ... cannot be read" is FALSE. The 20 persistence samples already store `births_total` alongside `population` at every 100 ticks. In the newest closure report (seed 1, case 0) births run 359,058 to 372,811 over ticks 1900-2000 against a standing population of 8,818 — 13,753 births in the final 100 ticks. A mean-field per-capita turnover rate and, specifically, whether the population is still turning over at the horizon, are both derivable from stored fields today. The finder's own motivating contrast ("reached generation 22 by tick 400 and then stopped turning over") is already distinguishable: a stalled population would show `births_total` going flat, and it does not.

2. "no min, no quartiles" is true only at the population level. The same report already stores each sampled genome's own `generation` (`crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:2209`, `generation: Some(creature.generation)`); case 0 seed 1's 12 sampled genomes read 43,43,44,50,51,51,51,52,52,54,55,56. A sample-level spread exists.

3. A generation-indexed trajectory also already exists in the report — `drift_depth.checkpoints` = [0, 22, 250, 1000, 2000] with per-depth structure and birth-outcome readings — but it walks 50 synthetic neutral lineages, not the selected production population, so it answers a different question and does not close this gap.

NARROWED CLAIM: what is genuinely absent from the stored report is a *measured* population generation depth at any tick before the last one, and any population-level spread beyond median and max. The consequence is narrower than "turnover cannot be read": it is that the relation between ticks and measured generation depth within a run is unreadable, so one cannot confirm that the derived birth-rate turnover actually translated into advancing lineage depth, nor read where in the run the depth was accumulated.

PROPOSAL CORRECTION: adding `mean_generation` alone gives the trajectory half and does NOT address the spread half the finder's own `missing` field names (no min, no quartiles). A spec should either store median at the same cadence instead of/alongside the mean, or explicitly drop the spread complaint. Also note the criterion cited (`docs/roadmap.md:45`, "every closure reading is taken at 22 generations") is a historical 2026-09-07 record, not a current reading — the newest stored closure reads median 49, so the criterion should be cited as the origin of the concern, not as the present depth.

Narrow the claim on five points. (a) "Cohort turnover rate cannot be read" is overstated: `births_total` is on all 20 persistence samples and `births_per_100_ticks` is a top-level indicator, so birth-driven turnover IS readable across the run. The genuine absence is narrower — the generation-depth trajectory (ticks-per-generation within a run, whether depth is still advancing at the horizon) and the depth spread (min/quartiles). (b) The stored depth reading is conditional, not unconditional: it exists only in the GOAL profile, only at `cases[].mutational_neighborhood.evolved.per_seed[].generation_distribution`, and falls back to `Indicator::Undefined` when the neighborhood battery is absent (bench.rs:1176, 2311). The gate sibling `docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability.json` contains exactly one `"generation"` key (the founder's) and zero population depth. So the sole population depth reading rides on the mutational_neighborhood indicator. (c) Layer naming: `mean_generation` is NOT in SimStats (layer a) and NOT a `last_tick_*` field (layer c). It lives at `crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:184` in `structure_means`, feeding the `v3-cli run` NDJSON stream (already present in `docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/{cost,control}.ndjson`) — a fourth surface. The gap is at layer (b) and the reuse is within the same crate, so the cheap-fix argument stands, but state the surface precisely. (d) Preempt a reader confusion the key names invite: `drift_depth`'s checkpoints 0/22/250/1,000/2,000 and its `median_generations` are a synthetic drift-walk depth AXIS over 50 lineages, not the live population's depth over time; they do not fill this gap. (e) Do not carry "generation 22" forward as current. The roadmap.md:45 citation is accurate as a dated 2026-09-07 note, but the newest closure reads median 49 / max 62 on the T12.F04 baseline worlds, so 22 is historical, not what is stored today. The proposal itself survives the hard constraints: `mean(creature.generation)` is applied simulation state, a mean not a composite score, consumes no RNG, and is O(population) on the already-gated 20-sample cadence that `mean_energy` uses (bench.rs:1755-1758 comment) — same cost class, effectively free, and correctly paired with the `mean_genome_size`/`mean_mesh_nodes` proposal (both also grep to 0 in the goal JSON).

title: memory_sensitivity fractions have no exposure denominator; the carrier census exists only for 12 sampled genomes per seed
missing: Per seed, the count of final creatures whose reachable structure can respond to the intervened substrate at all: reads_shared_memory / writes_shared_memory / has_stateful_compute_node / has_plasticity over the whole final population. The computation already exists and is pure and RNG-free (`structural_companions`, crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/companions.rs:13-34), but it is run only over the 12 genomes per seed sampled by the mutational-neighborhood probe.
evidence: docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json: memory_sensitivity.per_seed[] carries only {different_from_{zeroed,scrambled,either}_{count,fraction}, final_creature_count, seed} — final_creature_count is every living creature (8,818 / 7,715 / 21,818), unfiltered. Companions are stored only at deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].mutational_neighborhood.evolved.per_seed[].sampled_genomes[].companions — 12 genomes per seed, 36 total, with reads_shared_memory true for 2/12, 7/12, 1/12 and has_plasticity false for all 36, while the same report records deterministic.totals.plasticity_updates = 2,922,222. The denominator is set at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:2005-2035 (fraction over `observations.len()`), and crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:263-290 shows `observe_final_actions` evaluates every living creature with no structural filter. docs/progress.md line 54 already reconciles the mismatch by hand: "a probe blind spot or inert structure, not proof memory is absent."
why: The sample-size field is not what is missing — count and final_creature_count are both stored, so a binomial interval is computable downstream, and no CI field is needed. What is missing is exposure. The denominator includes every creature whose reachable structure cannot read the intervened substrate, so the fraction moves with population composition and neither a flat reading nor a rise can be attributed. companions.rs:1-5 states this is precisely what companions are for: "so a zero neighborhood reading can be attributed to absent structure, inert (unreachable) structure, or a probe blind spot rather than assumed to mean 'no sensitivity'" — yet that attribution is available for 12 of 8,818-21,818 creatures. Readings are currently 1, 2 and 4 different-from-either creatures per seed; with no exposure count, a future rise cannot be shown to be a rise in memory use rather than a change in who is alive.
criterion: The goal profile's cognition indicators (memory sensitivity first, learning and prediction measures as they are added) rise across the series of closed features relative to the goal series' first reading, and each rise survives at least one later feature.
proposal: Inside the goal-indicator block only — the `observe_goal_indicators.then(...)` closure at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1901-1930 — call the existing `structural_companions` over `sim.creatures` and store, per seed, four u64 carrier counts plus the population n next to the existing memory_sensitivity per-seed row. Counts only: no ratio, no composite, no new probe, no extra run. Keep it out of the unconditional path so the gate profile's cost is unchanged (`functional_complexity` already walks every creature unconditionally at bench.rs:1891-1894, which is the cost precedent; `mesh_reachable_nodes` at crates/v3-core/src/creature/genome/analysis.rs:260-272 is an uncached BFS, so this is a second whole-population walk, not free). New report fields carry serde defaults per the T01.F11 precedent so stored reports still load.
corrections: Absence confirmed; three points in the finder's evidence and framing need narrowing. (a) The plasticity contrast is misread, not a probe blind spot: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:1048-1059 accumulates `plasticity_updates_total` while iterating `creature.genome.nodes.iter().enumerate()` — every node, reachable or not — whereas companions' `has_plasticity` is reachable-only. 0/36 reachable plasticity alongside 2,922,222 updates is fully consistent with plasticity living entirely in unreachable junk and is not evidence that the 12-per-seed sample missed carriers. (The proposed population-wide reachable count is in fact what would disambiguate junk plasticity from reachable plasticity, so the proposal survives its own evidence being wrong.) (b) Layer and cost: this is absent at all three layers, not merely unstored — no SimStats counter and no population-wide computation exists anywhere — so it is a genuinely new closure-time whole-population walk, not the serialization of an existing counter. `mesh_reachable_nodes` (crates/v3-core/src/creature/genome/analysis.rs:261-273) resolves each edge target with a linear `iter().position()` over all genome nodes, giving per-genome cost O(reachable x targets x total_nodes) including drift-accumulated junk, while the cited precedent `functional_complexity` (analysis.rs:423-448) uses a HashMap index. It is likely still bounded at goal-profile scale, but a spec must time it in the wall-clock block rather than call it free. (c) The four flags do not map one-to-one onto the four probes: `reads_shared_memory` folds LoadSlot/LoadSlotImm/LoadSlotPrev together, so it is exposure for both `memory_sensitivity` (current slots) and temporal `previous_slots` without separating them; `has_stateful_compute_node` and `has_plasticity` correspond to `operator_state`; nothing among the four covers `persisted_outputs` (graph `tick_start_outputs`). A spec should split the read flag or state explicitly which probe each count is the exposure denominator for.

Three narrowings, none flipping the verdict. (a) The criterion at roadmap.md:35 asks only that the indicator rise; it names no denominator, so the need for exposure is interpretive rather than literally required. It is well-anchored — companions.rs:1-5 states exactly this purpose, and docs/roadmaps/t09-cognition-and-learning.md:44 already uses the word ("An inadequate exposure or inconclusive comparator is recorded as such") — but "criterion cited" overstates the link: the criterion needs the fraction; exposure is what makes a rise in that fraction readable. (b) The cost is unmeasured and should not be sold as free. `mesh_reachable_nodes` (crates/v3-core/src/creature/genome/analysis.rs:260-272) calls `position()` inside its BFS, giving O(total_nodes x targets x total_nodes) per genome, whereas `functional_complexity` (analysis.rs:424) builds a HashMap index first; no genome node cap exists in v3-core. Over 21,818 creatures the pessimistic cost is low single-digit seconds, not ~100 ms — still under ~3% of the 485 s goal run, so the disproportionate-cost test fails either way, but the spec should state the bound honestly and reuse functional_complexity's indexed BFS rather than the O(n^2) walk. (c) The proposed "plus the population n" is redundant: `final_creature_count` already sits in the same per-seed row. Store the four carrier counts only.

Three narrowings, none fatal.

(1) The proposed count is an UPPER BOUND on exposure for `memory_sensitivity`, not an exact denominator. `crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/companions.rs:48-52` ORs `LoadSlotPrev` into `reads_shared_memory` alongside `LoadSlot`/`LoadSlotImm`, so the flag conflates current-tick and previous-tick reads, while the probe intervenes on the 16 current slots only (`[0.0; 16]` at `crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:281`; predeclared at `docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:90`). To be an exact denominator the flag needs splitting into current vs previous. Conversely, `has_stateful_compute_node` and `has_plasticity` are the exposure flags for `temporal_memory_sensitivity`'s operator_state and persisted_outputs arms, not for `memory_sensitivity` — so the four counts serve two indicators, which the claim should say.

(2) The `has_plasticity` 0/36 vs `plasticity_updates` 2,922,222 juxtaposition is a sampling gap, not a contradiction: the counter is cumulative over every creature-tick in the run, including creatures that died, and T11.F01's own report had 3 of 36 sampled genomes carrying plasticity (`docs/specs/roadmap/t11-f01-mutational-neighborhood-indicator.md:401-403`). It is suggestive evidence for sample blindness, not proof of it.

(3) The per-seed `different_from_either_count` readings are 1 (seed 11), 4 (seed 22), 2 (seed 33), not "1, 2 and 4" in that seed order.

title: plasticity_updates counts edge visits, not weight changes — churn and learning are indistinguishable
missing: A counter of plasticity updates whose written weight actually differs from the prior weight. Both update loops increment unconditionally, so an update with dw == 0.0 (zero pre/post activity, or a zero outcome signal, or a zero eligibility trace) and an update already pinned at the +/-weight_clamp boundary each increment the counter identically to a real weight move.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/runtime/plasticity/hebbian.rs:144-146 — `weights[edge_idx] = (w + dw).clamp(-w_clamp, w_clamp); total_cost += cost_per_update; update_count += 1;` with no comparison of old versus new. Identical shape at crates/v3-core/src/runtime/plasticity/reward.rs:77-80. The counts reach SimStats at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:604 (Hebbian, via WorkCounters) and tick.rs:1059 (reward-modulated). The stored goal report records deterministic.totals.plasticity_updates = 2,922,222 (per_creature_tick 0.046976) with no change/no-op split anywhere. SimStats already carries the analogous distinction for the mutation domain: mutation_events_applied_total_semantic_noop and _semantic_change at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:208,210.
why: Whether any of the 2.92M recorded plasticity updates moved a weight cannot be answered from the stored report. A population of saturated or zero-signal edges reads exactly like live learning. The counter's only closure use today is as a compute-cost regression signal — docs/progress.md line 67 flags "plasticity work +30.64%" for T11.F18 — which says nothing about learning. The T09 track states the constraint directly (docs/roadmaps/t09-cognition-and-learning.md:46): "Controller size, executed operations, memory writes, or plasticity updates are not cognition by themselves. Use them only as supporting structural observations." As a structural observation, a visit count without a change count supports nothing.
criterion: Distinguish execution failure, inaccessible mutations, insufficient retention, absent ecological benefit, and inadequate exposure.
proposal: Add one u64 to SimStats, `plasticity_updates_changed_total`, incremented at those same two sites only when the stored weight differs from its prior value — the old value is already in hand (`w` at hebbian.rs:144, `weights[edge_idx]` at reward.rs:78). This is an ADDITIONAL field: do not redefine or split `plasticity_updates_total`, which is a pinned comparison counter (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:34, asserted at ComparisonLevel::Severe in crates/v3-cli/tests/bench.rs:460-465) with live epoch baselines, and which also drives the per-update energy charge. Store the new counter beside plasticity_updates in the per-seed/totals work-counter block as a reported field only, without adding it to the pinned comparison counter list, and with a serde default per the T01.F11 precedent so stored reports still load.
corrections: Claim stands; three narrowings. (1) The enumerated no-op causes are partly wrong and understate the strongest case: "zero pre/post activity" yields dw == 0.0 only for Classic, Oja and AntiHebb — the Covariance rule computes `eta * (pre - 0.5) * (post - 0.5)`, which is `eta * 0.25` at pre = post = 0 (hebbian.rs:136-141). The guaranteed no-op the finder missed is a zero learning rate: `cfg.learning_rate.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` admits eta = 0.0 at hebbian.rs:101 and reward.rs:54 with no guard, so a plasticity node configured at rate 0 increments the counter and charges `cost_per_update` energy on every edge, every tick, with mathematically zero weight movement. f32 rounding (`w + dw == w` for tiny dw within clamp) is a further no-op that still counts. (2) The "+30.64%" figure in docs/progress.md is the T11.F18 GATE profile's flag against T03.F08, not a goal-report reading. (3) The T09 track's line 47 ("Freeze or reset learned weights and reward traces when testing learning dependence") is T09.F08's planned behavioral learning-dependence indicator; the proposed change counter is a cheaper structural precursor to it, not a duplicate, and should not be folded into or discarded as covered by T09.F08.

Two narrowings. (1) "As a structural observation, a visit count without a change count supports nothing" is overstated. Energy is charged per visit at both sites (`total_cost += cost_per_update` immediately beside each increment), so plasticity_updates_total is the correct quantity for the compute-cost accounting and regression role it currently serves — including the docs/progress.md T11.F18 "+30.64%" flag. It is mute specifically on whether learning occurred, not worthless. (2) Ownership: this is not a standalone new feature. The cited criterion belongs to T09.F08 (docs/roadmaps/t09-cognition-and-learning.md:37, open, "Depends on: T01.F12, T02.F02, T11.F10"), whose scope at t09:43 already covers "interventions for ... learned weights, and reward traces" and directs "Wire new indicators into the goal profile and version changed definitions instead of rewriting old readings." The changed-update counter belongs folded into T09.F08 as a cheap precondition reading — it tells you whether there is any weight movement to intervene on before the freeze/reset interventions are run — rather than opening a separate feature for one u64.

Narrow the claim on four points. (1) The title overstates the fix. A changed-weight counter separates no-op updates from weight-moving updates; it does not separate churn from learning — undirected jitter that moves a weight every step would read 100% changed. Per docs/roadmaps/t09-cognition-and-learning.md:46 ("Controller size, executed operations, memory writes, or plasticity updates are not cognition by themselves. Use them only as supporting structural observations") the counter is a structural observation that rules out a null — it can show that no weight moved — and cannot support a positive learning claim. Retitle to something like "plasticity_updates does not distinguish weight-moving updates from no-ops". (2) "Both update loops increment unconditionally" holds only inside the per-edge loop; both paths bounds-check and `continue`/`break` before it (reward.rs:59-70, hebbian.rs:121-123), so some edges are already skipped entirely. (3) The layer is both (a) runtime-absent and (b) stored-report-absent: the SimStats field alone answers nothing at closure unless it is also emitted in bench.rs's per-seed/totals work-counter block, which the proposal does specify — label it "runtime-absent, and stored-report-absent by consequence". (4) Scale the expected payoff honestly: plasticity fires on roughly 4.7% of creature-ticks (0.046976 per creature-tick, 2,922,222 over 62,207,164), so this splits a minority counter, not the bulk of recorded work. Ownership: rather than a standalone feature, fold the counter into a scheduled owner — T09.F03 or T09.F08, which already own the learning question and the still-Undefined `learning_dependence` key (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:495, 2463) — consistent with docs/roadmaps/t10-evolutionary-scale-and-experiment-infrastructure.md:58.

title: Reward-modulated learning is invisible: its updates are summed into the Hebbian counter and nothing reward-related reaches the deterministic block
missing: A separate count of reward-modulated (three-factor) weight updates. `apply_reward_modulated_updates` already returns `update_count`, and the tick loop adds it into the very same `plasticity_updates_total` field that the Phase-1 Hebbian counter feeds. Nothing separates outcome-driven learning from unsupervised Hebbian churn, and no count of creatures carrying reward-modulated nodes exists at any layer.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:1059 (`sim.stats.plasticity_updates_total += u64::from(update_count);`) and tick.rs:604 (`stats.plasticity_updates_total += self.plasticity_updates;`) write the same field; the doc comment at tick.rs:577-580 confirms it ("plasticity_updates_total also receives the reward-modulated contribution from Phase 2.5"). crates/v3-core/src/runtime/types.rs:108-110 documents the opposite and is wrong: "Hebbian weight updates applied (reward-modulated updates are counted separately in `SimStats`, since they run after the mesh phase)." In the stored goal report, a grep for eligibility/reward/trace/outcome/learning keys returns only environment.phase_wall_clock_ms_per_seed[].reward_learning_ms (2422.37 / 2310.24 / 2545.26 ms — host-dependent wall clock, outside the deterministic block) and the always-Undefined learning_dependence placeholder. T11.F07's own closure report (docs/progress/features/t11-f07-reward-trace-clock-goal.json) is the same.
why: T11.F07 closed the reward-trace clock and the operators that build reward modulation are live in production (EnableRewardModulation / DisableRewardModulation / MutateRewardSource / MutateTraceDecay, crates/v3-core/src/mutation/graph/hebbian.rs:9-12 and mutation/graph/mod.rs:222-225), so the simulation can grow reward-modulated nodes. Yet no closure report can say whether a single reward-modulated update ever fired, nor whether the 2.4 s/seed reward-learning phase does anything beyond scanning creatures with no reward modulation (the `has_reward` early-continue at tick.rs:1023-1032). A frozen-versus-live learning comparison cannot be set up against a mechanism that is not known to fire.
criterion: Goal: Learning within a lifetime. Whether the existing plasticity and reward modulation help a creature in the overgrazing world, measured with learning frozen versus live.
proposal: Add one u64 to SimStats, `reward_modulated_updates_total`, incremented at tick.rs:1059 from the same `update_count` value — in addition to, never instead of, the existing sum, so `plasticity_updates_total`, its energy charge and its pinned epoch baselines are untouched. Store it beside plasticity_updates in the per-seed/totals work-counter block as a reported field, not added to the pinned comparison counter list, with a serde default per the T01.F11 precedent. Fix the stale doc comment at runtime/types.rs:108-110 in the same change.
corrections: Two narrowings. (1) "Nothing reward-related reaches the deterministic block" is overstated: reward-operator names do appear inside `deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].drift_depth.readings[].opportunities.discarded_selected_inapplicable_by_operator.Graph.*` and `...discarded_no_eligible_node_by_operator.Graph.*` (e.g. MutateTraceDecay = 336, MutateRewardSource = 151). Those are single-lineage drift-walk tallies of mutation attempts discarded as inapplicable — evidence the operators are selected and fail on the walked genome, not a reading of reward modulation existing or firing in the live population. Likewise `mutational_neighborhood...sampled_genomes[].companions.has_plasticity` (bench.rs:1127, derived at crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/companions.rs:61 from `compute_node.plasticity.is_some()`) is a battery-sample boolean that is true for plain Hebbian too, so it cannot separate reward-modulated from unsupervised plasticity; every sampled value in the newest report is false. The core claim survives unchanged: no count of reward-modulated weight updates and no count of creatures carrying reward-modulated nodes exists at any layer, and no live-population reward reading reaches the stored report. (2) `crates/v3-core/src/runtime/types.rs:108-110` is misleading, not "wrong / the opposite": "reward-modulated updates are counted separately in `SimStats`, since they run after the mesh phase" is mechanically accurate as "not routed through this `WorkCounters` field"; it invites but does not assert a distinct SimStats field. Treat the same-change edit as a doc clarification, not a documented bug. Minor: the proposal's "its energy charge" implies the counter drives a cost — it does not; `update_cost` is applied per-update at tick.rs:1060 independently of the counter.

Three narrowings; the gap and the proposal survive all of them.

(1) "nothing reward-related reaches the deterministic block" is overstated. Four reward/trace operator names — EnableRewardModulation, DisableRewardModulation, MutateRewardSource, MutateTraceDecay — DO appear inside deterministic.goal_indicators...mutational_neighborhood.operator_rows in both the goal report (42 rows each) and the gate report (founder/operator_rows/33). But aggregated across all 42 rows per operator they read applied 0, changed 0, skipped 1590 of 1590 trials: a mutation-applicability probe over sampled genomes that never once applies, not a production count of updates firing. That existing reading is indirect evidence reward modulation may be unreachable by mutation on this substrate (a T13.F01-style inapplicability signature); the proposed counter converts that inference into a direct production reading. The genuine absences stand — no production count of reward-modulated updates, and no carrier count, at any layer.

(2) "its energy charge" is loose: plasticity_updates_total drives no energy. The charge is update_cost, applied at tick.rs:1057 (creature.energy -= update_cost) independently of the counter, so the counter has no energy semantics to preserve.

(3) Ownership and timing. This has no owning feature today, and AGENTS.md routes changes through roadmap features. T09.F03's dependencies T11.F07 (closed), T11.F09 and T02.F04 are not all met — T11.F09 and T02.F04 are both unchecked — and T09.F03 is second-to-last in the roadmap.md:45 priority order, so this is not a standalone feature and not urgent-now work. Carry it as a one-line rider on whichever comes first: T11.F09 (Learned-State Inheritance Integrity) is the next scheduled feature to touch plasticity weights and traces, otherwise T09.F03's just-in-time spec. Store it in the per-seed/totals work-counter block beside plasticity_updates with a serde default per the T01.F11 precedent — as a supporting structural observation per t09-cognition-and-learning.md:46, not as a new cognition indicator, which also keeps it clear of the "wire the indicator into the goal profile" requirement.

Narrowed claim: `SimStats` has no separate count of reward-modulated (three-factor) weight updates — tick.rs:1059 and tick.rs:604 both write `plasticity_updates_total`, and the stored goal report's `per_seed[].plasticity_updates` therefore cannot attribute its 1.2M updates between unsupervised Hebbian churn and outcome-driven learning. That single field is the whole gap, and no open feature owns it. Three corrections to the finder's framing:

(1) "Nothing reward-related reaches the deterministic block" is FALSE as stated. The stored report does carry reward-related keys inside `deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].mutational_neighborhood`: operator rows for `EnableRewardModulation`, `DisableRewardModulation`, `MutateRewardSource`, `MutateTraceDecay` (and their `Graph.*` forms). What is absent is a reward-modulated *update count*; mutation-event tallies for the reward operators are present.

(2) The doc comment at crates/v3-core/src/runtime/types.rs:108-110 is NOT wrong. Read against T10.F10's spec (lines 84-95, 300-315), "reward-modulated updates are counted separately in `SimStats`" means via a separate call site into `SimStats`, explaining why `WorkCounters.plasticity_updates` excludes them — which is accurate. tick.rs:577-580 documents the merge explicitly. Drop "fix the stale doc comment" from the proposal or downgrade it to an optional clarification; it is not a defect.

(3) "No count of creatures carrying reward-modulated nodes exists at any layer" is overstated. `has_plasticity` (crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/companions.rs:27, surfaced at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1127) is already stored per sampled genome in the goal report and reads 0/36. It is a superset flag (any reachable graph compute node with `plasticity.is_some()`), does not isolate reward modulation, and covers a sample rather than the population — but it exists.

Also correct the value statement, which the evidence makes sharper than the finder claimed: `EnableRewardModulation` requires an existing pure-Hebbian node (crates/v3-core/src/mutation/graph/hebbian.rs:9), founders have none, and the report already shows `EnableRewardModulation` applied 0 / skipped 240 on evolved genomes with `has_plasticity` 0/36. So the stored report already supports the circumstantial inference that reward-modulated updates likely never fire; the proposed counter would confirm that cheaply and directly rather than reveal something wholly invisible. Finally, the proposal's phrase "plasticity_updates_total, its energy charge" is loose — the energy charge is `update_cost`, returned separately by `apply_reward_modulated_updates` and unrelated to the counter.

title: No shared-memory write counter at any layer, though the changed-write predicate already exists in the tracer
missing: A count of applied shared-memory writes, and of writes that changed the slot value. WorkCounters carries mesh_hops, vm_steps, graph_relax_iters and plasticity_updates and nothing for memory; SimStats has no memory counter either. Old and new values are already in hand at every write site.
evidence: VM write sites crates/v3-core/src/runtime/vm.rs:501-507 (StoreSlot), 514-520 (StoreSlotImm) and 527-531 (ClearSlot) each compute `old_value` and `new_value` and pass both to `trace_sink.record_slot_write`. Graph sinks write shared memory at crates/v3-core/src/runtime/cgp/effects.rs:161-174 (WriteSlot / ClearSlot, setting `applied = true`). Production execution uses the no-op sink — crates/v3-core/src/runtime/vm.rs:77, `fn record_slot_write(&mut self, _slot_idx: usize, _old_value: f32, _new_value: f32) {}` — while the inspector-only traced executor implements exactly the changed-write filter at crates/v3-core/src/runtime/traced_vm.rs:82-90: `if (old_value - new_value).abs() > f32::EPSILON`. The WorkCounters struct at crates/v3-core/src/runtime/types.rs:100-111 has no memory field, and stats.rs contains no memory counter.
why: memory_sensitivity reads 1-4 of 8,818-21,818 creatures and nothing in the stored report says whether shared memory is written at all in production. A near-zero read sensitivity with near-zero writes means the substrate is never written; the same reading with millions of writes means memory is written but never reaches a decision. Those are different diagnoses with different owning features, and the report cannot tell them apart. The T09 track has already declared memory writes one of the supporting structural observations it intends to use, and no such observation exists.
criterion: Controller size, executed operations, memory writes, or plasticity updates are not cognition by themselves. Use them only as supporting structural observations.
proposal: Add two u32 fields to WorkCounters (crates/v3-core/src/runtime/types.rs:100-111), `shared_memory_writes` and `shared_memory_writes_changed`, incremented at the three VM sites and the two graph-sink sites, the second using the same epsilon predicate traced_vm.rs:83 already applies. Fold both into SimStats in the existing commit at tick.rs:601-604 alongside vm_steps and mesh_hops, and store them in the per-seed/totals work-counter block as reported fields only — not added to the pinned six-counter comparison list, so epoch baselines and the severe-flag set are unchanged — with serde defaults per the T01.F11 precedent. This is applied execution counted where it happens, in the same per-instruction cost class as vm_steps; no probe, no extra run, no derived score.
corrections: Three narrowings. (1) The claim "nothing in the stored report says whether shared memory is written at all in production" is wrong. The stored goal report already carries a structural boolean `writes_shared_memory` (reading true in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json) at deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].mutational_neighborhood.evolved.per_seed[].sampled_genomes[].companions, computed statically over reachable VM instructions and wired graph sinks at crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/companions.rs:22,37,54,81 and serialized at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1125,2127 — shipped by T11.F01 (closed, docs/roadmaps/t11-...:39). The "absent structure" branch of the finder's diagnosis is therefore already excluded on the sampled genomes; the genuinely unmeasured fact is narrower: whether that structure's writes actually EXECUTE in production and how often they change a slot value. (2) "at any layer" needs one qualifier: individual slot writes are recorded at the inspector layer for sampled creatures (traced_vm.rs:82-90 to runtime/trace/domain.rs:140 to v3-server/src/transport/sample_assembler.rs:131 and sample_protocol.rs:104). What is absent at every layer is a COUNT — cumulative or per-tick — and any count on the production (no-op sink) path. (3) "The T09 track has already declared memory writes one of the supporting structural observations it intends to use" overreads docs/roadmaps/t09-cognition-and-learning.md:46, which is an interpretation caution ("not cognition by themselves ... use them only as supporting structural observations"), not a delivery commitment; T09.F08 is scheduled but far down the priority list in docs/roadmap.md:45 (after T02.F02, depends on T11.F10) and does not own this counter.

The gap is real but three supporting statements are wrong and the proposal needs one correctness clause.

(1) "Nothing in the stored report says whether shared memory is written at all" is FALSE. The goal report already stores `companions.writes_shared_memory` (bench.rs:1124-1127, computed at crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/companions.rs:37-90) on the 12 battery-sampled evolved genomes per world — 7/12, 6/12, 10/12 true in the T13.F01 goal report. It is a wired-write predicate over mesh-reachable nodes, not an applied-write count; it is absent from the founder half and absent entirely from the gate report (0 occurrences). So "the substrate is never written" is already partly excluded structurally. The narrower true claim: no count of applied or changed writes exists at any layer; what exists is a has-a-wired-write boolean on 12 battery-sampled genomes, and mesh-reachable is not executed.

(2) "The T09 track has already declared memory writes one of the supporting structural observations it intends to use, and no such observation exists" misreads docs/roadmaps/t09-cognition-and-learning.md:46. That line is a constraint (memory writes are only supporting structural observations, never cognition), not a declaration of intent — and per (1) a structural observation of memory writes does exist. The gap is the execution count, not the structural observation.

(3) "Old and new values are already in hand at every write site" is FALSE for the two graph sinks: effects.rs:161-174 WriteSlot/ClearSlot overwrite `shared_memory[s]` without reading the prior value, so the changed predicate needs an extra read there. The three VM sites do carry both. Plumbing is otherwise trivial — `side_outputs: &mut MeshSideOutputs` is in scope at effects.rs:108, matching vm.rs:229 and cgp/execute.rs:117.

(4) NEW correctness clause the proposal misses: counting at the VM instruction sites counts VM-local writes, not APPLIED shared-memory writes. vm.rs:166 copies shared memory into `slot_copy`; the copy is committed back only on the halt/terminal paths (vm.rs:190, 196, 466, 485), and both exhaustion paths (vm.rs:225 and 460) break with `NodeResult::exhausted()` under an explicit "Do NOT commit memory" comment. Writes made before an energy exhaustion are therefore discarded. With T03.F10's ramping compute cost live (goal vm_steps -84.6%), exhaustion is not a rare path.
