To satisfy AGENTS.md's "telemetry must derive from applied simulation behavior", the counter must be staged per dispatch and folded into WorkCounters only on the commit paths — or else be named `shared_memory_writes_attempted` rather than applied.

Two narrowings. (1) CRITERION FRAMING: t09:46 is a limiting clause ("not cognition by themselves"), not a commission — the finder overstates it as T09 having "declared memory writes one of the supporting structural observations it intends to use." The load-bearing anchors are instead the T09 Track Success Criterion at docs/roadmaps/t09-cognition-and-learning.md:18 ("The existing VM, graph, mesh, shared-memory, stateful-node, plasticity, and reward-modulation mechanisms are qualified independently and in combination") and the T09.F08 note that "runtime failures require targeted repair in T11" — the never-written vs written-but-unread distinction is exactly that T09-to-T11 handoff decision. The natural owner is T09.F08 or one bounded counter feature ahead of it; the proposal names no owner. (2) APPLIED vs ATTEMPTED — a real defect in the proposal as written: VM slot writes go to a local working copy, `let mut slot_copy: [f32; 16] = *shared_memory;` (vm.rs:166), committed only through `macro_rules! commit_slots` (vm.rs:174-179) at four exits (vm.rs:190, 196, 466, 485). Two exits break WITHOUT committing — vm.rs:225 and vm.rs:460, the first carrying the explicit comment at vm.rs:216-217 "// Do NOT commit memory." on energy exhaustion. Incrementing at the three VM instruction sites therefore counts ATTEMPTED writes, including every write discarded when a dispatch runs out of energy — which under T03.F10's ramped per-step cost (goal vm_steps -84.6% at closure 23f230af) is a common path, not an edge case. That framing fails AGENTS.md's "telemetry must derive from applied simulation behavior." Fix: accumulate per-dispatch locals and fold them into `work_counters` inside `commit_slots!()` so only committed writes count, or rename the field to attempted/instruction-level and say so. The graph path needs no such handling — cgp/execute.rs:299-308 passes the creature's `shared_memory: &mut [f32; 16]` straight through, so effects.rs:161-174 writes land immediately; do not collapse the applied graph writes and the provisional VM writes into one undifferentiated field. Also note the changed-write predicate is per-instruction against the working copy, so two writes to one slot in a dispatch count twice even when the committed net value is unchanged.

title: Structural companions collapse substrates the temporal indicator intervenes on separately
missing: `reads_shared_memory` is a single boolean spanning both current-tick and previous-tick reads, and there is no reward-modulation flag at all. `StructuralCompanions` carries functional_complexity, reachable_node_count, reads_shared_memory, writes_shared_memory, has_stateful_compute_node and has_plasticity — no current/previous split, no has_reward_modulation.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/companions.rs:14-28 (struct) and :50-55, where `LoadSlot | LoadSlotImm | LoadSlotPrev` all set the one flag and the graph branch matches `GraphSource::SharedMemory { .. }`, discarding the `previous` field. The runtime does distinguish them: `SharedMemory { slot: u8, previous: bool }` at crates/v3-core/src/creature/genome/cgp.rs:18, resolved at crates/v3-core/src/runtime/cgp/sources.rs:32-42, and `VmInstruction::LoadSlotPrev` is a distinct opcode at crates/v3-core/src/runtime/vm.rs:522-525. The temporal indicator intervenes on three named substrates — PreviousSlots, PersistedOutputs, OperatorState at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:292-296 — and previous_slots reads 0.000000 in every seed of docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json. Reward modulation is likewise a distinct genome field (`PlasticityConfig.modulation`, set and cleared at crates/v3-core/src/mutation/graph/hebbian.rs:241-283) that no companion reports.
why: previous_slots = 0.000000 across all three seeds cannot be attributed to absent structure versus inert structure, because the only structural flag lumps previous-tick reads together with current-tick reads — exactly the conflation companions.rs:1-5 exists to prevent. The same holds for reward modulation: has_plasticity cannot distinguish a plain Hebbian node from a reward-modulated one, so the reward-update counter proposed elsewhere in this audit would have no structural companion, and the 0/36 has_plasticity reading in the newest report cannot be read against the 2,922,222 plasticity updates in the same report.
criterion: report structural companions per sampled genome: whether any reachable instruction or edge reads or writes shared memory, and whether any stateful compute node or plasticity is present, so a zero sensitivity reading is attributed to absent structure, inert structure, or a probe blind spot rather than read as one thing
proposal: Add two booleans to `StructuralCompanions`: `reads_shared_memory_previous` (set by LoadSlotPrev at companions.rs:50-52 and by `GraphSource::SharedMemory { previous: true, .. }` in the edge scan) and `has_reward_modulation` (true when any reachable graph compute node's `plasticity.modulation` is Some). Leave the existing `reads_shared_memory` in place as the union so current consumers and stored reports are unaffected. All are pure structural reads at sites the walk already visits — the VM arm already names LoadSlotPrev, and the graph edge match only needs the `previous` field it currently discards. New fields carry serde defaults per the T01.F11 precedent. No probe, no execution, no extra run cost.
corrections: Narrower and correctly attributed: the gap is that `StructuralCompanions` (companions.rs:14-28) has no previous-tick read flag and no reward-modulation flag, so the sampled-genome companion block cannot say whether previous-tick reading structure is present at all. Three corrections to the finder's framing. (a) Scope: companions are computed only for the 12 sampled evolved genomes per seed inside `mutational_neighborhood` (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:2198), whereas `temporal_memory_sensitivity` is measured over the full final population (8,818 creatures at seed 11). A `reads_shared_memory_previous` flag would attribute `previous_slots = 0.000000` at 12-genome sample level only, not for the population the indicator scores; the finder's "cannot be attributed" phrasing implies a population-level answer the companion set cannot give either before or after the fix. (b) The "0/36 has_plasticity versus 2,922,222 plasticity_updates" tension is a sample-versus-population and structural-flag-versus-cumulative-counter mismatch, not a modulation split problem; `has_reward_modulation` does not resolve it. Drop that as motivation and justify the modulation flag on its own terms. (c) Reward modulation is not entirely unnamed in the stored report: `EnableRewardModulation`, `DisableRewardModulation` and `MutateRewardSource` appear as mutational-neighborhood `operator_rows` entries (72 occurrences each in the T13.F01 goal report). Those are mutation-trial outcome tallies, not a structural fact about the sampled genome, so the structural gap stands — but the proposal should acknowledge the operator rows as the nearest existing signal rather than claim reward modulation is invisible everywhere.

The previous-tick half stands as stated; the reward-modulation half should be dropped from this item and deferred. (1) `reads_shared_memory_previous` is real, unowned by any open feature, structurally free at sites the walk already visits, and would attribute a live 0.000000 previous_slots reading in 3/3 seeds against structure that mutation can actually create (vm/operators.rs:238, graph/operators.rs:882). Keep it. (2) `has_reward_modulation` adds no information today: `modulation` lives inside `PlasticityConfig`, so the flag is a strict subset of `has_plasticity`, which reads 0/36 in the newest report — the new flag would read 0/36 too and is derivable from the existing field. It also has no reading to attribute, which is the whole purpose companions serve under the cited T11.F01 criterion: no indicator intervenes on learned weights or reward traces, since TemporalMemorySubstrate::OperatorState perturbs `graph.tick_start_state` only (simulation/tick.rs:358-367). Its owner is T09.F08, which explicitly adds the learned-weights and reward-trace interventions (t09:43), or the sibling reward-update counter proposed elsewhere in this audit if that is adopted — the companion travels with whichever reading lands. (3) The stated justification for it is a non-sequitur: the tension between 0/36 has_plasticity and 2,922,222 plasticity_updates is sample scope (36 genomes sampled by the neighborhood battery versus whole-population execution counters), and a modulation flag does not touch it.

Narrow to one boolean, and correct the layer label.

(1) LAYER: the finder labels this `runtime-absent`. Companions are neither SimStats (a) nor per-tick (c) — they are computed in crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/companions.rs and ALREADY STORED in layer (b): 36 companion blocks appear in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json. So this is not the cheap "exists in (a), missing from (b)" plumbing pattern; it is a source-level struct addition with two touch points — the struct and walk in companions.rs, and `to_neighborhood_companions` / `NeighborhoodCompanions` at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:2122. Still cheap, but not one file.

(2) DROP `has_reward_modulation`. Three reasons: (a) the cited criterion names "stateful compute node or plasticity" only — modulation is not in it; (b) it is uninformative by construction today — `has_plasticity` is false in all 36 companion blocks in the newest report, and `modulation` is a sub-field of `PlasticityConfig` (mutation/graph/hebbian.rs:241-283 sets it only on a node that already has plasticity), so the new flag would read false 36/36; (c) the finder's stated motivation — reading 0/36 `has_plasticity` against the 2,922,222 `plasticity_updates` in the same report — is a sample-vs-population scope mismatch (36 sampled neighborhood genomes vs the whole run's runtime updates) that a modulation flag does nothing to resolve, and it leans on a reward-update counter "proposed elsewhere in this audit" that is not itself verified. Reward traces already have an owner: open T09.F08 (docs/roadmaps/t09-cognition-and-learning.md:43) explicitly scopes "separate interventions for current plus previous shared memory, persistent graph state, learned weights, and reward traces."

(3) SCOPE OF THE ATTRIBUTION CLAIM. Companions are per sampled genome (36, drawn for the mutational neighborhood), while `temporal_memory_sensitivity` runs over the full final population (~8,818 + 7,715 + ... creatures). The split therefore attributes the sample's structure — which is exactly what T11.F01 asks for ("per sampled genome") — but does not directly attribute the temporal indicator's own denominator. Do not widen it to a population-level companion to close that gap.

Surviving claim: add one boolean, `reads_shared_memory_previous`, set by `VmInstruction::LoadSlotPrev` at companions.rs:50-52 and by `GraphSource::SharedMemory { previous: true, .. }` in the edge match, keeping the existing `reads_shared_memory` as the union so stored reports and current consumers are unaffected, plumbed through bench.rs:2122 with a serde default.

title: No production mutation supply funnel reaches the stored report; the only stored funnel is the drift walk
missing: SimStats.mutation_events_{attempted,applied,skipped}_total, mutation_events_{attempted,applied}_total_by_{domain,operator}, mutation_events_skipped_by_reason, mutation_events_skipped_total_by_operator, mutation_operator_funnel_total_by_operator and mutation_skip_reasons_total_by_operator are accumulated on every production birth and are never written to the gate or goal JSON.
evidence: ABSENCE: grep -c in crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs returns 0 for every one of those 20 field names (checked individually). Stored key lists confirm it: docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json path .deterministic.per_seed[] has 12 keys (seed, ticks, creature_ticks, mesh_hops, vm_steps, graph_relax_iters, plasticity_updates, actions_applied, births, final_population, extinction_tick, tick_zero_connectivity) and .deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[] has 15 keys, none mutation-related; the gate report docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability.json has the identical per_seed shape. PRESENCE: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:227-270 merges every one of them into sim.stats on each production birth; crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:501-521 already exports them live.
why: The only stored mutation-opportunity funnel is .deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].drift_depth.readings[].opportunities, which is produced by the mutation-only drift walk (crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/drift.rs:1 'Mutation-only lineage depth observations, isolated from ecological state'; DriftSizes::PRODUCTION at drift.rs:35-40). So every stored supply reading is drift by construction. No closure can answer what supply the population under selection actually received (attempted vs applied vs skipped, per domain, per operator), nor compare selection against drift, even though the run counted it all.
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t13-neutral-module-recruitment.md:18 — "A replicated recruitment baseline separates variation between lineages from offspring sampling, and drift from selection; every repair has a comparable reading without replacing historical results." (also :17, "Stored readings distinguish module creation, mutation opportunity, ... denominators and observation limits" — the denominator, births, is already in the row.)
proposal: Extend the existing case-row builder at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1358-1405 — which already lifts sim.stats.move_actions_attempted_total and the move_actions_blocked_total_by_cause map straight into cases[] — with mutation_events_{attempted,applied,skipped}_total plus applied_by_domain and applied_by_operator. Convert the HashMaps through the existing domain_keys/operator_keys BTreeMap helpers at bench.rs:805-819 (already written for the drift walk) so the deterministic block stays byte-reproducible per roadmap.md:38. Raw applied-behavior counts only, no score, no new profile or run.
corrections: Two overstatements to narrow. (1) "Never written" / "no closure can answer what supply the population actually received" is too absolute at the repo level. Besides the live server export the finder cites, crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:65-90 (TickSampleEvent) and build_tick_sample at crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:188-230 already export mutation_events_{attempted,applied,skipped}_total, _total_by_domain, _total_by_operator and the semantic noop/change split into the CLI run's NDJSON stream, and two such streams are stored in-repo at docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/control.ndjson and cost.ndjson. So the production-population supply IS partially recoverable today from sweep side-artifacts — coarsely (no skip reasons, no operator funnel, no reachability split, no per-lineage rows) and only for runs where someone kept the stream. The accurate claim: no production mutation-supply reading reaches the gate or goal closure report that drives docs/progress.md and docs/progress/index.html; the only supply funnel in that report is produced by the mutation-only drift walk, so every stored closure reading of supply is drift by construction and cannot be compared against selection. (2) Minor proposal defect: the domain_keys/operator_keys helpers at bench.rs:805-819 take BTreeMap, but the SimStats maps are HashMap (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:200, 206, 212, 216), so they must be collected into BTreeMap first (or given new helpers) rather than reused directly — the same HashMap-to-ordered-output step WorldTracking::observe already performs for its own lookups.

Four narrowings. (1) "Every stored supply reading is drift by construction" is overstated. .deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].mutational_neighborhood.evolved.per_seed[].sampled_genomes[].operator_rows and .pooled_operator_rows already store attempted/applied/skipped operator tallies over genomes sampled FROM the selected population. The correct, narrower claim: the realized production-birth funnel is unstored; the nearest stored proxy is a one-step probe on sampled evolved genomes using probe RNG, not the run-integrated funnel the population under selection actually received. (2) This lift does not close criterion :18 and only partly serves :17. Pooled per-world totals cover mutation opportunity, domain/operator breakdown and the births denominator, but carry no lineage depth (:17) and cannot separate variation between lineages from offspring sampling (:18); a production-vs-drift funnel comparison is further confounded by generation-depth mix, since generation appears only in the neighborhood sample. Drift-vs-selection separation is owned by T13.F02's baseline assay and T13.F06's "ordinary goal-profile ecological reading"; treat this as a cheap complement, not a route to closing :18. (3) The proposal's mechanics are slightly wrong: domain_keys/operator_keys at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:805-819 take &BTreeMap, while SimStats holds HashMap<MutationDomain, u64> / HashMap<MutationOperator, u64> (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:200-217), so the lift needs a collect-into-BTreeMap step first to stay byte-reproducible — trivial, but "convert through the existing helpers" is not literally true. (4) The absence is broader than the 20 named fields: mutation_outcome_summary, mutation_value_totals_by_operator and mutation_{reachable,unreachable,executed,not_applicable}_target_total are equally unstored, so scope the fix deliberately rather than lifting everything.

The claim's second half is overstated. Strike "nor compare selection against drift": that comparison is T13.F02's explicit charter (docs/roadmaps/t13-neutral-module-recruitment.md:46, criterion :18), a controlled, paired, predeclared design, and the track warns against uncontrolled versions of it (:47) — putting goal-world SimStats totals (~22 generations under selection) next to the drift walk (2,000 generations, 50 lineages, no selection) is not that comparison and must not be sold as it. The defensible narrower claim: no stored gate or goal report — in any docs/progress/features/*.json, not merely the newest — records what mutation supply the goal-world population under selection actually received (attempted vs applied vs skipped, by domain and operator), even though SimStats accumulates all of it on every production birth (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:227-270) and v3-server already exports it live (crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:501-521). Every stored supply reading is drift-walk provenance by construction. No open feature owns that lift; the closest scheduled owners (T13.F02, then T13.F06, then T11.F13) each measure supply inside their own harness or arms rather than in the goal-profile case rows.

title: T11.F17's own delivery instrument (executed/reachable/unreachable target draws) is counted every production run and stored nowhere
missing: SimStats.mutation_reachable_target_total, mutation_unreachable_target_total, mutation_executed_target_total and mutation_not_applicable_target_total — the production share of mutation target draws landing on executed, reachable, or unreachable structure.
evidence: ABSENCE: grep -c in crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs returns 0 for all four names; no matching key anywhere in the goal JSON key tree (only .deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].drift_depth.readings[].opportunities.{reachable,unreachable,executed}_target_events exists, from the drift walk). PRESENCE: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:313-316 accumulates all four per birth; crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:506-508 exports them live; the feature is on by default — executed_bias defaults to 0.9 (crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:763-774, asserted at :2191).
why: Answers the T11.F17 question directly: the 1.0% -> 9.1% figure was an on/off counterfactual over 60 offline gen-1,990 genomes (docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:106), so it is not reproducible from any single stored report by construction. The closest stored proxies are the evolved-half battery changed_fraction (sampled genomes, no A/B arm) and the drift walk's executed_target_fraction (0.688 at depth 2,000 in the t13-f01 goal report) — drift, not selection. The repair's own production instrument, the thing the roadmap already cites as evidence ('the run's own counter records 66.8% of target draws landing on unreachable structure'), is counted on every goal run and never stored, so no later closure can tell whether executed-biased delivery is still delivering under selection.
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:87 — "no closed feature lowers an indicator component below the previous closed feature's reading unless its spec predeclared and justified the change"; the accepted evidence form for this repair is named at :106 ("the run's own counter records 66.8% of target draws landing on unreachable structure").
proposal: Add the four u64 counters to the same case-row builder at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1358-1405, beside the existing move funnel, plus an executed_target_fraction computed with the existing fraction_or_undefined helper over the applied total — the same field shape the drift walk already stores, so the drift and selection readings sit side by side and compare directly. No new run, no new profile.
refutations: Factual absence confirmed but the cited criterion does not require the signal. (1) grep -c in crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs returns 0 for all four names, and bench.rs reads zero stats.mutation_* fields at all; the identically-named JSON fields come from neighborhood::recruitment (bench.rs:789-896, from RecruitmentCheckpoint.opportunities), not SimStats. So the layer claim is true. (2) MISAPPLIED CRITERION: docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:87 ("Floors and the no-regression rule") constrains existing indicator components from regressing; it cannot require creating a new one. (3) MISATTRIBUTED EVIDENCE FORM: :106's "the run's own counter records 66.8% of target draws landing on unreachable structure" is descriptive prose about the user's 281,405-tick pre-repair deep run, not a closure evidence contract. The owning feature's own spec sets the contract and excludes the stored report: docs/specs/roadmap/t11-f17-executed-biased-mutation-targeting.md:70 scopes the counter to MutationSummary/SimulationStats plus the v3-server status block, "no frontend display." T11.F17's goal-profile predeclarations at :106 are on the T11.F16 drift walk and the evolved-half changed fraction, not on a production target-draw counter. (4) THE QUESTION IS ALREADY ASSIGNED: the tail of :106 states the paired long run under selection, executed_bias 0.9 against 0.0 to generation 500+, "was not a closure condition and is the reading T11.F13 takes." A single stored counter cannot answer an A/B question — the finder concedes exactly this about the 1.0%->9.1% figure. (5) SCOPE/VALUE: the signal is neither a diversity nor a cognition measure nor perf regression, so it sits outside the user's standing basic-tracking preference; and at goal depth (median generation 49-56 in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json) it would land in the 0.74-0.86 saturation band visible in the stored drift readings (0.855/0.736/0.691/0.688), i.e. the shallowness T11.F16 was created to escape. SURVIVING TRUE FACT, not a program need: production draws its executed set from ParentExecuted::Record(&parent.graph_runtime.dispatch_record, parent.age) at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:213, while the stored drift walk substitutes ParentExecuted::Indices from battery.executed_node_ids (crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/drift.rs:196-204), so the stored drift executed_target_fraction guards the selector and bias parameter but not the production record plumbing. That plumbing is already guarded at the correct layer by tests — crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick/tests/dispatch_record.rs, crates/v3-core/src/mutation/engine/tests.rs:1357, and the runtime invariant at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:720 — which is a test concern, not a stored-report indicator.
corrections: Three narrowings. (1) Scope the layer precisely: the counters are absent from the stored closure report (layer b) and from every doc under docs/progress/; they are not absent from the codebase, and the T11.F17 spec names them in its Telemetry row (docs/specs/roadmap/t11-f17-executed-biased-mutation-targeting.md:70) without ever recording a value, so "stored nowhere" means "no machine-readable reading in the JSON that drives docs/progress.md and index.html, and no prose reading in the spec either." (2) The finder understates the gap by citing only the newest report: the drift_depth.readings[].opportunities block does not exist in docs/progress/features/t11-f17-executed-biased-mutation-targeting-goal.json at all (it arrived with T13.F01), so T11.F17 closed with zero stored evidence of its own delivery, drift or otherwise. (3) The T11.F17 counting claim does not depend on the feature being enabled — record_target_reachability increments at executed_bias 0.0 too (v3-core/src/mutation/types/mod.rs:699-707, and the spec says so at :560-562), so the "on by default" evidence supports the "still delivering under selection" motive, not the "counted every run" leg. Also note the proposal lands in the goal profile only: cases[] exists solely in the goal JSON, so this would be a goal-run reading, not a per-feature gate reading, and roadmap L87's no-regression rule would govern it only prospectively, once wired in as an indicator component.

Narrower true claim: the PRODUCTION-POPULATION share of mutation target draws is not stored in the goal report; the drift-lineage share already is. Five overstatements to fix:

1. "Stored nowhere" is false. T13.F01 (commit 7d1f9a12, today) stores the identical instrument — reachable_target_events / unreachable_target_events / executed_target_events / executed_target_fraction — in every closure's drift walk (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:789-792, populated at :892-898), 15 occurrences in the t13-f01 goal JSON. Only the production/selection reading is missing.

2. The cited criterion does not require this. docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:87 names the indicator components under the no-regression rule as the drift-depth readings ("behavior-changing births per all births and executed nodes at generations 1,000 and 2,000"). Production target shares are not a declared component, so the rule does not compel them.

3. The gap is broader than framed. deterministic.per_seed and .totals carry NO mutation counters at all (only ticks, creature_ticks, births, actions_applied, vm_steps, mesh_hops, graph_relax_iters, plasticity_updates), and cases[] carries no mutation funnel either — not attempted/applied/skipped. The four target counters are one slice of a whole-funnel absence; a proposal should either say so or scope deliberately.

4. "The drift and selection readings sit side by side and compare directly" is wrong. The drift walk reads a single lineage at fixed checkpoints (gen 22/250/1000/2000); a production counter is cumulative over all births across the whole population. Different denominators, different depth distributions — not directly comparable.

5. It does NOT "answer the T11.F17 question directly." The 1.0% -> 9.1% figure was measured at generation ~1,990. Goal-run genomes reach median generation 49-56 (max 71) across the three baseline worlds, where most births are near-founder and the implementation short-circuits to a uniform draw whenever the executed set equals the mesh. The stored production share would land inside the drift walk's own 0.855 (gen 22) to 0.736 (gen 250) band and be dominated by trivially-executed shallow births. Real but modest value: it is selection rather than drift, over the whole population. Frame it that way, and note T11.F13 already owns the deep under-selection A/B this would not substitute for.

title: Per-operator lifecycle outcomes on real carriers are recorded at every death and never stored
missing: SimStats.mutation_outcome_summary and mutation_value_totals_by_operator — specifically their applied-behavior sums carriers_observed_total, survival_ticks_sum, offspring_spawned_sum, reproduced_once_total, survived_short_horizon_total and survived_long_horizon_total.
evidence: ABSENCE: grep -c in crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs returns 0 for mutation_outcome_summary, mutation_value_totals_by_operator, mutation_outcome_baseline_by_generation_bucket and mutation_outcome_baseline_global; no matching key in the goal or gate JSON. PRESENCE: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:85-104 records an outcome observation for every removed creature carrying at least one birth operator, and the death path reaches it — crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick/helpers.rs:5-19 and crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:184-190 both route through Simulation::remove_creature. The carrier list is populated on every production birth at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:317-320 and assigned at :384. Already exported live at crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:511-521.
why: This is the largest already-built, already-paid-for mutation-effect signal in the codebase and no closure report can read a byte of it: a 6,000-tick goal run makes 1,157,605 births (t13-f01 goal .deterministic.totals.births) and pays the recording cost for every one of them at removal. Two caveats belong in any spec: it is a death-cohort statistic (recorded only on removal, so end-of-run survivors are right-censored and they are the successful ones), and per-operator rows are not disjoint (a multi-operator carrier is recorded once under each of its operators).
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:102 (T11.F13's stated requirement, a planned feature) — "Report requested/applied supply, absolute and conditional behavioral outcomes, discovery, retention, persistence, and compute cost." The 'absolute behavioral outcomes' half is exactly these sums.
proposal: Store ONLY the applied-behavior sums (carriers_observed_total, survival_ticks_sum, offspring_spawned_sum, reproduced_once_total, survived_{short,long}_horizon_total), pooled and per operator via operator_keys at bench.rs:805-819, in the case-row builder at bench.rs:1358-1405. Explicitly exclude viability_score_sum, viability_score_delta_sum, {helpful,neutral,detrimental}_total and confidence_{low,medium,high}_total: that class is a z-score against a running baseline (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:400-441), i.e. a composite score, which fails AGENTS.md's applied-behavior rule and roadmap.md:55/:63. Land it as a stored reading like the move funnel, not as an indicator component, so it does not fall under the no-regression floor rule.
refutations: Lens 3 fails: the cited criterion is real but misattributed, and what it actually asks for is already stored. docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:102 (T11.F13) reads "Report requested/applied supply, absolute and conditional behavioral outcomes, discovery, retention, persistence, and compute cost." In a rate-characterization feature, "conditional" means per applied event and "absolute" means per birth — that is T11.F01's own wording at t11:90, "silent, changed, and dead fractions per operator at one event and per birth." Both halves are already in the stored goal report: docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json carries cases[].mutational_neighborhood.{founder,evolved}.operator_rows[] (per-operator one-event tallies: applied/silent/changed/dead with fractions) and .births (per-birth tallies with a births_total denominator, bucketed by_events). The phrase does not designate death-cohort survival/offspring sums, so the criterion is satisfied by existing storage and this proposal is not needed to meet it. Second, survival/reproductive outcome readings are already owned elsewhere and the program has chosen a controlled design for them that an uncontrolled death pool cannot supply: t09:43 (T09.F08) requires "subsequent survival, resource, and reproductive outcomes over bounded paired trajectories," with starting world/body state and RNGs held fixed and grouped by lineage with uncertainty, and t11:90 states outright that "paired short world trajectories for survival and reproduction are optional and not required for closure." A repo-wide grep of docs/roadmaps/*.md for offspring|survival|realized fitness|carrier|lifecycle returns no criterion asking for per-operator realized fitness from a pooled cohort. Third, the reading cannot bear the interpretation claimed even on its own terms: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:93 gates the pooled summary on a non-empty birth_mutation_operators list, so the sums contain no unmutated comparator at all — per-operator rows can only ever be read against other mutated carriers, never against a baseline, which is why the code pairs them with the generation-bucketed baseline machinery at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:400-441 that the proposal explicitly strips out. Storing them anyway is exactly the confirmatory apparatus the user has deferred, against a standing preference for basic diversity/cognition tracking plus perf regression.
corrections: The gap is real as stated; five mechanics in the proposal need narrowing. (1) `operator_keys` at bench.rs:812 maps `BTreeMap<MutationOperator, u64>` and cannot be reused here — the source is `HashMap<MutationOperator, MutationValueTotals>` (stats.rs:271), so a new mapping into a `BTreeMap<String, _>` is required or the stored report is not byte-stable across runs. (2) The insertion point the finder gives by line range is `WorldTracking::observe` (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1358), the per-case cumulative-counter reader, and it is the right place. (3) The applied sums would ship with no unmutated control cohort: the pooled `mutation_outcome_summary` is itself gated on non-empty `birth_mutation_operators` (simulation.rs:93), so it covers mutated-birth carriers only, and the sole all-removals baseline is the composite `RunningStats` the proposal correctly excludes — a spec must either accept operator-vs-operator comparison only or add a non-carrier removal counter, which would also be the repo's first stored death count. (4) "1,157,605 births ... pays the recording cost for every one" conflates births with removals; removals are unstored (no death counter exists anywhere in SimStats), so that figure is an upper bound and `carriers_observed_total` would itself be the first stored reading of removal volume. (5) The right-censoring caveat is confirmed — bench.rs never drains the population at end of run, so end-of-run survivors are never recorded — and the non-disjoint per-operator rows are confirmed by the per-operator loop at simulation.rs:100-106 recording the same observation once under each carried operator. Finally, the nearer planned owner of lineage mutation-effect attribution is T08.F02 (docs/roadmaps/t08-heredity-and-recombination.md:39), which reads battery silent/changed/dead classes along surviving lineages — the complement of this death cohort — so a spec should state that the two are complementary rather than duplicate.

The mechanical half of the finding is accurate and worth recording as a fact, not as a gap: SimStats.mutation_outcome_summary and mutation_value_totals_by_operator exist (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:271,274), are recorded on every removal carrying a birth operator (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:85-104, reached via tick/helpers.rs:9-15 and tick.rs:184-189), and are exported live (crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:511-521) but appear zero times in crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs and in the stored gate/goal JSON. That absence is real and deliberate-compatible: no current or planned criterion requires it, T11.F13 will predeclare and store its own readings when it runs, and if per-operator realized-fitness ever is wanted, T09.F08 and T11.F13 already specify the paired-trajectory, fixed-RNG, lineage-grouped form it must take rather than an uncontrolled, right-censored, non-disjoint death cohort.

The gap and the exclusion argument stand; four things in the claim need narrowing.

1. CRITERION MISATTRIBUTED. T11.F13's "absolute and conditional behavioral outcomes" (docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:102) is T11.F04's phrase from :93 — "report absolute outcomes per all births alongside conditional mutated-birth fractions" — i.e. battery silent/changed/dead measured per all births versus per mutated births. It is not a request for survival/offspring lifecycle sums. T11.F13 IS scheduled (docs/roadmap.md:45), but it is not this telemetry's owner and its criterion does not support the proposal. The honest framing is that no criterion asks for this reading today; it is an unclaimed cheap signal, and the track criterion it would actually serve is T08's "Along surviving lineages, heritable changes that altered behavior are distinguished from silent ones" only obliquely, since these sums are pooled death-cohort outcomes and not per-lineage.

2. NOT PURELY "ALREADY BUILT" — a non-carrier reference is missing. `mutation_outcome_summary` is gated on a non-empty `birth_mutation_operators` (simulation.rs:93), so it covers dead carriers only. The one all-removals accumulator, `mutation_outcome_baseline_global`, holds a viability_score mean/std — exactly the composite the proposal correctly excludes. Storing only carrier rows therefore yields sums with no clone/non-carrier control; the numbers are comparable across operators and against nothing else. A spec should either add one `MutationValueTotals` accumulator on the else-branch of `remove_creature` (a small runtime addition, not a bench-only change) or state in the report that rows carry no non-carrier baseline.

3. COST PHRASING. `build_mutation_outcome_observation` and `classify_mutation_outcome` run for EVERY removal, clones included (simulation.rs:88-92); only `record_outcome` is carrier-gated. The cost is per removal, not per birth, and carrier recordings are far fewer than 1,157,605.

4. SPEC MECHANICS TO CARRY. (a) The carrier list is `summary.applied_by_operator.keys()` (reproduction.rs:317-318) — a SET of distinct operators, so a three-VmInsert carrier records once under VmInsert; per-operator rows are non-disjoint across operators AND collapse event multiplicity within one. (b) `survived_{short,long}_horizon` are thresholds on `creature.age` against `SHORT/LONG_SURVIVAL_HORIZON_TICKS` (simulation.rs:125-126) — applied behavior, but the constants must be recorded in the report. (c) `mutation_value_totals_by_operator` is a `HashMap` (stats.rs:271), so the reading must be collected into a `BTreeMap<String, _>` keyed by `operator.as_key()` (the pattern of `operator_keys` at bench.rs:812-819) or the `deterministic` block will not reproduce byte-for-byte. (d) The exclusion of viability_score/{helpful,neutral,detrimental}/confidence_* is correct and required: simulation.rs:139-140 literally comments "Composite score tuned for observability", and roadmap.md:55 and :63 forbid a composite score.

title: Operators discarded for selecting an inapplicable node are computed on every production birth and thrown away
missing: No SimStats counter aggregates MutationSummary.events[].discarded — the operators the engine selected, found no applicable site for, and threw away before another operator of the same domain succeeded.
evidence: ABSENCE: record_attempt (crates/v3-core/src/mutation/types/mod.rs:603-611) is called only for the winning operator (crates/v3-core/src/mutation/engine/mod.rs:328), so MutationOperatorFunnel.attempted/applicable never sees a discard; crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:227-316 reads no field of summary.events at all; grep for discarded_selected_inapplicable outside tests hits only crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/recruitment.rs:257,315,354. PRESENCE: the records are built on every birth at crates/v3-core/src/mutation/engine/mod.rs:315-338 (MutationEventRecord.discarded), and the offline aggregate is already stored at .deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].drift_depth.readings[].opportunities.discarded_selected_inapplicable_by_operator.
why: T13.F01's headline finding — roughly half of attempted mutation events discard an operator after selecting an inapplicable node — is the evidence base for T13.F03, and it is measurable only on the drift walk. The identical per-event record is produced for every one of the 1.16M production births in a goal run and dropped on the floor, so T13.F03's repair cannot be read under selection, only under drift.
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t13-neutral-module-recruitment.md:19 — "Adding modules that cannot accept an operator does not suppress that operator on valid targets elsewhere; growth and connection operations still reach silent scaffold."
proposal: One HashMap<MutationOperator,u64> in SimStats summed from summary.events[].discarded in the existing merge block at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:227-316, then one stored map in the case row via operator_keys (bench.rs:805-819). Reuse the drift walk's field name discarded_selected_inapplicable_by_operator so the drift and selection readings are directly comparable. Observation only: the records already exist, so this consumes no RNG and changes no execution.
corrections: Three narrowings, none of which change the verdict. (1) The proposal's "one HashMap<MutationOperator,u64>" is wrong as written and would produce a mislabeled field: `Opportunities::record` (crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/recruitment.rs:312-318) splits `events[].discarded` on `pick.is_some()` into TWO maps — `discarded_selected_inapplicable_by_operator` (a node was selected, no applicable site) and `discarded_no_eligible_node_by_operator` (nothing was ever selected). Summing raw `discarded` into a single map and reusing the first field name would silently fold the second population into it. The production counter must be both maps, split the same way, or it is not the same reading. (2) The proposal's comparability claim does not hold with the discard map alone. A full key walk of the stored goal report finds NO production per-operator mutation counter of any kind — no attempted_by_operator, no funnel, no skip-by-operator — outside the battery and the drift walk. That is a separate and distinctly cheap layer-(b) gap: SimStats already carries `mutation_events_attempted_total_by_operator`, `mutation_operator_funnel_total_by_operator` and `mutation_skip_reasons_total_by_operator`, and bench.rs stores none of them. The drift readings store `attempted`, `attempted_by_operator` and both discard maps together; a production discard map with no denominator beside it cannot be compared to them, so the proposal must also store the production attempted-by-operator denominator in the same case row. (3) "computed on every production birth" overstates by ~2x: records are built per attempted mutation event, and the walk shows ~0.55 attempts per birth (55,204 attempted / 100,000 births; `zero_event_births` exists for exactly this). Read it as "every attempted mutation event on every production birth."

The runtime absence and the layer call ("runtime-absent") are correct, but three parts of the framing are overstated and should be narrowed. (1) The cited criterion does not require this signal. T13.F03's scope note in the same track file specifies the proof mechanism as fixtures and property tests — "Prove with fixtures/properties that padding a genome with operator-inapplicable modules cannot erase a valid target, growth still reaches blank modules, and genuinely unavailable operators skip atomically." A production discard counter is the consequence reading the same note calls for ("changed applied mixes are measured consequences of the repair"), i.e. useful corroboration under selection, not a precondition for satisfying criterion :19. Drop "T13.F03's repair cannot be read under selection" as a blocking claim; it is a real but non-blocking observability gap. (2) "Directly comparable to the drift reading" is false as proposed. The drift walk's Opportunities row (crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/recruitment.rs:240-258) carries `births`, `attempted`, and `attempted_by_operator` alongside the discard maps, giving the map a denominator. A key walk of docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json shows NO production-birth mutation counter of any kind reaches cases[] — not even the already-existing SimStats `mutation_events_attempted_total_by_operator`. Storing the discard map alone would give it no denominator. The proposal must also store `attempted_by_operator` (and births) beside it, or drop the comparability claim. (3) It is therefore not a trivial reuse of an existing row shape: this would be the first production-birth mutation reading in the stored case row, a new reading class. Still cheap, but scope it and justify it as such rather than as "one more map via operator_keys."

Narrower claim: SimStats has no per-operator counter for MutationEventRecord.discarded, so the goal run's ~1.1M production births (372,811 births/seed x 3 cases in the T13.F01 goal report) build the records and drop them; the only stored discard reading is the offline drift walk. Three overstatements to fix. (1) "T13.F03's repair cannot be read under selection, only under drift" is too strong: T13.F02, the next scheduled feature, reuses these same event records under bounded selection in its harness; what is uniquely missing is a whole-population reading from the production goal run, not any selection reading. (2) The cited criterion (docs/roadmaps/t13-neutral-module-recruitment.md:19) is T13.F03's semantics criterion, which its scope proves by fixtures and properties; the stored-readings criterion (line 17) was already answered by T13.F01's drift walk. This counter buys drift-vs-selection comparability, not an otherwise unmet track criterion. (3) The proposal would store an unanchored numerator: no production mutation telemetry of any kind reaches the stored report today — mutation_events_attempted/applied/skipped_total, the per-operator maps, and mutation_operator_funnel_total_by_operator all exist in SimStats but never enter bench.rs's JSON (they surface only in the CLI run NDJSON, crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:202-215). A stored discard map therefore needs its production denominators stored beside it, and should mirror both drift-walk maps (discarded_selected_inapplicable_by_operator and discarded_no_eligible_node_by_operator, crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:798-800) for the direct comparison the proposal wants.

title: The production clone fraction (births receiving no applied mutation event) is not counted
missing: A count of production births whose MutationSummary applied no event — the clone fraction, and with it the per-birth supply distribution's zero mass.
evidence: ABSENCE: grep for zero_event across crates/v3-core/src and crates/v3-server/src hits only crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/{births.rs,recruitment.rs,drift.rs} and one engine test; SimStats (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:191-348) carries no per-birth event-count field, and it is not recoverable from totals because the per-birth event count is a draw, not 0/1. PRESENCE: applied_events > 0 is already production's own mutated-birth gate at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:323 and :339; the drift walk stores its own version at .drift_depth.readings[].opportunities.zero_event_births (55,878 of 100,000 at depth 2,000 in the t13-f01 goal report).
why: roadmap.md:64 carries "90.2% of births are clones" as a standing 2026-09-04 audit fact that no closure has re-read since, on a substrate whose mutation delivery has changed repeatedly (T11.F04, T11.F17, T11.F18). Note a definition divergence already live in the same stored report: crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/recruitment.rs:282 counts attempted_events == 0 while crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/births.rs:116 counts applied_events == 0, and both are serialized as zero_event_births under drift_depth. Any production counter must pick one and say so.
criterion: docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:102 (T11.F13's stated requirement) — "Report requested/applied supply, absolute and conditional behavioral outcomes, discovery, retention, persistence, and compute cost."
proposal: One u64 in SimStats incremented in the existing merge block at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:227 when summary.applied_events == 0, matching production's own gate at :323/:339 rather than the recruitment tracker's attempted-based definition; store it plus a fraction over the existing per-seed births denominator in the case row. Name it so it cannot be confused with the drift walk's attempted-based reading.
refutations:
REFUTED on two independent grounds.

GROUND 1 — the reading already exists in the stored closure report (layer b), computed with the finder's own proposed definition. `docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json` carries, per case, `mutational_neighborhood.founder.births.{zero_event_births, births_total, by_requested_events, by_events}` and `mutational_neighborhood.evolved.per_seed[].pooled_births.{zero_event_births, births_total, by_requested_events, by_events}`. Today's values: founder 292/500 = 58.4%; evolved 1300/2400 = 54.2% on genomes sampled by rank from each seed's final population (median generation 49-56), on all three baseline worlds. It is computed at `crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/births.rs:116` as `applied_events == 0` — exactly the definition the finder says a new counter "must pick." The finder listed births.rs among its own grep hits but disclosed only the drift walk's attempted-based reading (`recruitment.rs:282`), omitting the neighborhood probe's applied-based one in the same stored report. Three of the finder's specific claims fail as a result: (i) "roadmap.md:64 carries 90.2% ... that no closure has re-read since" is false — this probe runs in every goal closure, and `docs/progress/readings/t11-f04-mutation-supply-and-neutral-scaffold.md:89` and `:193` explicitly recorded the successor numbers ("292" zero-applied of 500 founder births; "1,300 zero-applied births and 1,100 mutated births" of 2,400) at T11.F04's closure; (ii) "the per-birth supply distribution's zero mass" is not missing — `by_requested_events` and `by_events` are the full per-birth histograms; (iii) the task's cheap-gap pattern (present in runtime/per-tick, absent from the stored report) is inverted here — the quantity is present in the stored report and absent only from SimStats, which is not the flagged gap shape.

GROUND 2 (Lens 2) — a SCHEDULED feature owns it. T11.F13 "Mutation-Rate Characterization" is unchecked at `docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:63` and appears in roadmap.md's priority list for new starts at `docs/roadmap.md:45` (after T11.F10, before T12.F04) — so this is a scheduled owner, the strong form of refutation, not an unscheduled/deferred one. Its criterion at t11:102 is the very line the finder cited: "Report requested/applied supply, absolute and conditional behavioral outcomes, discovery, retention, persistence, and compute cost." Precedent that the probe is the accepted layer for this quantity: closed T11.F04's criterion at t11:93 required "Keep requested, applied, and skipped supply distinct and report absolute outcomes per all births alongside conditional mutated-birth fractions," and it was satisfied by exactly this neighborhood probe rather than a SimStats counter. Nearby T13.F02 (`docs/roadmaps/t13-neutral-module-recruitment.md:28`) also carries recruitment-opportunity pooling via `recruitment.rs`.

The criterion is real and quoted verbatim (docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:102 does say "Report requested/applied supply, absolute and conditional behavioral outcomes, discovery, retention, persistence, and compute cost"), and every code line reference checks out. But the proposed counter fails Lens 3 on need: it would report a config constant that the closure report already carries.

(1) ALREADY STORED, UNDER THE PROPOSAL'S OWN DEFINITION. The finder proposes counting applied_events == 0 "rather than the recruitment tracker's attempted-based definition". That exact counter already exists and already ships in every goal report: crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/births.rs:116-117 counts applied_events == 0, and it is serialized at deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].mutational_neighborhood.evolved.per_seed[].pooled_births.zero_event_births = 1300 of births_total 2400 (0.542) and .founder.births.zero_event_births = 292 of 500 (0.584) in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json. The evolved half is sampled from the real goal-run population, not the founder drift walk.

(2) RECOVERABLE FROM CONFIG, so it is not a measurement. crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:785-786 sets mutation_probability = 0.44 and per_birth_mutation_events_min = 1, so the gate at crates/v3-core/src/mutation/engine/mod.rs:22-24 is a plain Bernoulli and a passing gate always requests >= 1 event. Zero-attempt mass is therefore 1 - 0.44 = 0.56 by construction, confirmed arithmetically in the stored report: 100,000 births - 55,878 zero-event = 44,122 mutated = 0.441. The finder's stated reason for irrecoverability ("the per-birth event count is a draw, not 0/1") is wrong: the gate is exactly 0/1.

(3) THE APPLIED/ATTEMPTED SPLIT IS EMPIRICALLY EMPTY, which is the only thing that could have made the applied side unrecoverable. Skipped events are 11 of 55,204 attempted in the drift walk (drift_depth.readings[4].opportunities: attempted 55,204, applied 55,193, skipped 11) and skipped: 0 in BOTH neighborhood batteries (evolved pooled_births.any_events.skipped = 0, founder births.any_events.skipped = 0). So applied-zero equals attempted-zero to within 0.02%, and the memory note's "~half of attempted mutation events discard an operator" (T13.F03) is an in-event redraw, not a counted skip. A new u64 would confirm 0.56 to three decimals.

(4) "No closure has re-read since" is false. Every closure re-reads a clone fraction, including the applied-based one in (1); drift_depth.readings[].opportunities.zero_event_fraction reads 0.5427, 0.5552, 0.5551, 0.5588 across checkpoints in the same report.

Adding a runtime counter for a quantity fixed by a config constant and already serialized twice is exactly the kind of confirmatory machinery the user rejected as overengineered (KISS decision 2026-09-07). Separately, the criterion is T11.F13's, and T11.F13 has not started (it is gated after T11.F10, which is not closed), so under the same-feature wiring rule this is not an outstanding obligation of any closed feature.
corrections: The only thing genuinely absent is a SimStats counter over the run's actual production births — i.e. a clone fraction weighted by which parents really reproduce, over all ~260k real births, rather than the probe's fixed resample of 12 ranked genomes x 200 births per seed. That residual is worth little: `requested_event_count` is genome-independent (`crates/v3-core/src/mutation/engine/mod.rs`, per `docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:106`, "draws 0.55 events per birth regardless of genome size") and the stored probe reads zero skipped requests, so the production clone fraction equals P(zero requested) plus P(all requested events skipped), and only the second term can diverge from the probe. The tell is that `zero_event_births` reads an identical 1300/2400 across all three seeds and all three worlds: the reading is fixed by the birth-seed stream and the supply policy, not by the population, so a production counter would converge to the same value up to sampling noise on the skip term. The correct narrow framing is therefore "the applied-event skip term is not observed over production births," not "the production clone fraction is not counted" — and the definition divergence the finder raises (attempted-based in `recruitment.rs:282` vs applied-based in `births.rs:116`) is already resolved in favor of applied-based wherever the clone fraction itself is reported.

The absence is real but the significance is overstated. The roadmap's standing "90.2% of births are clones" (docs/roadmap.md:64) is essentially 1 minus the mutation trigger probability, not an emergent property: `mutation_probability` was 0.10 at the 2026-09-04 audit and is now 0.44 (crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:785, raised by commit c542c87f, T11.F04), and the drift walk's stored `zero_event_fraction` of 0.558780 (55,878/100,000) is 1 - 0.44 to three digits. So the attempted-based clone fraction is already a config constant, and the applied-based counter the finder proposes adds only the all-skipped residual over it — 11 skipped of 55,204 attempted events in that same drift reading. The honest new information is that residual on production genomes (which sit nearer `genome_size_cap` 1200 than drift-walk genomes do), not a re-read of a 90.2% figure whose movement is explained by the config change alone. Two additions: (1) the finder understates the surrounding gap — `mutation_events_*` and `carriers_observed_total` appear zero times in the stored goal JSON, so layer (b) carries no production mutation-supply reading of any kind, and a clone count would be the first; (2) ownership is partly pre-assigned — docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md T11.F13 already requires "Report requested/applied supply, absolute and conditional behavioral outcomes, discovery, retention, persistence, and compute cost", though as per-arm reporting for its rate comparison rather than a standing production counter. Minor: the finder's grep list omits crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/recruitment/tests.rs, a test file, which is immaterial.

Two narrow findings survive, and neither is a runtime telemetry gap; both are documentation/naming fixes.

(a) STALE ROADMAP FACT (real, and the finder's best point). docs/roadmap.md:64 carries "90.2% of births are clones" as a 2026-09-04 audit fact pinned to commit 4b8650ef. That figure implies mutation_probability ~= 0.098; the current default is 0.44 (crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:785), so the production clone fraction is now ~56%, not 90.2%. The line is stale as a description of the current substrate. The fix is to update the prose citing the values already stored — mutational_neighborhood.evolved.per_seed[].pooled_births.zero_event_births (1300/2400) and drift_depth.readings[].opportunities.zero_event_fraction (0.5588 at depth 2,000) — not to add a SimStats field. Note the roadmap line presents 90.2% as dated evidence tied to a commit rather than a live claim, so this is a clarity refresh, not a correctness bug.

(b) DEFINITION COLLISION UNDER ONE KEY (real, confirmed). crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/recruitment.rs:282 counts attempted_events == 0 while crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/births.rs:117 counts applied_events == 0, and both serialize as "zero_event_births" into the same stored report (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:783 and :1112) — visible side by side at drift_depth.readings[].opportunities.zero_event_births vs drift_depth.readings[].births.zero_event_births. The two currently agree to within 0.02% because skips are ~0, so this is latent rather than active, but the shared key name is genuinely ambiguous and worth disambiguating if either definition is ever read as authoritative. This is a rename, not new telemetry.

The one thing genuinely absent — a clone count over the production birth stream itself (deterministic.per_seed[] carries births but no zero-event count, and SimStats has no such field) — carries no information beyond the config constant, because the gate is drawn per birth before any genome inspection and is therefore independent of population state.

title: The one production counter named for silent mutations is provably always zero and is still exported as if measured
missing: Production has no behavioral silent/changed/dead classification of births at all; mutation_events_applied_total_semantic_noop is a constant 0 and semantic_change always equals mutation_events_applied_total.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/mutation/types/mod.rs:321-324 — pub const fn semantic_category(self) -> MutationSemanticCategory { MutationSemanticCategory::SemanticChange } — no match arm, so every applied event classifies as SemanticChange; the counters are incremented from it at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:230-233 and via record_applied at crates/v3-core/src/mutation/types/mod.rs:613-628 (funnel.semantic_change). It is nonetheless exported live at crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:501-503, and a test at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:598-600 (inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests, opened at :124-125) uses semantic_change > 0 as a guard that can never be false.
why: Answers the production-births question head on: the silent/changed/dead fractions in the stored report come only from the offline battery over sampled genomes (mutational_neighborhood) and the drift walk — never from production births — and the single runtime counter that reads like the production equivalent measures nothing. A reader of SimStats or the live payload would take the constant for a measurement. A per-birth battery in production is deliberately NOT proposed: it would run the 48-scenario battery over ~1.16M births per goal run and blow the minutes-scale closure budget.
criterion: NONE
proposal: Delete mutation_events_applied_total_semantic_{noop,change} from SimStats, MutationSummary.applied_semantic_{noop,change}_events, MutationOperatorFunnel.semantic_change, MutationOperator::semantic_category(), and the two v3-server payload fields at state.rs:501-503; fix the always-true test guard at actions/mod.rs:598-600. The neighborhood battery and the drift walk remain the only silent/changed sources, and they are honest about their sample. AGENTS.md: backward compatibility is not a default goal.
corrections:
Four narrowings/strengthenings, none of which overturn the finding.

(a) The test guard is NOT a tautology. `crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:599-600` reads `result == ReproductionActionResult::Spawned && sim.stats.mutation_events_applied_total_semantic_change > 0`. Because semantic_change == mutation_events_applied_total identically, that conjunct is exactly `mutation_events_applied_total > 0`, which IS false whenever the single scheduled event is skipped — skips are common in production (T13.F01 closure recorded ~half of attempted events discarding an operator after selecting an inapplicable node). So it is a redundant alias reading as a behavioral filter, not an always-true guard; the fix is a rename to `mutation_events_applied_total > 0`, not repairing a broken assertion.

(b) The blast radius is undercounted. The finder named five sites; the actual export surface also includes `crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:202,452` (a SECOND live export the finder missed — the per-operator `MutationOperatorFunnel.semantic_change`, which for the same reason equals `applied` for every operator), `crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:87-88,229-234` (TickSampleEvent — this is why the constant is baked into stored sweep NDJSON under docs/progress/sweeps/), `crates/v3-server/src/transport/protocol.rs:75-76,259-262,574-575`, `view_assembler.rs:317-318`, `query/projection.rs:225-226`, and `frontend/src/types/protocol.ts:107-108,134-135` plus store tests. The live export range is state.rs:501-504, not 501-503.

(c) The field is spec-mandated, which sharpens "exported as if measured" beyond the finder's framing: `docs/reference/v3-evolution-observability-spec.md:56-57` lists both counters as required, :107-108 mandates the invariant `semantic_noop + semantic_change = applied_total`, and :168 declares `semantic_category` as "(`SemanticNoop` or `SemanticChange`, when applied)" — a two-way classification the code structurally cannot produce. `docs/reference/v3-mutation-spec.md:438-439` repeats the summary fields. Two tests assert the reconciliation invariant (`crates/v3-cli/tests/cli.rs:160-162`, `crates/v3-server/tests/server.rs:1485-1488`) and pass trivially because one term is a constant 0. Any deletion must therefore amend those two reference specs, not just code.

(d) "No classification at all" should read "no BEHAVIORAL classification". Production does carry a structural one — `mutation_{reachable,unreachable,executed,not_applicable}_target_total` — recording whether the mutated target sits on the executed path. That is the nearest production proxy and it measures something real; it is simply not a silent/changed/dead reading of the resulting birth, so the claim stands as narrowed.

(e) Weighting: this is not a newly discovered gap. `docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:70` already records it verbatim — "`mutation_events_applied_total_semantic_noop` | 0 of 4,513,532 (the counter classifies by operator category, not by measured behavior; it cannot see silence)" — in the note that drove the 2026-09-07 roadmap amendment (T11.F16/F17). The finder's diagnosis is correct and independently reproduced, but it re-derives a known, documented fact rather than surfacing an unknown one.

Three corrections; the gap stands but the finder's framing is off in ways that change the fix. (1) The test-guard claim is wrong, not overstated. crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:598-600 guards on sim.stats.mutation_events_applied_total_semantic_change > 0; since that equals mutation_events_applied_total, the guard is "at least one mutation event applied to this sim" — a real filter that is routinely false at 0.55 requested events per birth (the loop retries seeds precisely because of it). It is MISNAMED, not vacuous; the fix is renaming it to mutation_events_applied_total > 0, not deleting it as dead code. (2) Layer and provenance. The finder labels this "runtime-absent"; more precisely the constant lives in (a) SimStats (stats.rs:207-210, whose doc comment "Applied events classified as semantic-noop" is the actual misleading text) and (c) the live payload, and it also reaches stored CLI sweep artifacts via crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:87-88,229-234 — but it never enters (b), the stored closure goal report: the only "semantic" token in docs/progress/features/*.json is the word "semantics" from feature slugs. And it was not designed dead: commit 6fd21072 (T11.F15) collapsed the former `TopologyRewriteNodeId => SemanticNoop` arm when it removed that operator, so this is dead-by-side-effect of a closed feature. Even before that it was an operator-label classifier over exactly one operator — never a behavioral per-birth classification — so "the one production counter named for silent mutations" was never the production equivalent of the battery's silent/changed/dead. (3) The deletion surface is materially larger than proposed and includes a normative spec that must be amended in the same change: docs/reference/v3-evolution-observability-spec.md:56-57 (both counters on the required list), :107-108 (the required invariant noop + change = applied), and :168 (a required per-event semantic_category field that is not implemented as an event field at all); plus crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:87-88,229-234, crates/v3-server/src/transport/protocol.rs:75-76,259-262,574-575, view_assembler.rs:317-318, query/projection.rs:225-226, and the contract tests crates/v3-cli/tests/cli.rs:153-160 and crates/v3-server/tests/server.rs:367-372,1485-1486, which assert the invariant the spec requires. Minor nuance, not a refutation: production does carry a carrier-outcome classification (MutationValueTotals helpful/neutral/detrimental with confidence buckets), but that is an outcome/value reading, not a behavioral silent/changed/dead classification of births, so the finder's core "no behavioral classification of production births" holds.

Upheld but reclassify as layer (a)/(c) housekeeping, not a measurement gap, and fix four points.

1. Priority. This touches nothing in layer (b): no stored closure report, no goal epoch, no docs/progress.md row, no criterion. It should not compete with real stored-report gaps.

2. "A guard that can never be false" is wrong. At `crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:598-600`, `semantic_change > 0` is exactly equivalent to `mutation_events_applied_total > 0`, which CAN be false — a drawn mutation event can be skipped. The 10,000-seed loop with the `observed` flag and the sibling test `skipped_only_mutation_event_does_not_trigger_phenotype_mutation` both exist because skips occur. The guard is redundant, not vacuous; it needs a mechanical substitution to `mutation_events_applied_total > 0`, not a "fix".

3. "Exported as if measured" overstates, and the provenance is not a stub. `semantic_category()` is a static per-operator property that once had a real match arm — `TopologyRewriteNodeId => SemanticNoop` — deleted with that operator by T11.F15 (commit 6fd21072, 2026-09-06); the track records the retirement at `docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:104` ("`RewriteNodeId` (14.8% of mesh supply) is a semantic no-op ... `RewriteNodeId` retired"). `TopologyRewriteNodeId` now appears nowhere in the tree. So noop == 0 is a TRUE statement about today's operator set, not a broken reading; the real defect is that a `const fn` with no match makes the field structurally incapable of ever being non-zero. The track also already guards the misreading the finder worries about, at `:90`: "an operator-labeled semantic-change counter is not behavioral novelty."

4. Blast radius is 23 files, not "the two v3-server payload fields". Beyond the cited sites it includes the WebSocket protocol type `frontend/src/types/protocol.ts:107-108,134-135`, `crates/v3-server/src/transport/protocol.rs:75-76,259-262,574-575`, `view_assembler.rs:317-318`, `query/projection.rs:225-226`, the CLI per-tick `TickSampleEvent` at `crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:87-88,229-234` (a consumer the finder omitted entirely), and reconciliation assertions at `crates/v3-cli/tests/cli.rs:153-160` and `crates/v3-server/tests/server.rs:367-372,1485-1486`. Mitigating: no frontend component renders the value — only type declarations and test fixtures — so the change is mechanical.

Net: a constant-by-construction counter arguably already fails AGENTS.md's "telemetry must derive from applied simulation behavior", so removal moves toward compliance rather than away from it.

title: No total (junk-included) structure census of the living population
missing: Per-creature `cached_genome_size` (total `genome_size()` units, junk included) and `genome.nodes.len()`, pooled over the final living population. The stored report pools only `functional_complexity` (reachable-and-live-code-only) into `reachable_structure_size_distribution`.
evidence: crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1893-1896 builds `complexities` from `functional_complexity(&c.genome)` alone over `sim.creatures.values()`; bench.rs:2419 feeds that single vector to `reachable_structure_size_distribution`. `grep -c genome_size docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json` = 0 (also 0 in the gate report). The only `total_node_count` keys in that JSON are `goal_indicators.cases[].mutational_neighborhood.{founder,evolved.per_seed[].sampled_genomes[]}.mesh_execution` (12 sampled genomes per case out of 8,818/7,715/21,818) and `cases[].drift_depth.readings[].mean_total_nodes`. crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/drift.rs:1 declares the walk "Mutation-only lineage depth observations, isolated from ecological state" (no selection, no energy) and drift.rs:53 restricts its totals to "Integer totals over whole lineages, never VM instructions or graph internals" — i.e. mesh nodes, never `genome_size()` units.
why: Junk accumulation is total-minus-reachable. Today total is readable only on an unselected, energy-free walk and on 12 genomes per case, so no closure can answer whether T03.F08's carrying charge is actually shrinking carried structure under selection. The quantity the charge is levied on (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:139-141, `genome_carry_cost_per_unit * genome_size`, 1e-4 per unit) appears in no stored report anywhere. The pooled reachable median has fallen from the goal-v1 baseline's 97 to 87 and the max from 798 to 478, and nothing says whether junk fell with it or grew underneath it.
criterion: Executed mesh node counts, route variation with input, hop-cap hits, and total and reachable node counts are recorded at every closure, and every mesh-layer claim states the generation depth it was read at. (open T11 track criterion, docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:31)
proposal: In the loop that already builds `complexities` (bench.rs:1893), also pool `c.cached_genome_size`, `c.genome.nodes.len()`, and a per-`backend_def` node tally. Emit `total_structure_size_distribution` and `mesh_node_count_distribution` through the existing `structure_size_distribution()` helper, plus `mesh_nodes_total_by_backend` counts, beside the existing reachable distribution — per case and pooled, same shape. Counters over applied state only: no new run, no RNG draw, no execution change.
corrections: Claim stands for layer (b) but the finder's "why it matters" is wrong in four places. (1) The quantity is NOT only readable on the unselected walk and 12 sampled genomes: `structure_means` at crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:165-185 already computes mean `cached_genome_size` and mean `genome.nodes.len()` over the living, selected population and emits them as `mean_genome_size` / `mean_mesh_nodes` on every `tick_sample` of the v3-cli `run` NDJSON stream (tests crates/v3-cli/tests/cli.rs:214-240); v3-server also exposes per-creature `genome_size` at crates/v3-server/src/http/creature.rs:55,369. (2) "Appears in no stored report anywhere" is false: docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/cost.ndjson and control.ndjson store it — that paired long run was T03.F08's own closure evidence. The accurate statement is that no RECURRING closure report carries it, so no later closure can re-read it. (3) The "median 97 -> 87, max 798 -> 478" trend framing is unsound: intermediate goal reports swing 71-114 median, and the T12.F04 baseline-world change re-based the reading — t12-f04-baseline-world-set-goal.json already reads exactly 87/478, so T13.F01 moved nothing. Keep only "junk-vs-reachable is unmeasurable at closure". (4) The cited T11 criterion (docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:31) asks for total and reachable MESH node counts at every closure, which `drift_depth.readings[].total_nodes` and battery `mesh_execution.total_node_count` already satisfy; it does not demand a live-population census in `genome_size()` units. The load-bearing motivation is T03.F08's carrying charge being levied on an unreported quantity — cite that, not T11:31. Layer nit: `cached_genome_size` lives in creature state (crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:176), not in SimStats, so the layer label is "runtime creature state with two existing consumers (v3-cli run stream, v3-server), not stored by bench". The fix is therefore cheaper than proposed — reuse `structure_means`' two sums in the bench.rs:1893 loop — and the proposed per-backend tally should extend the existing `MeshBackendCounts` type (today walk/battery only) rather than introduce a new one.

Two parts of the finding are wrong and must be narrowed.

(1) LAYER MISATTRIBUTION. The finder labels this "exists-in-a-or-c-not-stored." It is neither: `cached_genome_size` is per-creature state (crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:176, computed at :217), not a SimStats cumulative (a) or a `last_tick_*` field (c) — SimStats has zero genome-size hits. It also already exists in a fourth place the three-layer taxonomy does not name: the v3-cli run-stream emitter `structure_means` (crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:161-185) already computes mean `cached_genome_size` (junk included), mean `genome.nodes.len()`, and mean generation over the living population and emits them as `mean_genome_size` / `mean_mesh_nodes` / `mean_generation`. Corrected layer statement: exists in per-creature state and in the CLI run-stream emitter; absent from SimStats and from the stored closure report (b). This makes the fix cheaper than claimed, not more expensive — `structure_means` is the copy-paste precedent.

(2) "NO CLOSURE CAN ANSWER WHETHER T03.F08'S CHARGE IS SHRINKING CARRIED STRUCTURE" IS FALSE. The split was a recorded design decision, and T03.F08's own closure answered it. docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:51 assigns the goal profile to read the reachable distribution and "a long run under selection for total node count at depth" separately, "since the drift walk has no energy and cannot show a carrying cost." T03.F08 did exactly that: docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/cost.ndjson and control.ndjson are a paired 12,000-tick selected run carrying `mean_genome_size` (131.28 at tick 500, 142.01 at tick 1000 in the cost arm; 131.63 at tick 500 in the control arm) and `mean_mesh_nodes`. Likewise "total is readable only on an unselected, energy-free walk and on 12 genomes per case" is false.

NARROWED TRUE CLAIM: the total (junk-included) structure reading under selection exists but is a one-off sweep artifact tied to T03.F08's closure — means only, not a distribution, on its own horizon and config, not comparable to the goal profile's 87/478 reachable numbers. It is not repeated per closure and is not stored in docs/progress/features/*.json, so no later closure can track carried structure against the reachable distribution without re-running that sweep. That, not unmeasurability, is the gap, and the proposed pooling in bench.rs:1893 is the cheap fix for it.

FRAMING CONSTRAINT: docs/roadmaps/t01-experimental-science-and-causal-evaluation.md:71 records the decision to "use reachable size as one structural axis" because syntactic measures "can misclassify bloat." That bars presenting a `total_structure_size_distribution` as a complexity or cognition indicator; it does not bar recording total size to measure bloat. Any implementation must land it as a structural diagnostic beside the reachable distribution, not as a new complexity measure.

Narrowed claim. (a) Wrong criterion. t11:31 is real but t11:103 scopes it to "per sampled genome ... the total and reachable node counts, the executed node count over the battery, a route-variation flag ... hop-cap hits, and a knockout count", plus "the generation distribution of the final population". Its owner T11.F14 is CLOSED (t11:65), and that half is already in the stored report (total_node_count x6, reachable_node_count x12, mean_total_nodes x4). t11:31 does not ask for a pooled census of the living population, and the `genome_size()` half of the proposal has no cited criterion at all. Worse, `genome_size()` (crates/v3-core/src/creature/genome/mod.rs:265) sums nodes + input refs + targets + VM instructions + constants + graph internals — exactly the composite that t11:103 faults `functional_complexity` for being ("a composite ... so its median of about 100 says nothing about the mesh").
