Do not present it as satisfying a mesh node-count criterion. The correct justification is T03.F08's own verification clause at docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:51. (b) "No closure can answer" is overstated. The reading exists and was taken: crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:165-186 `structure_means`, and docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/cost.ndjson carries `mean_genome_size` and `mean_mesh_nodes` per tick sample from T03.F08's own closure run. The gap is that this never enters the bench goal report, so it is a one-off sweep rather than a per-closure reading. (c) Layer label is loose. This is neither SimStats (a) nor `last_tick_*` (c): it is per-creature applied state (state.rs:176) already folded by a v3-cli stream observer (lib.rs:165) but absent from bench.rs's stored report. (d) Trim the scope. Pool only what `structure_means` already computes — `cached_genome_size` and `genome.nodes.len()` over the final living population — in the existing bench.rs:1893 loop, emitted through the existing `structure_size_distribution()` helper beside `reachable_structure_size_distribution`. Drop `mesh_nodes_total_by_backend`: `"backends"` already appears 54 times in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json (drift `MeshTotals.backends`, T11.F18's per-backend measurement), so the tally is redundant. This is a two-field addition riding an existing feature's spec, not a new feature.

Narrowed claim: the stored CLOSURE REPORT (docs/progress/features/*.json) carries no junk-included structure census of the living population — only reachable-and-live `functional_complexity`. That is the whole of the verified gap. Four corrections to the finder's framing:

(1) "The quantity the charge is levied on appears in no stored report anywhere" is FALSE. `crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:162-186` (`structure_means`) already pools `cached_genome_size` and `genome.nodes.len()` over the living population into `TickSampleEvent` as `mean_genome_size` / `mean_mesh_nodes` / `mean_generation` (lib.rs:65-72, 188-196; pinned by `crates/v3-cli/tests/cli.rs:224-247` at founder 111 units / 2 nodes), and those readings ARE stored under docs/progress — `docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/{cost,control}.ndjson`, 24 tick_samples per arm.

(2) "No closure can answer whether T03.F08's carrying charge is actually shrinking carried structure under selection" is FALSE — that exact question was already answered under selection by the stored paired sweep: at tick 12,000 the cost arm reads mean_genome_size 386.5 / mean_mesh_nodes 10.13 against the control's 1,093.8 / 18.40, neither arm extinct. The real residual gap is narrower: the reading is not in the recurring closure report, so it is not taken per baseline world, not regression-tracked across closures, and is a mean only, with no distribution.

(3) The proposal re-litigates a recorded, reasoned decision. `docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f08-genome-size-maintenance-cost.md:40-43` makes "No ... goal-profile indicator" an explicit non-goal, choosing the three CLI `tick_sample` fields as "the only new instrument"; lines 373-375 give the reason: "The paired long run is the feature's structural reading: the goal profile at generation 50 cannot see a 3.5% charge, and the drift walk has no energy." The spec's own reconciled numbers support that — at generation ~48 the arms differ 183.191 vs 172.294 units (~6%), which a single closure reading at that depth cannot resolve as a selection effect. Any proposal to add this to the goal profile must answer that objection, not ignore it.

(4) The cited T11 criterion (docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:31) is misapplied: it asks for total and reachable MESH NODE counts at every closure, and those are recorded (mesh_execution.total_node_count, drift total_nodes); it never asks for `genome_size()` units, and never asks for a population census. It is at most thinly met (12 sampled genomes per case is not a population reading).

Layer label correction: `cached_genome_size` is per-creature applied state (`crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:176,217`) charged at `crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:136-142`, not a SimStats counter and not a `last_tick_*` field — it is in neither layer (a) nor (c) as defined; it is applied state plus an existing v3-cli run-stream helper. The proposal's cheapness claim survives and is in fact stronger (a pooling helper already exists in the same crate), but its value proposition should be restated as "make the existing means a standing per-closure, per-world, distributional reading" rather than "measure something unmeasurable today".

title: Founder structural baseline is computed inside the report builder and thrown away
missing: The founder genome's `functional_complexity` and `genome_size()` — the reference value the master criteria compare every later population distribution against. The founder half stores only `reachable_node_count` (a mesh-node count of 2).
evidence: crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:2156 calls `structural_companions(&subject)` and keeps only `.reachable_node_count`, discarding the `functional_complexity` that struct already carries (crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/companions.rs:15 and :89). The serialized founder half in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json has exactly the keys `births, generation, mesh_execution, operator_rows, reachable_node_count`. crates/v3-cli/tests/cli.rs:229 pins the founder's `mean_genome_size` at 111.0 today, while docs/roadmap.md:52 and docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:84 both compare against "the founder's 96".
why: docs/roadmap.md:52 makes "reachable structure with median 97, p75 124, and maximum 798 against the founder's 96" the baseline row the master criteria read every later closure against — but 96 is a hand-recorded constant no report re-reads, and it has already gone stale: docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:51 records "the founder's 96 (111 at the T03.F08 revision; the 96 is the depth note's reading from an earlier revision)". The same number 96 is used in one place as the founder's `genome_size()` and in another as the founder's reachable-structure baseline — two different quantities. Nothing in the pipeline can catch either the unit confusion or the next drift.
criterion: reachable structure with median 97, p75 124, and maximum 798 against the founder's 96. The master criteria compare later goal readings against this row. (docs/roadmap.md:52)
proposal: Add `functional_complexity` and `genome_size` to the founder half of `mutational_neighborhood` (both already computable from the `subject` genome at bench.rs:2145-2156; `functional_complexity` is literally already computed there). One extra row per report, recomputed from the pinned founder at every closure, so every later comparison cites a number the report itself carries.
corrections: The gap and the proposal stand; the finder's diagnosis of the constant is understated and should be restated. It is not "the same number 96 used as two different quantities". Measured at HEAD, 96 matches NEITHER quantity: founder genome_size()=111 and founder functional_complexity()=complexity()=63. Since reachable_structure_size_distribution is built from functional_complexity over live creatures (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1896), "reachable structure with median 97, p75 124, and maximum 798 against the founder's 96" (docs/roadmap.md:52, repeated at docs/roadmap.md:64 and docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:84) is stale for the very measure it governs, overstating the founder reference by ~52% and correspondingly understating the growth the master criteria read. The T03.F08 spec's explanation of the 96/111 gap as an earlier-revision genome_size reading (commit 085ef918, docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f08-genome-size-maintenance-cost.md "Notes for AI Agents": "the canonical V3Alpha1 founder is 111 genome_size() units (complexity 63) at this revision") therefore does not account for the roadmap.md:52 usage at all. Two consequences for the proposal: (1) adding the two founder fields to the report does not by itself correct those three doc lines — a documentation correction, or an explicit instruction to re-read the row from the next closure report, must ship with it; (2) the genome_size half is already partially pinned outside the report at crates/v3-cli/tests/cli.rs:229 (mean_genome_size 111.0 in the `run` tick_sample stream), whereas no test anywhere pins a founder functional_complexity value, so functional_complexity is the field with no regression coverage of any kind and is the higher-value half of the addition.

Two narrowings. (1) LAYER: the finder labeled this `exists-in-a-or-c-not-stored`, which is wrong. The founder's `functional_complexity` is in neither `SimStats` (a) nor any `last_tick_*` field (c) — it is computed inside the report builder itself (layer b) at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:2156 and discarded before serialization. That makes the fix cheaper than the finder's label implies: nothing has to cross a layer boundary, only two fields have to survive into `NeighborhoodFounderHalf`. (2) STALENESS: the finder argued staleness only by the `genome_size` proxy (the pinned 111.0 at crates/v3-cli/tests/cli.rs:229 versus the recorded 96). Measured at HEAD, the founder's `functional_complexity` is 63 and its `genome_size()` is 111. So the master-criteria row at docs/roadmap.md:52 is wrong in its OWN unit today — the reachable-structure baseline it compares median 97 / p75 124 / max 798 against should be 63, not 96 — and the t03 usage is wrong at 111. Neither hand-recorded 96 matches the founder in either unit, and no stored report carries either number for the pipeline to catch it. (Placement quibble, not a verdict change: the founder half is duplicated per case, three identical copies in the goal report, and `reachable_structure_size_distribution` exists both per-case and at the top level, so a founder reference row alongside the top-level distribution would be at least as natural as inside `mutational_neighborhood.founder`.) Note for the parent: `crates/v3-core/tests/tmp_founder_probe.rs` is an untracked leftover from a sibling agent's probe, timestamped 11:49; it is not mine and I left it in place.

Three narrowings. (a) Unit: functional_complexity is the field that actually matches the cited criterion, since reachable_structure_size_distribution is built from functional_complexity (bench.rs:1896 -> :2419). genome_size is a different quantity — T03.F08's charged unit, pinned at 111.0 by crates/v3-cli/tests/cli.rs:229 — cheap to add alongside, but it is not what "the founder's 96" should be compared against, and adding it does not close the separate, already-recorded absence of any population genome_size reading. (b) The defect is stronger than the claimed 96-vs-111 unit confusion: the founder's reachable-structure value measured today is 63, so the roadmap anchor is wrong in its own unit as well, not merely swapped with the other one. The likely history (T11.F04's neutral scaffold raises genome_size but not functional_complexity, fitting 96 -> 111 with functional_complexity unchanged at 63) suggests 96 may never have been the reachable-structure value at all, but I did not confirm that; state it as "matches neither of today's founder values" rather than asserting a specific drift. (c) Framing: docs/roadmap.md:34-37's Final Success Criteria compare later goal readings to the goal series' first reading, not to the founder; the founder number is anchor text inside that baseline row at :52. So this is a correctness repair of the report's reference row — one recomputed structural fact per report — not a value the master criteria mechanically consume, and the finder's "the reference value the master criteria compare every later population distribution against" overstates it.

title: No executed-node census of the living population, though every creature carries its own dispatch record
missing: `creature.graph_runtime.dispatch_record.executed_indices(creature.age, config.mutation.executed_window_ticks)` counted over the final living population. Every executed-node count in the stored report comes from the offline battery instead.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:26-58 defines `DispatchRecord` (one entry per mesh node holding the age it last dispatched; `executed_indices` is public) and it is populated every hop at crates/v3-core/src/runtime/mesh.rs:300. crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:213 reads exactly this record at every production birth (`ParentExecuted::Record(&parent.graph_runtime.dispatch_record, parent.age)`), resolved at `config.executed_window_ticks` = 100 (crates/v3-core/src/mutation/engine/mod.rs:102, crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:767+778). In the goal JSON, `executed_node_count` / `executed_nodes` appear only under `mutational_neighborhood.*.mesh_execution` (12 sampled genomes per case) and `drift_depth.readings[]` — both battery-derived; crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/operators.rs:167-169 comments that the battery's executed set is an "Observation stand-in for a live parent's dispatch record (T11.F17)".
why: T11.F17 changed production mutation targeting on the basis of this record, and the depth note's central structural claim (about 4 executed nodes inside a ~124-node genome) is re-read at every closure only on a synthetic walk and a 12-genome sample. Whether the live population's executed core grows, shrinks, or holds is unanswerable from any stored report, and the reading that is stored is a stand-in rather than applied simulation behavior.
criterion: Executed mesh node counts, route variation with input, hop-cap hits, and total and reachable node counts are recorded at every closure, and every mesh-layer claim states the generation depth it was read at. (open T11 track criterion, docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:31)
proposal: In the same final-population pass as the gap above, record `dispatch_record.executed_indices(creature.age, config.mutation.executed_window_ticks).len()` per creature and emit `executed_node_count_distribution` beside the reachable and total distributions, stamping the window value used. Requires threading the mutation config to the observation point; read-only, no RNG, no execution change.
corrections: Claim stands; four narrowings. (a) LAYER: the finder tags this "exists-in-a-or-c-not-stored", but DispatchRecord is per-creature runtime state (`creature.graph_runtime.dispatch_record`, state.rs:103), not a SimStats cumulative field (a) nor a `last_tick_*` field (c). The signal exists in the simulation but in NO telemetry layer. The "cheap fix" verdict survives anyway, for a different reason: bench.rs:1893 already walks `sim.creatures.values()` at exactly the right moment. (b) The proposal's "requires threading the mutation config to the observation point" is wrong — `sim` is in scope at bench.rs:1893 and `sim.config.mutation.executed_window_ticks` is directly reachable (cf. `sim.config.mutation.mutation_probability` at actions/mod.rs:687). The fix is simpler than proposed. (c) "beside the reachable and total distributions" — there is no live total distribution to sit beside; `total_node_count` is stored only per battery-sampled genome. Narrow to "beside the reachable distribution." (d) CRITERION FRAMING: the T11 criterion (docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:31) asks that executed mesh node counts be "recorded at every closure" — and they are, from the battery. So this is not criterion absence; it is a provenance failure against AGENTS.md's "Runtime-facing telemetry and state must derive from applied simulation behavior", plus the living population's executed-core size being unreadable from any stored report. Also correct "12 sampled genomes per case, not the population": the 12 evolved genomes ARE drawn from the live population — it is only their executed set that is a battery replay rather than each creature's own record.

The gap is real but overstated in four places, and one caveat is missing. (1) "Requires threading the mutation config to the observation point" is false — `crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1893` already iterates `sim.creatures.values()` and `sim.config.mutation.executed_window_ticks` is in scope on the same `sim`; zero plumbing. (2) "beside the reachable and total distributions" — only one structural distribution is stored, and `reachable_structure_size_distribution` is populated from `functional_complexity`, a composite (node count plus targets, live VM slice, constants, input references, per `docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:103`), not a reachable-node count; no total-node distribution exists at all. Say "beside the existing composite structure-size distribution". (3) The cited T11 criterion (`docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:31`) is met in letter — executed mesh node counts ARE recorded at every closure. The gap is provenance (battery re-execution vs. applied dispatches) and coverage (36 sampled genomes plus a synthetic drift walk vs. the whole living population), not absence. (4) "A stand-in rather than applied simulation behavior" overreaches: the program's own recorded position is that the battery counts are the right reading (`docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:249`: the reachable and executed counts "are the right readings for 'how much brain is in use,' and the T11.F14 battery already produces them"), so the battery is a deliberate choice, not an oversight. The same note concedes at :256 that "the world's inputs are not the battery's", so the correct framing is a second, applied-behavior reading the report does not have, not a correction of a wrong one. Missing caveat: `executed_indices(age, window)` filters `age - last < window && last <= age`, so a creature younger than 100 ticks counts every dispatch of its life and has simply seen fewer inputs than a 100-tick-old one. The distribution would therefore track the population's age structure (the birth pulse) as much as the executed core, so the proposal must stamp the age distribution or report the count for `age >= executed_window_ticks` separately.

Four narrowings, none fatal. (1) The cited criterion is already literally satisfied — executed mesh node counts ARE recorded at every closure, and the mutational_neighborhood half carries evolved.per_seed[].generation_distribution, so the depth stamp the criterion demands is present. The criterion is a fit for this signal, not a requirement of it; the proposal must not be justified as closing an unmet criterion. (2) The defensible justification is narrower and directly citable: production mutation targeting reads parent.graph_runtime.dispatch_record at every birth (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:213), and no stored closure reading ever reads that record — the newest goal report stamps its executed set as battery-derived. The T11 track itself flags the divergence at docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:106, which notes the T11.F17 counterfactual "used 1.0 with a battery-derived executed set; production uses the creature's own ticks, whose inputs differ from the battery's" — so the roadmap already records that these are different quantities and nothing measures the production one. Do not lean on the AGENTS.md "applied simulation behavior" line; the battery is explicitly self-labeled observation, so that framing is arguable while the reproduction.rs:213 asymmetry is not. (3) "Requires threading the mutation config to the observation point" is overstated — sim is already in scope at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1893-1897, where reachable_structure_size_distribution is built from sim.creatures.values(), so sim.config.mutation.executed_window_ticks is directly available and no threading is needed. (4) Add an interpretive caveat the proposal omits: executed_indices is age-windowed, so creatures younger than the 100-tick window structurally under-report and the distribution mixes them with mature creatures; the emitted field must stamp the window and report or filter on age to be readable. Nearest partial owner for attribution: T11.F13's deferred paired long run (same roadmap file, line 106) plans a depth census including "contributing executed nodes", but names the depth note's battery method (docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:93), not the dispatch record, and is a rate-characterization feature rather than a telemetry one.

title: The stored report carries no mutation counters from the production run at all
missing: SimStats' applied mutation totals for the actual goal run — at minimum `mutation_events_applied_total_by_operator` for the structure-changing topology operators (AddNode, RemoveNode, CopyNode, SpliceNode) and the `mutation_{executed,reachable,unreachable,not_applicable}_target_total` split.
evidence: `grep -c` on both docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json and the gate report returns 0 for each of `mutation_events_applied_total`, `mutation_executed_target`, `mutation_reachable_target`, `semantic_noop`, `mutation_outcome_summary`. The fields exist at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:206, 262, 264, 267, 269. crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:195-230 already serializes them on the `v3-cli run` NDJSON tick_sample stream. `WorldTracking::observe` (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1359-1380) is the existing hook that copies SimStats counters into `cases[]`, and it copies move and eat counters only.
why: Every mutation number in the stored report is produced by an offline battery or an unselected drift walk on their own RNG streams — none of it is what the production run actually did. Nothing records how much structure the goal run's mutation engine added or removed, nor whether T11.F17's executed-target bias fired in production. The structure census has a partial stock term and no flow term.
criterion: Runtime-facing telemetry and state must derive from applied simulation behavior; backward compatibility is not a default goal. (AGENTS.md:11)
proposal: Extend `WorldTracking::observe` to copy the four target-classification totals and the applied-by-operator counts for the topology operators out of `sim.stats` into each case, exactly as it already copies `move_actions_blocked_total_by_cause`. Raw counters only; no derived fractions beyond the per-case shape that already exists.
corrections:
Three narrowings, none of which reverse the verdict.

(1) The finder's evidence sentence "crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:195-230 already serializes them" is half wrong. lib.rs:195-235 serializes mutation_events_{attempted,applied,skipped}_total, ..._by_domain, ..._by_operator, and mutation_events_applied_total_semantic_{noop,change} on the `v3-cli run` NDJSON tick_sample stream — but NOT the four-way target split. `mutation_{reachable,unreachable,executed,not_applicable}_target_total` appear on no v3-cli stream at all; their only non-SimStats exposure is the live server at crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:506-509. So the applied-by-operator half of the ask has a ready v3-cli precedent; the target-split half does not, and is layer (c) only. The `exists-in-a-or-c-not-stored` label remains correct.

(2) Worth stating explicitly because it is a grep trap that cuts the finder's way: the stored report DOES contain the key names `executed_target_events`, `reachable_target_events`, `unreachable_target_events` and `executed_target_fraction` under `cases[].drift_depth.readings[].opportunities`. These are NOT production. They come from `recruitment::Opportunities::record` (crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/recruitment.rs:280-300) pooled over `drift::observe(&founder, battery, ...)`, and `compute_drift_depth` (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1011-1023) starts from `founder_genome(FounderProfile::V3Alpha1)` with its own `walk_seed_formula` (WALK_SEED_BASE + lineage_index) and `birth_seed_formula` — no `Simulation` is passed in. Same for `mutational_neighborhood`, whose trials are re-run offline under `snapshot_seed`/`sequence_seed`. The finder did not confuse these; anyone re-checking the claim by name-grep alone would.

(3) Scope note: production `mutation_events_applied_total` is not absent from the repo — it appears in the ad-hoc `v3-cli run` NDJSON at docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/{cost,control}.ndjson. The claim is correctly scoped to the stored closure report, so this refutes nothing, but "not stored" should not be read as "never captured anywhere."

Narrower, corrected claim: (1) No criterion mandates goal-run mutation counters — the case rests on provenance and zero cost, not on a requirement. AGENTS.md:11 is a constraint on how telemetry is derived, not an instruction to store a new signal, and the harness readings do derive from applied behavior (of the battery/drift sim). The T13 track is not a mandate either: its F01 scope note explicitly places the new cohort tracking "in the observation harness, not an unbounded production genealogy," and T13.F01 delivered per-operator attempted/applied/skipped tallies that way — `cases[].mutational_neighborhood.*.operator_rows[].tally` carries {trials, applied, skipped, silent, changed, dead} per operator, and `drift_depth.readings[].births` carries the same shape. So file this as an unfilled cheap slot, not unfinished T13.F01 scope; T13.F03 (Mutation Target Applicability, open) is the natural owner since its whole premise is per-operator applicability. (2) The finder's "nothing records whether T11.F17's executed-target bias fired in production" is if anything understated for the stored layer but should be stated precisely: `mutation_executed_target_total` appears in zero files under docs/ — not in docs/progress/readings/t11-f04*.md, t11-f18*.md, t13-f01*.md, nor any feature JSON. (3) The stored report is not devoid of production flow: per_seed carries production births, vm_steps, mesh_hops, plasticity_updates, and births_per_100_ticks is production-derived. The specifically missing flow term is mutation. (4) Operator names are TopologyAddNode / TopologyRemoveNode / TopologyCopyNode / TopologySpliceNode (crates/v3-core/src/mutation/types/mod.rs:141-151); the enum has ~40 variants. (5) Restricting the copy to four topology operators is an arbitrary cut — serializing the whole `mutation_events_applied_total_by_operator` map (plus attempted, and the four target totals) is simpler, is what lib.rs:195-235 already does, and adds ~40 integer keys per case to a report that already carries thousands of operator rows.

The gap and the proposal stand; one evidence line is overstated. The finder says crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:195-230 "already serializes them" for both the by-operator applied counts and the four target-classification totals. It serializes only the former group: `mutation_events_{attempted,applied,skipped}_total`, `..._by_domain`, `..._by_operator`, and `mutation_events_applied_total_semantic_{noop,change}`. The four target-classification totals (`mutation_{reachable,unreachable,executed,not_applicable}_target_total`, crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:262-269) appear NOWHERE in v3-cli — the `reachable_target_events`/`executed_target_events` hits at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:789-792 and 892-896 are the drift walk's pooled `MutationSummary` tallies, not SimStats. So "the NDJSON stream already carries the shape" is true for the by-operator map and false for the target split; the latter would be a first-time serialization (still a trivial u64 copy from `sim.stats`). Two smaller notes: the operator variants are named `MutationOperator::Topology{AddNode,RemoveNode,CopyNode,SpliceNode}` (crates/v3-core/src/mutation/engine/mod.rs:623-633), and cherry-picking four of them is unnecessary — copying the whole `mutation_events_applied_total_by_operator` map keeps the report consistent with the existing NDJSON shape, provided keys are emitted in sorted order so the closure's second-run byte match holds.

title: Nothing counts which backend a newly created mesh node received
missing: A count of applied node-creating events by the backend the new node was given (Graph vs VM). SimStats has no backend-keyed counter of any kind.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/mutation/topology/birth.rs:30 — every new detour node draws `rng.gen_bool(0.5)` between `blank_graph_backend(config)` and `minimal_vm_backend()`, in production, at every AddNode/SpliceNode application (crates/v3-core/src/mutation/topology/mod.rs:155-157). `grep -n backend crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs` returns no matches. The only `backends` keys in the goal JSON are standing censuses — `cases[].drift_depth.readings[].backends` and `mutational_neighborhood.*.mesh_execution.backends` — which conflate creation with retention.
why: The T11.F18 criterion asserts equal creation probability measured by backend, but the only stored evidence is standing composition on an unselected walk plus 12 sampled genomes. At drift depth 2,000 the walk stands at graph total 3,723 / executed 102 / contributing 2 against vm total 4,244 / executed 108 / contributing 31; nothing separates a creation asymmetry from differential loss, and under selection plus the T03.F08 carrying cost the question is entirely unmeasured.
criterion: New mesh detours can be either Graph or VM with equal creation probability, preserve the existing decision path and state effects at insertion, and are measured separately by backend for creation, execution, and behavioral contribution. (T11.F18, docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:35)
proposal: One SimStats counter, `mesh_nodes_created_total_by_backend` (two keys), incremented where the backend is drawn in `birth::detour`, carried into `cases[]` by `WorldTracking::observe` alongside the other production counters. Applied behavior, two integers, no derived score.
refutations: The stored goal report already counts new mesh nodes by the backend they were created with, so "nothing counts which backend a newly created mesh node received" is false as of T13.F01 (closed today on main at e19eac83). Owner: T13.F01 — Module Recruitment Observability, docs/roadmaps/t13-neutral-module-recruitment.md:27, CLOSED ([x]) and SCHEDULED in roadmap.md:45's priority list; its F01 scope (t13-...:44) explicitly says "Record actual mutation attempts, applicable targets, applied edits and local failures by backend/operator, plus cohort transitions for newly introduced modules." This is a stronger refutation than an unscheduled owner: the field is not merely planned, it is shipped and populated. Code: crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/recruitment.rs:35-56 defines `ModuleBackend` with the doc comment "The backend a module carries when it is created", built via `From<&BackendDef>`; recruitment.rs:757-759 bins every module's cohort facts into `reading.graph` / `reading.vm` by that field; recruitment.rs:457-458 holds the two CohortCounts; the module is registered at creation (recruitment.rs:524, :637) with the provenance rule that distinguishes a new node from a CopyNode copy. Emission: crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:821 `module_recruitment`, reaching the JSON at `deterministic.goal_indicators.cases[].drift_depth.readings[].recruitment.{graph,vm}`. The finder's central worry — that standing censuses "conflate creation with retention" — is resolved by this block, which reports created / present / deleted / contributing separately per backend at five depths. Measured in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json, Orchards in grassland at depth 2000: graph created 3903, present 3686, deleted 217, contributing 2; vm created 4415, present 4207, deleted 208, contributing 27 (Canyon country and Confluence carry the same shape). The finder cited only `readings[].backends` and `mesh_execution.backends` and missed the sibling `recruitment` key added by the same feature. Its proposal (a SimStats counter carried into cases[] by WorldTracking::observe) would duplicate a reading that exists, and duplicating it in production genealogy is explicitly out of scope per t13-neutral-module-recruitment.md:45: "New cohort tracking belongs in the observation harness, not an unbounded production genealogy."

The signal IS stored, under a name the finder missed, in the exact JSON object the finder quoted from. The finder's numbers (graph total 3,723 / executed 102 / contributing 2; vm total 4,244 / executed 108 / contributing 31) are `cases[0].drift_depth.readings[-1].backends` in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json. The sibling key `recruitment` in that same reading holds `graph: {created 3903, deleted 217, present 3686}` and `vm: {created 4415, deleted 208, present 4207}`. That is a backend-keyed creation count, stored in layer (b), sitting one key away from the census the finder called the "only" evidence.

Source confirms it is a creation counter, not a census: crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/recruitment.rs:35-56 defines `ModuleBackend` as "The backend a module carries when it is created", derived via `From<&BackendDef>`; :100-101 stamps `created_depth` and `backend` onto each `Module` at creation; :757-759 splits readings by `module.backend` into `reading.graph` / `reading.vm`; :365-382 documents and maintains the invariant `created == deleted + present`.

This defeats the claim's central "why it matters": "nothing separates a creation asymmetry from differential loss" is false — created/deleted/present is exactly that separation, and it answers the question in the finder's favorite direction, since deletions are near-equal (217 graph vs 208 vm) so the standing-census gap is a creation-count difference, not differential loss. The claim's title ("Nothing counts which backend a newly created mesh node received") is therefore wrong as stated.

The walk is not a parallel code path: crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/drift.rs:144 applies mutations through the production `MutationEngine::apply_mutations_with_food_type_count`, the same engine that reaches crates/v3-core/src/mutation/topology/mod.rs:155-157 -> `birth::detour` and its `rng.gen_bool(0.5)` at crates/v3-core/src/mutation/topology/birth.rs:30. The walk exercises the identical creation draw the finder wants counted.

Likely cause of the error: the finder read the T11.F18 goal report (docs/progress/features/t11-f18-backend-neutral-mesh-node-growth-goal.json), which does have only the census. The `recruitment` block was added by T13.F01, closed today at e19eac83.

Only the narrow layer-(a) statement survives — `grep -n -i backend crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs` returns nothing, so SimStats has no backend-keyed counter — but the finder's own proposal is the wrong fix for the one real residual (see correction).

The criterion is quoted correctly (docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:35) but the finder's central evidence sentence is false, and the need is attributed to a criterion that is already closed.

1) Creation BY BACKEND was measured, by design, and is not "only standing composition." The T11.F18 spec anticipated exactly this objection: docs/specs/roadmap/t11-f18-backend-neutral-mesh-node-growth.md:103 "Extant totals are not creation counts," and :105 "For creation evidence, add one ignored release characterization beside the existing topology/battery tests, using production `TopologyMutator::apply`." That was delivered: crates/v3-core/src/mutation/topology/f18_tests.rs:311 `t11_f18_paired_growth_characterization` applies 200 production `TopologyMutator::apply` events per growth operator to the unchanged V3Alpha1 founder (seeds 20260908+trial) and tallies `created_graph`/`created_vm` from the actual `backend_def` of the new node, alongside per-backend execution, contribution, and parent-signature equality. Results are recorded in the spec at :218-228 — AddNode 91/109, SpliceNode 91/109, AddRouteTarget 103/97 — and the feature's own success criterion at :322 is checked: "Closure evidence separates backend creation, execution and contribution at named depths." The finder's claim that "the only stored evidence is standing composition on an unselected walk plus 12 sampled genomes" ignores this, and its own operator list undercounts (it names AddNode/SpliceNode only; AddRouteTarget also routes through `birth::detour` — track line 81, and the test's GROWTH set).

2) The criterion is closed ([x], T11.F18) and the question the finder actually poses is a retention question owned by open features, not a creation-probability question. T11.F18's contract explicitly settled it: "Equal creation odds do not require equal backend counts in surviving creatures" (track line 82; spec :276). Separating creation from differential loss under selection plus the T03.F08 carrying cost is T13's scope — T13.F02 ("separating lineage variation, dormant preparation and selection from mere growth") and T13.F06 ("discovered and retained... including the cost of carrying it"), docs/roadmaps/t13-neutral-module-recruitment.md:26-34 — and docs/roadmap.md:48 states T13 "does not reopen T11.F18, alter its recorded exception." If that work needs a created-by-backend counter it adds one wired to its own indicator under the same-feature rule; adding it now under T11.F18's name is misattribution plus speculative telemetry against the standing KISS/basic-tracking preference.

3) Supporting: crates/v3-core/src/mutation/topology/birth.rs:30 draws `rng.gen_bool(0.5)` unconditionally, independent of source backend and site, so a production counter would re-measure a source constant every run rather than reveal anything the constructor-level characterization does not already fix.

Residual bite, and why it still does not carry: the characterization test asserts parent-signature equality and zero contribution but does not assert the created split, and it is `#[ignore]`, so nothing automated guards the 0.5. That is a test-assertion concern about a source literal, not a telemetry gap — and a stored counter would not guard it either without a threshold check, which is precisely the verify-stamp machinery the user rejected as overengineered (2026-09-07).
corrections: Not a reinstatement of the gap, only the surviving fragment: SimStats itself has no backend-keyed counter (confirmed — `grep -n backend crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs` is empty), so backend-keyed creation is read on the unselected drift walk in the observation harness rather than in the selected production ecology run. That fragment does not support the proposed feature: creation probability is a property of the mutation operator at crates/v3-core/src/mutation/topology/birth.rs:30 and is unaffected by selection, so the drift-walk reading answers the T11.F18 criterion directly; the selection-and-carrying-cost question the finder raises is retention, which T13.F02 (open, scheduled at roadmap.md:45, scope "Retain live/dead parent status, module count, costs and backend-specific exposure") and T13.F06 already own.

Narrow residual that survives, with a different fix than proposed: the stored per-backend `created` counts pool `New` and `Copy` provenance (crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/recruitment.rs:455 — "`new` + `copy` modules created at or before this checkpoint, pooled"). Copy-provenance modules inherit their backend from a pre-existing node rather than drawing it, so the pooled 3903/4415 split cannot test the `gen_bool(0.5)` coin in isolation and is not evidence against it. The T11.F18 criterion's "measured separately by backend for creation" is met in form but not sharp enough to isolate the draw.

The fix is to split the existing recruitment cohort ladder by `Provenance` — already tracked per `Module` at recruitment.rs:66-70 — in the drift-depth walk reading, reporting `created` as new-vs-copy within each backend. No SimStats change, no new run, no new walk.

Reject the finder's proposed `mesh_nodes_created_total_by_backend` SimStats counter: the walk already exercises the identical `birth::detour` path, and creation is a fair coin drawn before any fitness evaluation, so it is selection-independent by construction. A live-population count under selection and the T03.F08 carrying cost would return ~50/50 regardless of what selection does, adding no information over the walk while spending runtime and report budget.

title: The 20-checkpoint within-run series carries no structure reading
missing: Mean total `genome_size()` units and mean mesh node count at each of the 20 persistence checkpoints. The series carries population, mean_energy, births_total and the world/action counters only, so structure is read once, at the final tick.
evidence: crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1779-1785 builds `PersistenceSample { tick, population, mean_energy, births_total, tracking }`; the stored `population_persistence.per_seed[].samples[]` keys are exactly those plus WorldTracking's move/eat/food keys. The T03.F08 evidence for carried structure over time had to be produced outside the report by a hand-run 12,000-tick sweep (docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/run.sh; its cost.ndjson samples carry `mean_genome_size` and `mean_mesh_nodes`, emitted by crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:70-78 on the `v3-cli run` stream — a code path the closure report never uses).
why: A single final-tick distribution cannot say whether carried structure is growing or shrinking during a run, which is exactly the reading T03.F08's verification asks for. Today obtaining it means re-running a separate manual sweep at every closure that wants it, so in practice no closure reads it.
criterion: Verification runs `cargo test -p v3-core --test viability` first, re-reads persistence against the T11.F04 sweeps, and reads the goal profile's reachable-structure distribution and, since the drift walk has no energy and cannot show a carrying cost, a long run under selection for total node count at depth against the depth note's 0.06 nodes per generation. (docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:51)
proposal: Add one lazy closure alongside the existing `mean_energy` closure at bench.rs:1875-1884 returning mean `cached_genome_size` and mean `genome.nodes.len()`, stored on `PersistenceSample`. Same O(population)-at-20-checkpoints pattern `mean_energy` already uses; two numbers per sample, no derived index.
refutations: The cited criterion (docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:51) is real and quoted verbatim, but it does not require this signal in the stored closure report. Read whole, it explicitly splits the reading in two: "reads the goal profile's reachable-structure distribution and, since the drift walk has no energy and cannot show a carrying cost, a long run under selection for total node count at depth against the depth note's 0.06 nodes per generation." The separate long run is prescribed precisely because a short reading cannot show a carrying cost. That criterion was discharged: docs/progress.md:66 records T03.F08's closure (2026-09-07, beee4c05) with the exact trajectory readings the finder says no closure obtains — paired 12,000-tick run, cost arm mean genome size 386.54 in 10.13 mesh nodes at generation 177.3 vs control 1,093.84 in 18.40 nodes at generation 301.3, node slope 0.045824 vs 0.054430 against the 0.0595 drift reference. The finder's "in practice no closure reads it" is false. The proposal also cannot satisfy the criterion it cites: the goal profile runs 3 seeds x 2,000 ticks sampling every 100 (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1750) and reaches median generation ~49-52 (max 62) in the newest report, while the cited benchmark is a per-generation rate from a 281,405-tick run at median generation 1,990 (docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:18) and T03.F08's own run needed generations 177-301; the proposed series has no control arm (the sweep was paired against rate 0.0) and adds no per-checkpoint generation depth, so it yields neither a nodes-per-generation slope nor a cost-vs-control difference. Finally there is no open consumer: T03.F08 is closed ([x]), mean_genome_size/mean_mesh_nodes appear nowhere in docs/roadmaps/, docs/roadmap.md or docs/workflow.md, docs/roadmap.md has zero hits for genome size or carried structure, and T11.F13 (docs/roadmaps/t11-neural-substrate-evolvability.md:102), the forward consumer of the junk bound, predeclares its own rates, seeds, horizon and compute budget for its arms rather than reading the closure profile. Cost is not the objection (cached_genome_size is O(1) per creature); the objection is that no criterion, open or discharged, asks the stored report to carry it, making this confirmatory apparatus against the standing basic-tracking-plus-perf-regression preference. The layer fact itself is accurate: crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs TickSampleEvent emits mean_genome_size/mean_mesh_nodes on the run stream and PersistenceSample at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1779 does not store them.
corrections: Three narrowings. (a) LAYER: the finder's tag `exists-in-a-or-c-not-stored` is wrong. The signal is in neither (a) nor (c) — SimStats has no genome-size or node-count field and no `last_tick_*` structure field. It is derivable from creature state (`CreatureState.cached_genome_size`, crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:176, and `genome.nodes.len()`) and is aggregated only by `structure_means` for the `v3-cli run` stream (crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:189). Correct tag: derivable-from-state, emitted only on the `run` stream. (b) SCOPE: "structure is read once, at the final tick" understates the absence. For the live population, total `genome_size()` units — the exact quantity T03.F08 charges at 1e-4 — and total mesh node count are absent at EVERY tick, final tick included; the final-tick reading (bench.rs:1893-1897, `functional_complexity`) yields `reachable_structure_size_distribution`, a REACHABLE node count only. Total node counts appear only over the mutational-neighborhood's sampled evolved genomes (`evolved_sample_size` = 12 per seed in the t13-f01 goal run) and the drift walk's 5 checkpoints, neither of which is the population under selection. (c) WHAT THE FIX BUYS: the 20-checkpoint series would supply the within-run-trend half of the cited criterion, not the "at depth against the depth note's 0.06 nodes per generation" half — the closure horizon is 2,000 ticks (the T03.F08 sweep read mean_generation 9.4 at tick 500), and generation is never read on the live population at all. The 12,000-tick hand sweep (docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/run.sh:16) is not replaced by this proposal.

Three narrowings to the finder's framing; the gap itself stands.

1. LAYER MISLABEL. The finder tags this "exists-in-a-or-c-not-stored," but under the established taxonomy the quantity is in NEITHER (a) nor (c): `mean_genome_size` / `mean_mesh_nodes` are not SimStats fields and not `last_tick_*` fields. They live in per-creature runtime state (`cached_genome_size`, `genome.nodes.len()`) and are aggregated only by `structure_means(sim)` at crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:189, emitted on `TickSampleEvent` (crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:70-78) over the `v3-cli run` NDJSON path — a fourth surface the closure report never uses. Correct layer: "exists in per-creature runtime state and the CLI run stream, not stored in (b)." This makes the fix CHEAPER, not weaker: `structure_means` already exists and returns `(mean_genome_size, mean_mesh_nodes, mean_generation)`, so the proposal can reuse it rather than write a new closure.

2. "IN PRACTICE NO CLOSURE READS IT" IS OVERSTATED. T03.F08's closure did read it — out-of-report, via the manual sweep at docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/ (run.sh, cost.ndjson, control.ndjson all present on disk). The accurate claim is that obtaining the reading requires a separate hand-run sweep outside the closure report, which has been done exactly once.

3. THE CITED CRITERION IS FROM A CLOSED FEATURE. docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:51 is T03.F08's verification clause, and T03.F08 is checked closed (t03:37, closed on main at beee4c05). That criterion is already satisfied, so it justifies the reading historically, not prospectively. The forward-looking case rests on the scheduled adjacent features that will want carried structure over time under selection — T13.F06 (carrying cost of recruited tissue) and T11.F13 (junk-bound arms) — neither of which owns this series today.

title: Per-tick cognition energy (VM, graph, priority bids) is computed every tick and thrown away
missing: Cumulative f64 sums of the three energy quantities TickComputeStats already accumulates each tick: vm_sum, graph_sum, priority_bid_sum. Only per-tick means survive (last_tick_compute_vm_mean / _graph_mean / _total_{mean,min,max}, last_tick_priority_bid_mean); nothing cumulative exists in SimStats and nothing reaches PerSeed.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/runtime/mesh.rs:302-322 attributes node_energy_before - *energy to report.vm_cost / report.graph_cost per dispatch; crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:546-575 sums them plus output.priority_bid into TickComputeStats; crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:584-598 commit() writes ONLY last_tick_* means and then the struct is dropped (stats.rs:320-332 are the only sinks); crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1935-1948 PerSeed carries only u64 work counters (creature_ticks, mesh_hops, vm_steps, graph_relax_iters, plasticity_updates, actions_applied, births) and no energy field; in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json the only key matching /energy/ is population_persistence.per_seed[].mean_energy, and the gate half t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability.json is the same. Also note crates/v3-core/src/runtime/vm.rs:445 subtracts the SetPriorityBid payment from *energy inside the vm_cost attribution window, so vm_cost today silently conflates instruction charges with bids paid for turn order (bids order execution: tick.rs:1128 sort_by_priority_bid).
why: Targeted check 3: the program's ONE realized-cost reading, 'brain compute energy per creature-tick, mean 0.000152, which is 0.03% of the 0.5 per-tick decay' (docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:68), came from GET /v3/simulation/status on a hand-run server (that note's Section 3.1 header line 57), i.e. one tick of last_tick_compute_total_mean via crates/v3-server/src/state.rs:283-287 — layer (c), not a stored report. That single ad-hoc number is load-bearing: it is cited as 'junk is free (Section 3.1)' in the same note's line 49 and carried into the T03 track note as the premise that re-scoped T03.F08 as the junk bound. After T03.F10 made execution lethal, its closure could only report vm_steps -84.6% (docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f10-activity-ramped-compute-cost.md:382); the energy the ramp actually charged was never measured. The same reading also cannot separate compute from bids.
criterion: T03.F08 later reads its realized cost beside the 2026-09-07 figure
proposal: Add three f64 cumulative fields to SimStats — compute_energy_vm_total, compute_energy_graph_total, priority_bid_energy_total — accumulated in TickComputeStats::commit() from the sums it already holds (queue-order summation, deterministic by the existing comment at tick.rs:541-543), and mirror them into bench.rs PerSeed plus the per_creature_tick ratio block beside vm_steps. Realized amounts (the actual energy deltas), not nominal. Compute-proper is then vm_total - bid_total. No new probe, no extra run time.
corrections: Two corrections to the finder's framing, both narrowing the proposal rather than the gap. (1) The proposed arithmetic "compute-proper = vm_total - bid_total" is WRONG as specified. crates/v3-core/src/runtime/vm.rs:462 does `side_outputs.priority_bid = paid` — an overwrite, pinned by the last-write-wins test at crates/v3-core/src/runtime/mesh.rs:1063-1131 where a creature executing SetPriorityBid twice (5.0 then 2.0) reports priority_bid == 2.0. But `*energy -= paid` at vm.rs:445 fires on EVERY SetPriorityBid execution, and the enclosing node is BackendDef::Vm, so mesh.rs:317-320 charges all 7.0 to report.vm_cost. Cumulating TickComputeStats.priority_bid_sum therefore yields "final bid per creature-tick", not "bid energy paid", and subtracting it from vm_total leaves every superseded bid inside "compute-proper". Separating bids from instruction charges requires a new per-dispatch paid-bid accumulator in the VM's side_outputs — still cheap, but it is not the finder's claimed "no new probe, existing sums only". The plain cumulative totals (vm, graph, total) are correct as proposed; only the decomposition needs the extra field. (2) The cited criterion is already a completed miss, not a pending one: T03.F08 closed on main at beee4c05 (2026-09-07), and its spec docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f08-genome-size-maintenance-cost.md:57 satisfies "reads its realized cost" by re-citing the same layer-(c) ad-hoc 0.000152 figure rather than a stored reading. The gap has already cost one closure its realized-cost measurement. Minor: the determinism justification at tick.rs:541-543 covers integer commutation; f32/f64 energy sums are deterministic here by fixed queue order, not commutation — same conclusion, different reason, and any new cumulative field should say so.

Two narrowings to the proposal, not to the gap. (1) The bid half cannot be built from MeshOutput.priority_bid. That field is last-write-wins per creature per tick (vm.rs:462 `side_outputs.priority_bid = paid;` overwrites; proved by the test at crates/v3-core/src/runtime/mesh.rs:1063-1131, where two nodes bid 5.0 then 2.0 and output.priority_bid == 2.0), while every SetPriorityBid execution actually pays (vm.rs:445 `*energy -= paid;`). So priority_bid_sum undercounts realized bid energy whenever a creature bids in two nodes or in a loop, and the finder's derived "compute-proper = vm_total - bid_total" would overstate compute by exactly the discarded earlier bids. vm_cost itself is unaffected — the mesh.rs:301-322 energy-delta window captures all bids — so the conflation the finder identifies is real, but fixing it needs a new side_output accumulated at the vm.rs:445 payment site, not a mirror of the existing bid value. Only the VM pays bids (no priority_bid surface exists under crates/v3-core/src/runtime/cgp/), so graph_cost is unconflated. (2) Do not place the new energy fields inside the per_creature_tick block that T10's regression thresholds compare (docs/roadmaps/t10-...:61, 10% flag / 50% severe), because roadmap.md:57 requires every new capacity to add an applied energy cost — an energy-per-creature-tick under those thresholds would flag every future mechanism feature by design. Report it beside vm_steps but excluded from the flag/severe comparison; the same T10:61 sentence separating compute cost from the energy tradeoff is the license for that split. Also note the source sums are f32 (tick.rs:503-511), so the cumulative fields should be f64 accumulated once per tick from the f32 tick sum, not f32 running totals.

Narrowed on program need, not on the gap itself. The cited criterion is real but is a sequencing note attached to two features that are BOTH CLOSED as of 2026-09-07 — T03.F10 and T03.F08 are `[x]` at docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:41 and :37, with closure rows at docs/progress.md:65-66 — and under the roadmap's closure contract (docs/roadmap.md:45, "closure state lives only in the track checkboxes and docs/progress.md, closed IDs stay in place") it is not an open requirement. Nothing in the Final Success Criteria (docs/roadmap.md, Final Success Criteria block) asks for an energy cost reading; its compute criterion is "no severe unjustified compute regression", which the existing work-counter plus wall-clock comparison already serves. The nearest OPEN consumer — not a requirement — is T11.F13 (docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:63 `[ ]`), which must "Report requested/applied supply, ... persistence, and compute cost" (:102) and runs a per-node-supply arm paired with "a junk bound ... a per-node cost through T03.F08"; that "compute cost" is satisfiable today by vm_steps/mesh_hops/graph_relax_iters plus wall time, so realized energy would sharpen it rather than unblock it. T09.F08's "realized costs" (docs/roadmaps/t09-cognition-and-learning.md:44) is interpretation guidance, not a required reading. Also correct one supporting citation: the determinism comment at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:541-543 justifies INTEGER work-counter commutativity only; the proposed f64 accumulation is deterministic because Phase 2 records in sequential queue order after sort_by_priority_bid (tick.rs:1128), not because of that comment. Layer classification (present in layer (c) as last_tick_compute_*/last_tick_priority_bid_mean, absent from the stored report at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1935-1948 PerSeed) and all other cited code evidence hold as stated.

title: Eating is the world's only energy inflow and no energy or food quantity is counted, only events
missing: Cumulative energy gained by eating, per food type. SimStats has exactly one eat counter, eat_actions_applied_total_by_type (event counts), and no counter of food units consumed or energy credited.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:71-82: apply_typed_eat credits (energy + food * reward).clamp(0.0, max_energy) where reward is the per-type energy_per_unit or the shared eat_reward_per_food, and records nothing; crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:717-733: execute_eat already reads food_before and passes it to the action log, but the only SimStats write is the per-type event increment at 726-729; crates/v3-core/src/kernel/ordinary_food/state.rs:111-120 consume_type zeroes the cell and returns the whole amount, so units per eat vary continuously with regrowth and cannot be recovered from event counts; SimStats field list (stats.rs:191-348) contains no intake sum; the stored report carries typed_eats_total and typed_eat_share (event counts and shares) and food_density_total, and no energy figure — grep for 'intake' in the goal JSON returns nothing.
why: With no intake total, every cost in the sim is unnormalizable: no charge can be stated as a share of what the population actually earns, and mean_energy (a stock) cannot distinguish a rich population eating little from a poor one eating constantly. It also breaks the food-type tradeoff the baseline worlds are built on: experiments/worlds/orchards-in-grassland.json:12,23 set energy_per_unit 4.0 vs 15.0 and experiments/worlds/confluence.json:192,202 set 5.0 vs 15.0, so a 3-4x difference in energy per bite is stored only as a share of eat events. crates/v3-cli/src/inspect.rs:70-100 already multiplies density by effective_energy_per_unit for a standing-energy reading, so the currency exists in the CLI and not in the report.
criterion: food types trading energy per bite against coverage, regrowth, and recovery (a tradeoff landscape, not the nutrient budget removed on 2026-09-07)
proposal: Add eat_energy_gained_total_by_type: HashMap<OrdinaryFoodTypeId, f64> to SimStats, incremented in execute_eat with the REALIZED gain (energy after the credit-and-clamp minus energy before, measured around apply_typed_eat so the max_energy clamp is not overstated), mirroring the existing eat_actions_applied_total_by_type shape. Store it in the goal report's per-case block beside typed_eats_total. One counter, no new pass over the world.
refutations:
REFUTED on Lens 3: the criterion is real and quoted verbatim but does not require the signal, and no other criterion does.

(1) The cited criterion is T12 track criterion 2, docs/roadmaps/t12-world-composition-and-baseline-worlds.md:19 — "Food types can differ in energy per bite, coverage, regrowth, and recovery THROUGH THE WORLD CONFIG ALONE, production defaults unchanged". It is a world-config capability criterion and it is already checked [x]. The amendment at the same file:49 states outright: "Track criteria 2 and 3 are met at T12.F04 (per-type food fields with production defaults unchanged, and the goal-worlds report recording each recipe's path and digest)", user-signed on 2026-09-09 at the merge. A met capability criterion cannot demand new telemetry.

(2) The same amendment shows the food pressure's reading was deliberately settled as eat share, citing "Confluence's 5% fruit eat share at T12.F04" as the evidence the tradeoff works. Adding an energy currency is a change to a signed baseline reading, not a gap fill.

(3) None of the seven Final Success Criteria in docs/roadmap.md mention energy, intake, or food; they name diversity indicators, cognition indicators, compute regression, mutational-neighborhood floors, reproducibility, progress.md rows, and the natural-analog rule.

(4) The shared baseline contract (docs/workflow.md:336-356) requires each NEW environmental-pressure feature to record "per-environment persistence and pressure observations" — it opens no food-energy reading clause and imposes nothing retroactively.

(5) The T12.F04 spec never considered an intake reading: grep over docs/specs/roadmap/t12-f04-baseline-world-set.md for intake/energy_gained/typed_eat returns only the config field list (line 43) and one prose "1.6 energy per bite" (line 72). The only "intake" in docs/roadmaps, docs/workflow.md, docs/roadmap.md is Charnov's theoretical intake rate in the T12 track note (t12:51) — literature framing, not a required reading.

(6) The finder's stated motive ("every cost in the sim is unnormalizable", telling a rich population from a poor one) is diagnostic/normalization apparatus, which is exactly what the standing user preference defers: basic diversity/cognition tracking plus perf regression only. Intake is neither a diversity nor a cognition measure, so the "wire the indicator into the goal profile" rule does not pull it in either. The only future hook is T03.F04 (Resource Conversion and Digestion Specialization, docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:29, open, depends on T02.F01+T03.F01), whose closure could reasonably own an intake-by-type reading — a hypothetical future need, not a present requirement.

Facts verified and worth keeping (the claim fails Lens 3, not Lenses 1-2): the runtime absence IS real — SimStats carries no intake sum, and the newest stored goal report (docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json) has zero occurrences of intake/eat_energy/energy_gained against 63 typed_eats_total, 63 food_density_total, 66 mean_energy. No hard constraint is violated by the proposal (applied behavior, one counter, no RNG, no execution change, negligible cost).
corrections: Three narrowings, one of which changes what gets built. (1) "Eating is the world's only energy inflow" holds at production defaults, not unconditionally: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:116-118 awards a created (not transferred) kill_complexity_bonus, whose multiplier defaults to 0.0 (crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:830). That bonus is likewise uncounted in energy terms (only predation_kills_total exists). Say "the only energy inflow at production defaults." (2) "No energy or food quantity is counted, only events" is overbroad — food_density_total (bench.rs:1393, from last_tick_food_total_density_by_type) is a stored food quantity; it is a standing-stock snapshot, not a flow. The accurate claim is "no consumed food units and no credited energy — no flow quantity." (3) The proposal's measurement point as written produces the wrong number: apply_typed_eat clamps the credit at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:80-81 and then debits eat_cost at mod.rs:83-87 before returning, so sampling creature.energy before and after the call yields gain minus eat_cost, not the credited gain. The counter must sample between the clamp and the debit — have apply_typed_eat return the realized gain, or split the cost debit out of it. Minor: "every cost in the sim is unnormalizable" overreaches; an intake total supplies the denominator, but no cost numerator (compute, maintenance, reproduction) is stored either, so intake alone enables the denominator rather than completing the normalization.

Narrowed claim: at production defaults eating is the only energy inflow and no energy or food quantity is counted anywhere, only eat events. Three corrections. (1) "The world's only energy inflow" is true only at production defaults — `crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:118` awards a kill-complexity bonus created from the victim's complexity rather than transferred, but `kill_complexity_bonus_multiplier` defaults to 0.0 (`crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:830`); separately, predation's transferred amount (`predation.rs:100-101`) is also counted only as events (`predation_actions_transferred_total`), so the uncounted-flow problem is broader than eating. (2) The proposal's measurement point is wrong as written: `crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:80-87` deducts `eat_cost` AFTER the credit-and-clamp, so an energy delta measured around the `apply_typed_eat` call in `execute_eat` yields gain minus cost, not the gain. The realized gain must be captured inside `apply_typed_eat` between the clamp and the cost deduction and returned, or computed as `min(food * reward, max_energy - energy_before)`. (3) The units-consumed half is nearly free and should be stated separately from the energy half: `crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:717` already holds `food_before`, and `consume_food_type` (`crates/v3-core/src/kernel/world.rs:137-139`) delegates straight to `consume_type` (`crates/v3-core/src/kernel/ordinary_food/state.rs:111-120`), which zeroes the cell and returns the whole amount, so `food_before` IS the units consumed — but it reaches only the per-creature action log (`tick.rs:733`), which `bench.rs` never reads, so it does not close the gap. Also correct the criterion cited: roadmap.md:47 / T12 track criterion 2 is a config-capability criterion already marked met, not a measurement one. The honest anchor is T12 criterion 4 ("every environmental mechanism feature closed after it records its readings on that set") plus the fact that the 3-4x per-bite differences in `experiments/worlds/orchards-in-grassland.json:12,23` (4.0 vs 15.0) and `experiments/worlds/confluence.json:192,202` (5.0 vs 15.0) are unrepresentable in event shares.

Two factual errors in the finder's write-up, independent of the verdict. (a) "records nothing" is overstated: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:637-649 pushes the per-eat food units (`amount` = food_before) together with `energy_before`/`energy_after` into a per-creature ring buffer, consumed live by crates/v3-server/src/http/creature.rs:319,337. The quantity per eat therefore exists per-creature at the live layer; what is absent is any aggregation into SimStats or the stored report. (b) The proposal's measurement point is wrong as written: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:82-86 deducts `adjusted_action_cost` INSIDE apply_typed_eat, so an energy delta measured around that call yields the clamped credit minus the eat action cost, not the intake. A correct counter must sit between the clamped credit and the cost deduction, or record `food * reward` with the clamp loss tracked separately. If an intake counter is ever wanted, it belongs to T03.F04's closure (the body-side digestion feature whose whole subject is per-type energy yield), not to T12, whose criterion 2 is closed.

title: Cognition terminated by energy exhaustion discards the whole action queue and is counted nowhere in production
missing: A counter of dispatches that ended with TerminationReason::EnergyExhausted during production ticks. The reason is produced by the executor and discarded by the production mode.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/runtime/mesh.rs:345-353: on result.energy_exhausted the mesh returns actions: vec![WorldAction::NoOp] — the queued actions are discarded — with TerminationReason::EnergyExhausted; crates/v3-core/src/runtime/mesh.rs:159-165: the plain (production) mode's finish() takes _termination_reason and drops it, so only the traced mode (traced_mesh.rs:159) keeps it; SimStats (stats.rs:191-348) has no termination or exhaustion field; the string 'exhaust' occurs 0 times in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json, and the T11.F14 mesh_execution block stores hop_cap_hits and hop_cap_fraction only — the hop cap is instrumented, the energy cap is not.
why: This is the applied consequence of every compute cost: after T03.F10 a creature that loops does not merely get truncated, it loses its turn and starves. The T03 roadmap note for T03.F10 states the design as 'the existing exhausted-energy path (queue discarded, NoOp, death at zero energy) does the rest', and its spec verified the path only on the drift-walk battery ('exhausts at five of the six battery energies (5, 15, 25, 31, 45; not 80)', docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f10-activity-ramped-compute-cost.md:122) — never in a world run. How often energy exhaustion fires in production, and whether it fires at all at goal-profile energies, is unknown at closure.
criterion: so a runaway loop starves its creature instead of being silently cut off at the step cap
proposal: Carry one bool on MeshOutput (or a u32 in the existing WorkCounters that already ride MeshOutput) set when the executor finishes with EnergyExhausted, sum it in TickComputeStats::record in queue order into a new SimStats u64 mesh_dispatch_energy_exhausted_total, and report it in PerSeed beside the other work counters. Counts an applied event, adds no probe, and needs no change to the traced executor.
corrections: Two narrowings. (1) The hop-cap contrast is cross-layer and should not be read as "production instruments the hop cap but not the energy cap": hop_cap_hits/hop_cap_fraction are computed in the synthetic mutational-neighborhood battery (crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/mesh_execution.rs:140-150, surfaced at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:979-981) over sampled genomes at fixed battery energies, not over the live population. Production aggregation instruments neither cap; energy exhaustion is additionally uninstrumented in the battery. (2) "The reason is produced by the executor and discarded" is true of the production mode only — the traced path preserves it (crates/v3-core/src/runtime/traced_mesh.rs:159) and v3-server ships EnergyExhausted per sampled creature (crates/v3-server/src/transport/sample_protocol.rs:33-35). The gap is that no aggregate count exists over the live population and none is stored at closure, not that the runtime never computes the reason.

Three narrowings. (1) "Counted nowhere in production" should be "no aggregate counter exists, so nothing reaches SimStats, PerSeed, or the stored report": the reason does survive on two non-production surfaces — the traced sampling path (`tick.rs:452-477` -> traced_mesh.rs -> `crates/v3-server/src/transport/sample_assembler.rs:69-70`) exposes `EnergyExhausted` per sampled creature in the live trace payload, and `MeshObservation` (`mesh.rs:169-171`) carries `termination_reason` for the neighborhood battery's `ObservedMeshExecution`, which `neighborhood/mesh_execution.rs` reads for hop-cap hits but never for exhaustion. Neither is a production-wide count. (2) Misattributed block: `hop_cap_fraction` lives on the drift-depth checkpoint struct (`crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:638-640`), not the T11.F14 `MeshExecution` block, which carries `hop_cap_hits` only (bench.rs:1163). The point stands — hop cap instrumented, energy cap not. (3) "Unknown at closure" is right for world runs, but the stored `drift_depth` block already carries an indirect battery proxy: T03.F10's spec predeclared `dead_per_all_births` with an explicit allowance (<=20/4,000) attributed to all-NoOp exhaustion at battery energies (`docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f10-activity-ramped-compute-cost.md`, Verification table). What is missing is a world-run reading, i.e. how often exhaustion fires at goal-profile energies under selection.

The gap is real but the need is overstated on three points.

1. PRIORITY (the main correction): the cited criterion belongs to a CLOSED feature. T03.F10 is checked off at docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:41 (closed on main at 23f230af). `grep -n exhaust docs/roadmap.md docs/roadmaps/*.md docs/workflow.md` finds no open feature that consumes an exhaustion frequency: the only other hits are T11.F06's "energy-exhaustion rollback" (t11:95) and T13.F04's "budget exhaustion behavior" (t13:49), both behavioral semantics to preserve, not readings to take. None of the seven Final Success Criteria (docs/roadmap.md:34-40) consumes this signal either. So this is post-closure verification of a closed mechanism claim, sitting outside the user's stated scope (basic diversity/cognition tracking plus perf regression) — worth doing opportunistically inside whatever feature next touches the mesh executor, not worth scheduling as its own feature until a consumer appears.

2. The hop-cap parallel is misattributed. `hop_cap_hits` in the goal report is NOT production instrumentation: it is the offline mutational-neighborhood / drift-depth battery reading (crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/mesh_execution.rs:24, MeshExecutionReading.hop_cap_hits, produced by ObservedMeshExecution), emitted at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:979-981 and denominated by `battery_executions`. Neither the hop cap nor the energy cap has a production-tick counter; the finder's "the hop cap is instrumented, the energy cap is not" compares an offline probe against production ticks.

3. "Discarded by the production mode" is right for the untraced executor (mesh.rs:162), but EnergyExhausted is not universally lost at runtime: it reaches layer (c) as TerminationReasonPayload::EnergyExhausted for the single sampled creature in the live server (crates/v3-server/src/transport/sample_assembler.rs:69-71). It is never aggregated and never stored, so the (a) SimStats and (b) stored-report absences stand — the correct framing is "exists per-sample in (c), absent as a counter from (a), absent from (b)", which is the cheap-fix category rather than a true runtime-absent one.

Four corrections; the gap survives all of them, narrowed.

1. "Whether it fires at all at goal-profile energies is unknown at closure" is FALSE and must not stand. T03.F10 is closed (checked at t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:40; docs/progress.md:65) and its closure read the consequence in production: goal vm_steps 22.566373, -84.56% against the pinned 146.184594, and seed 33's cap-running bloom (12.05% of 11,379 creatures at T11.F17) gone, with clades/entropy 136/1.649503 against 54/0.158688. The spec's Scope row (docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f10-activity-ramped-compute-cost.md, Scope) makes it analytic as well: a capped dispatch costs about 49 energy against initial energy 20 and reproduction at 30, so any population creature reaching the cap exhausts. The criterion is satisfied; what is missing is a direct count, not the evidence.

2. "Counted nowhere in production" should read "counted only as an undifferentiated NoOp." The exhaustion NoOp from mesh.rs:345 is applied at tick.rs:975 and increments last_tick_noop (tick.rs:696; stats.rs:310) — layer (c), per-tick, reset each tick, conflated with genuine NoOps, never accumulated into the stored report.

3. The hop-cap comparison is misattributed. hop_cap_hits is not production instrumentation: it is computed in the neighborhood observation battery, crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/mesh_execution.rs:140-148, from ObservedMeshExecution's termination_reason, and surfaced by bench.rs:638/979. Production instruments neither cap. The real asymmetry is battery-vs-production — and because that battery already matches on termination_reason, a one-line EnergyExhausted arm there is an equally cheap adjacent fix over sampled genomes, complementary to (not a substitute for) the production counter.

4. Granularity: mesh.rs:345 returns from the whole creature-tick mesh execution, so the counter is creature-ticks ended by exhaustion (at most one per creature-tick), not per-node dispatches. Per the spec's Exhaustion row, exhaustion settles energy to <= 0.0, so the reading is effectively compute-starvation deaths — the program's first and only death-cause reading, given the verified absence of any death counter (helpers.rs:9-15, tick.rs:184-189).

Design nuance: report it like births / final_population, not like vm_steps. It is an ecological-outcome count, so putting it under the work-counter +10% flag / +50% severe thresholds would flag on every later feature that touches the energy budget.

Two narrowings. (1) "Counted nowhere" is literally slightly false: the substituted NoOp is applied and increments `last_tick_noop` at `crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:696` (and rolls into `actions_applied_total`). But that is layer (c) — reset every tick (stats.rs:365), never accumulated, never stored — and it conflates energy exhaustion with genuine NoOp actions and with the other actionless exits that also emit a bare NoOp (`mesh.rs:268-274` MissingNode; `mesh.rs:277-285` MaxHopsReached and `mesh.rs:355-362` ActionEmitted via `into_actions_or_noop` on an empty queue; NoTargets at `mesh.rs:388`). The accurate claim is that exhaustion is unattributable, not uncounted. (2) "The hop cap is instrumented, the energy cap is not" overstates the contrast: `hop_cap_hits` is a neighborhood-battery reading counting `MaxHopsReached` over battery dispatches (`crates/v3-core/src/neighborhood/mesh_execution.rs:140-148`), not a production-tick counter — neither termination reason is counted in production. Adding `EnergyExhausted` to that same battery loop is a separate one-line fix, but only the production counter the finder proposes fills the layer-(b) gap for live populations.

title: Action charges are age-multiplied and ramped, so no stored counter can reconstruct what actions cost
missing: A cumulative sum of energy charged by action costs (move, eat, noop, reproduce, steal cost) and by the failed-action penalty. No SimStats field sums any charge, and the multipliers that scale every charge are themselves unrecorded.
evidence: Charge sites: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:56, :83, :116 (noop/eat/move via config.energy.adjusted_action_cost), crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:161, crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:62-67, crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:654-657 (debit_failed_action) — none touches sim.stats. Not derivable from counts even if counts were stored: crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:469-473 defaults age_cost to enabled: true, age_cap 500, max_multiplier 10.0, so the same action costs 1x to 10x depending on the actor's age, and 'age' occurs zero times in the stored report; crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:912-919 makes failed_action_penalty tick-dependent during the startup ramp. SimStats (stats.rs:191-348) holds only event counters. The per-action energy_before/energy_after pair that already exists (tick.rs:640-650, pushed into the per-creature ActionLog) is a NET delta including eat reward and steal gain, so it is not the cost, and the log is a bounded per-creature buffer dropped on death (predation.rs: sim.action_logs.remove).
why: Targeted check 3: the only published action-cost claim, 'Invalid actions 46,581,809 of 475,876,566 (9.8%), each costing the failed_action_penalty of 1.0 energy (ramped in by tick 62,680), five times a move' (docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:66), is nominal rate x event count and ignores the age multiplier that is on by default — the actual charge for a 500-tick-old creature is 10.0, not 1.0. Nothing in any layer can check that claim. Targeted check 4: this is why a predeclared cost cannot be verified at closure.
