T03.F01 is specified to work 'through the same energy accounting that governs eating and reproduction'; when it closes, the observable evidence for its cost is population and work counters moving, exactly as T03.F10 closed on vm_steps and T03.F08 on 'reachable structure ... no direction'.
criterion: Every body trait changes applied simulation behavior and has an observable ecological cost or tradeoff.
proposal: Add one f64 action_energy_charged_total to SimStats accumulating the REALIZED charge at the six sites. Cheapest plumbing: apply_noop/apply_typed_eat/apply_move take &mut CreatureState and config with no stats access, so snapshot in the tick.rs execute_* wrappers, which already hold ctx.energy_before, or have the apply_* functions return the charge they computed. Report it in PerSeed and as a per-creature-tick ratio. One counter; do not split by action type unless a later cost feature needs it.
refutations: Every code fact checks out, but the claim fails LENS 3: the cited criterion does not require this signal, and the proposed counter would not satisfy it. (1) The criterion is quoted verbatim from docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:16, but the same track file already operationalizes "observable ecological cost" for both closed cost features as applied behavioral readings, not a charge ledger: T03.F08's note specifies verification via the goal profile's reachable-structure distribution plus a long run for node count at depth, and T03.F10's via vm_steps falling on the goal profile plus persistence re-read against the T11.F04 sweeps. The track owner has already defined what "observable" means here. (2) The proposal cannot meet the criterion it cites. A single global f64 action_energy_charged_total (plus a per-creature-tick ratio) cannot attribute cost to a trait, cannot show a tradeoff, and cannot show the cost is ecological (i.e., reaches survival or reproduction); after T03.F01 ships, the criterion-level evidence is still the population/behavior contrast. It is neither necessary nor sufficient. (3) Precedent and the standing workflow rule put any action-cost reading inside the cost feature's own spec, not in a standalone telemetry feature: T03.F10 introduced last_tick_compute_total_mean/last_tick_compute_{vm,graph}_mean as part of the feature that introduced the compute cost. T03.F01 is unstarted, so its spec is the correct home. (4) It is outside the user's standing scope of basic diversity/cognition tracking plus perf regression; an energy-charge ledger is neither. Under "default to REFUTED when uncertain," passing the explicit refute triggers (criterion real, not a composite score, cheap, not on the deferred list) is not the same as the program needing the signal.
corrections: Correct but slightly imprecise in four details. (a) The scaling is complexity x age, not age alone: adjusted_action_cost = ComplexityEnergyCostConfig::multiplier x AgeEnergyCostConfig::multiplier (config/simulation.rs:507-524). Complexity defaults to enabled:false (config/simulation.rs:431-439), so under production defaults only the age multiplier varies — the finder's framing is right for defaults but incomplete for configs that enable complexity cost, which would add a second unrecorded multiplier keyed on cached_complexity (creature/state.rs:216, genome.complexity()), a quantity also absent from the stored report. (b) eat_cost defaults to 0.0 (config/simulation.rs:408), so of the six charge sites only five contribute anything under defaults. (c) On the docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:66 claim: the absolute "1.0 energy" is indeed wrong for aged creatures (a 500-tick-old creature pays 10.0), but the accompanying ratio "five times a move" survives, because move_cost 0.2 and failed_action_penalty 1.0 (config/simulation.rs:407,412) are scaled by the same multiplier; the ramp is the larger error for short runs, where the realized penalty is far below 1.0. (d) The nearest existing cost-adjacent telemetry, last_tick_compute_total_{mean,min,max} and last_tick_compute_{vm,graph}_mean (stats.rs:319-331), is a per-tick mean of brain compute cost at layer (c) — it is neither cumulative nor any of the six action charge sites, so it does not weaken the claim.

Two overstatements to narrow. (a) Targeted check 3 is half right: the age multiplier scales `move_cost` by the identical factor (same `adjusted_action_cost` call at actions/mod.rs:116 as `debit_failed_action` at tick.rs:654-656), so the ratio claim "five times a move" in docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:66 survives the multiplier unchanged; only the absolute figure — "each costing the failed_action_penalty of 1.0 energy" — is understated, by up to 10x for creatures at or past age 500 and by an unknown population-age-weighted factor overall. `complexity_cost` defaults to `enabled: false` (config/simulation.rs:431-434), so age is the only live multiplier. (b) "Nothing in any layer can check that claim" should be "no layer sums action or failed-action charges": layer (c) does expose realized compute charges (SimStats `last_tick_compute_{total,vm,graph}_*`, surfaced as `last_tick_compute_energy_*` in crates/v3-server/src/transport/protocol.rs:101-105), which is the source of the same note's 0.000152 energy-per-creature-tick line. The action-cost reconstruction additionally fails on the numerator, not just the rate: the invalid-action count is itself not in the stored goal report. Otherwise the gap, its layer (runtime-absent, therefore also absent from the stored report), and the one-counter proposal stand as stated.

Narrowed claim: a cumulative realized-charge counter is a genuine layer-(a) absence and a cheap instrument, but no current criterion requires it, and the proposal as scoped cannot satisfy the criterion it cites.

1. The criterion says "observable *ecological* cost or tradeoff" (t03:16), not an accounting ledger, and the program has already twice verified predeclared costs at closure without one — T03.F10 closed on vm_steps -84.6%, T03.F08 on the reachable-structure distribution plus a persistence re-read. So "this is why a predeclared cost cannot be verified at closure" is wrong; predeclared costs have been verified, via ecological proxies. The counter substitutes a direct read for a proxy — a better instrument, not a criterion gap.

2. The criterion governs zero closed features. T03.F01-F07 are all open (t03:23-37); the two closed T03 features (F08, F10) are not body traits. The need is anticipatory.

3. One undifferentiated f64 across six sites attributes nothing to any individual trait, so it cannot answer "every body trait has an observable cost." Per-trait attribution is T03.F01's own indicator. Per the standing rule that a feature wires its indicator in the same feature, the right home is T03.F01's spec, not a standalone telemetry feature — which is also what keeps it inside the user's declared scope rather than scope creep.

4. Evidence narrowing: the complexity multiplier is off by default (assert `!cfg.energy.complexity_cost.enabled`, config/simulation.rs:1354), so age is the *only* live multiplier — "multipliers" plural overstates. And the mesh-depth-research:66 claim's ratio survives: failed_action_penalty 1.0 and move_cost 0.2 (config/simulation.rs:407-412) both pass through the same `adjusted_action_cost`, so "five times a move" is exact; only the absolute 1.0 is nominal (up to 10.0 at age >= 500).

5. Scope note: an action-only ledger is a partial energy budget. The other sinks are per-tick decay and T03.F08's carrying charge, which tick.rs:141 applies flat (`energy_decay_per_tick + genome_carry_cost_per_unit * genome_size`) with no age multiplier — derivable in principle from rate x genome_size, except genome_size is itself unstored. So the counter is a magnitude check against the 0.5/tick decay, not an energy decomposition; it should be described that way.

Three narrowings. (1) The depth note's "five times a move" (docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:66) is NOT broken by the age multiplier: adjusted_action_cost applies the same complexity_cost.multiplier * age_cost.multiplier product to the failed-action penalty and to move_cost alike (config/simulation.rs:513-524), so the 5:1 ratio is exact at any age. Only the absolute "1.0 energy" is wrong — it is a nominal floor understating the realized charge by up to 10x. (Also, complexity_cost is disabled by default — the test at simulation.rs:2062-2066 must set enabled=true explicitly — so age is the only live multiplier, making the finder's 1x-to-10x range exactly right.) (2) The ActionLog's energy_before/energy_after pair (tick.rs:637-650) IS exactly the realized charge for Move and NoOp, since apply_move and apply_noop have no reward path; it is a net delta only for Eat and Steal. The real disqualifier is that the log is a bounded per-creature buffer, dropped on death, and never aggregated into SimStats or the stored report. (3) The runtime-absent gap is specific to action charges, the failed-action penalty, reproduce/steal costs, and T03.F08's genome-maintenance charge — it does not cover all energy sinks. Brain compute charge already has a layer-(c) reading: last_tick_compute_total_{mean,min,max} and last_tick_compute_{vm,graph}_mean (stats.rs:319, :331), documented as "Mean total (vm + graph) compute energy cost," which is where the depth note's "0.000152 energy per creature-tick" came from. That reading is still absent from the stored report (layer b) — no compute_total field appears anywhere in crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs, only in v3-server/src/state.rs:80-84 — so exposing it in the report is an even cheaper adjacent fix than the new counter.

The true kernel, narrowed. (a) Runtime absence is real and correctly located: no SimStats field sums any energy charge, and none of the six charge sites touches sim.stats — crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/mod.rs:56,83,116; actions/reproduction.rs:151; actions/predation.rs:62-67; simulation/tick.rs:654-657 (debit_failed_action). (b) The one concrete defect is a published-claim error, not a criterion gap: docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:66 states each invalid action costs the failed_action_penalty of 1.0 energy, but crates/v3-core/src/config/simulation.rs:466-473 defaults AgeEnergyCostConfig to enabled with age_cap 500 and max_multiplier 10.0, and simulation.rs:512-523 multiplies every base cost by it, so the realized charge is 1.0 to 10.0 by actor age. The note's absolute figure is wrong; its "five times a move" ratio survives, since move_cost (0.2) scales by the same multiplier. Fix the note, do not add a feature. (c) Layer correction: the label "runtime-absent" is right only for SimStats. The exact realized charge for move, noop, and failed actions already exists transiently as energy_before minus energy_after in the per-creature ActionLog (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:636-650) and is exposed live at crates/v3-server/src/http/creature.rs:319-337 — layer (c). The quantity exists; what is missing is aggregation into SimStats and storage in the closure report. Only the eat and steal deltas are net rather than cost. (d) If T03.F01 predeclares a per-trait cost rate and wants it checkable at closure, that spec should add a realized-charge reading following T03.F10's last_tick_compute_* precedent, scoped to the feature that introduces the cost, alongside the per-trait behavioral contrast the criterion actually asks for.

Narrowings, not reversals. (1) Only the AGE multiplier is live under production defaults: ComplexityEnergyCostConfig::default is enabled:false (config/simulation.rs:431-438), so "the multipliers that scale every charge" should read "the age multiplier (complexity scaling exists at simulation.rs:441-453 but is off by default)". (2) The criticism of docs/strategy/mesh-depth-research-2026-09-07.md:66 is half-overstated: failed_action_penalty (1.0) and move_cost (0.2) both pass through the same adjusted_action_cost, so the "five times a move" RATIO is multiplier-invariant and survives post-ramp; only the absolute "each costing ... 1.0 energy" figure, and any energy total derived from 46,581,809 x 1.0, are wrong for aged creatures. (3) "'age' occurs zero times in the stored report" is true of JSON key names, not raw text — the substring appears 1,586 times inside lineage/average. (4) eat_cost defaults to 0.0 (config/simulation.rs:408), so the eat site charges nothing under defaults; the six-site count is right but the default-load charges are move, noop, reproduce, steal, and the failed-action penalty. (5) Line-number fix: the reproduce charge is reproduction.rs:151-155, not :161.

title: The quantity T03.F08 charges every creature every tick is not in the report the feature closed against
missing: Mean carried genome_size per creature-tick (or the equivalent size x creature-tick integral). The Phase 0 charge is genome_carry_cost_per_unit * cached_genome_size, and cached_genome_size reaches no counter and no report field.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:162-166 charges phase_0_energy_charge(energy_decay_per_tick, genome_carry_cost_per_unit, creature.cached_genome_size) once per creature per tick; SimStats (stats.rs:191-348) has no size field; bench PerSeed (crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:385-397) has none; 'genome_size' occurs zero times in both halves of the t13-f01 report; only reachable_structure_size_distribution is stored, which by construction excludes the junk the charge is aimed at. The computation already exists on the other CLI path: crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:189-196 structure_means(sim) emits mean_genome_size in every `v3-cli run` tick_sample (see docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/cost.ndjson line 2), so bench is the only consumer that drops it.
why: Beyond the established 'genome size is not stored': the feature's own predeclared criterion had to be rewritten after implementation because nobody could read the charged quantity. docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f08-genome-size-maintenance-cost.md:195-199 records that the founder pays 2.22% of decay, not the predicted 1.9%, so 'the founder pays under 2% of decay' was revised on 2026-09-07 to 'no more than 2.5% of decay'; line 100 records the same correction (111 units, not the 96 the roadmap and depth note carried). Verification of the population-level charge required a bespoke paired 12,000-tick run outside the closure report (docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/run.sh, arms differing only in the rate) to obtain mean_genome_size 386.5 vs 1,093.8. Targeted check 4 again: the closure report itself could show only reachable structure with 'no direction'.
criterion: Trait mutation preserves bounded viable steps and exposes its applied outcomes through the goal-profile report.
proposal: Add genome_size_creature_ticks_total: u64 to SimStats, incremented by cached_genome_size inside the existing Phase 0 loop (integer, order-independent, no f32 concern), and report it in PerSeed with a per-creature-tick ratio. The ratio is mean carried size; ratio x genome_carry_cost_per_unit is the nominal charge (nominal, not realized — the energy floor at tick.rs:997 can clip it in the tick a creature dies). Cheaper alternative if core changes are unwanted: add mean_genome_size to the persistence sample struct in bench.rs (bench.rs:1290, 1753-1782) by reusing v3-cli's existing structure_means.
corrections: The gap is real but should be labeled and motivated more narrowly. (a) LAYER: not "stored-absent" — the quantity is absent from layer (a) too. SimStats has no size counter at all; cached_genome_size lives only on CreatureState (state.rs:176) and is aggregated only on the v3-cli `run` path (lib.rs:165-186 structure_means), which bench never calls. Correct framing: "no runtime counter anywhere; computable at zero cost from creature state; already computed on a sibling CLI path that the closure report does not use." (b) CAUSATION: "the predeclared criterion had to be rewritten because nobody could read the charged quantity" is overstated. The founder's charged size was readable — crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick/tests/phase0.rs:194 asserts cached_genome_size == 111 and state.rs pins the same value in `the_canonical_founder_genome_is_one_hundred_eleven_units`. The 96 -> 111 correction and the 2.22%-vs-1.9% criterion amendment came from a stale pre-implementation estimate carried in the roadmap and depth note, not from unreadable telemetry. What genuinely required the bespoke paired run is the POPULATION-level carried size at depth (386.5 vs 1,093.8), which no stored report can show. (c) The paired 12,000-tick run was the roadmap's own predeclared verification method, not an improvisation forced by the gap: docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:51 says verification "reads the goal profile's reachable-structure distribution and, since the drift walk has no energy and cannot show a carrying cost, a long run under selection for total node count at depth." The defensible complaint is that this reading is not repeated at any later closure, so no closure report after T03.F08 can show whether the junk bound is holding. (d) PROPOSAL PRECISION: genome_size_creature_ticks_total / creature_ticks is a size-by-creature-tick integral, whereas lib.rs mean_genome_size is a snapshot mean over living creatures at sample ticks; they are both readings of cached_genome_size but are not the same statistic, so the "cheaper alternative" is not a drop-in equivalent. (e) SCHEDULING: nothing currently plans a stored goal-report genome-size field. T11.F13 will read the carrying-cost lever as an arm (docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-genotype-phenotype-map.md:102, :119) and T03.F08's own text at t03:51 names it the comparison lever, but neither predeclares wiring a size indicator into the goal profile, so this remains new work rather than a duplicate of a planned feature.

Two narrowings. (1) Causation of the criterion rewrite is overstated. `docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f08-genome-size-maintenance-cost.md:190-200` attributes the 2026-09-07 revision of "the founder pays under 2% of decay" to "no more than 2.5% of decay" to the founder being 111 genome_size units rather than the 96 the roadmap and depth note carried — a stale figure, not an unreadable one. The founder's size was readable at the time, via the pinned unit test `the_canonical_founder_genome_is_one_hundred_eleven_units` (crates/v3-core/src/creature/state.rs:605 region) and the CLI test `tick_sample_reports_the_founder_structure_means_before_any_birth`, both named in that spec passage. What genuinely required machinery outside the closure report is the POPULATION-level charge: the reconciled generation-50 figure (183.191 units at generation 48.289, 3.66% of decay, cost arm vs 172.294 units, 3.45%, control) came from the bespoke paired 12,000-tick run at `docs/progress/sweeps/t03-f08/run.sh`, two arms differing only in the rate. Cite the population reading, not the founder criterion, as the thing the report could not supply. (2) The report is not entirely silent on structural counts, so the gap should be stated precisely: `drift_depth/readings[].mean_total_nodes` and `mutational_neighborhood/.../mesh_execution.total_node_count` do appear. Neither rebuts the claim — they are the drift-walk cohort and the sampled-genome battery, not the live population, and a node count is not the charged unit; the T03.F08 design table explicitly rejected mesh nodes as the unit because "Junk lives inside nodes as well as between them" and a 500-instruction node outweighs a 19-instruction detour. Narrowed claim: no live-population reading of the charged quantity (total genome_size units, junk included) exists in SimStats or in either half of the stored closure report; the only live-population structural reading stored is reachable-only, and the whole-genome mean is already computed on the `v3-cli run` path.

Narrower claim, with two of the finder's framings corrected. (1) The gap, stated precisely: the goal-profile report stores no reading of carried genome_size, so the multiplicand of an applied per-tick energy charge is invisible in every closure report after T03.F08; reachable_structure_size_distribution is a complexity() distribution (bench.rs:2419, 2545) and by construction excludes the junk the charge targets. This is both runtime-absent (SimStats has no size field) and stored-absent, but it is NOT absent from the codebase: v3-cli's `run` path already emits mean_genome_size per tick_sample (lib.rs:72, 189-196), so bench is the only consumer that drops it and the cheap fix is bench reusing structure_means, not necessarily a new SimStats counter. (2) Drop "the feature's own predeclared criterion had to be rewritten after implementation because nobody could read the charged quantity" — that is misattributed. docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f08-genome-size-maintenance-cost.md:100 and 195-199 attribute the 1.9% -> 2.22% revision to a stale founder figure (96 carried from the depth note vs the actual 111), and the founder's size was independently readable the whole time, by the core test the_canonical_founder_genome_is_one_hundred_eleven_units and the CLI test tick_sample_reports_the_founder_structure_means_before_any_birth (cli.rs:224-229). What the report cannot show is the POPULATION-level carried size, not the founder's. (3) Drop the implication that the bespoke 12,000-tick paired run was a workaround forced by an unnoticed gap: docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:51 predeclared exactly that plan — verification "reads the goal profile's reachable-structure distribution and, since the drift walk has no energy and cannot show a carrying cost, a long run under selection for total node count at depth". The real cost is recurrence: reading this charge again requires repeating that out-of-report paired run, and T13.F06 will need it. (4) The proposal itself is sound against the hard constraints — cached_genome_size is the applied charge's own multiplicand (not a derived composite score), it is u32 so the sum is order-independent, it consumes no RNG and changes no execution, and it is O(1) per creature-tick inside a loop that already runs. Keep the finder's own "nominal, not realized" caveat: the tick.rs:995-997 floor can clip the charge in a creature's death tick.

Three narrowings. (a) CRITERION MISATTRIBUTED, not misquoted. Line 17 of the T03 track is about *body-trait* mutation; T03.F08's own goal line in the same file calls it a cost on carried brain structure ("what running costs is T03.F10's"), so neither track criterion 16 nor 17 is the honest anchor. The anchors actually in the record are: the T03 track note's own admission that "the drift walk has no energy and cannot show a carrying cost", which is why verification was scoped to a separate long run; `docs/roadmap.md:57` ("Every new capacity must have an applied cost or tradeoff owned by the feature that introduces it"); and concretely **T11.F13** (`docs/roadmaps/t11-brain-evolvability.md:102`), which is predeclared to run a junk-bound arm reading `mutation.genome_size_pressure_enabled` (a cap on `genome_size()`) against T03.F08's carrying cost — that comparison needs carried `genome_size` under selection and today has no stored field to read. (b) THE CAUSAL STORY IN "why it matters" IS WRONG. `docs/specs/roadmap/t03-f08-genome-size-maintenance-cost.md:185-199` attributes the 2% -> 2.5% revision to the founder being 111 `genome_size()` units rather than the stale 96, caught by the unit test `the_canonical_founder_genome_is_one_hundred_eleven_units`, not to any missing report field; no stored field could have caught a pre-implementation constant. Only the second half — that population-level verification required a bespoke paired 12,000-tick run outside the closure report — survives, and the track note shows that was planned, not a discovery. (c) LAYER AND "NO DIRECTION" OVERSTATED. The signal is absent at both layer (a) SimStats and layer (b) the stored report; the existing computation sits on the separate `v3-cli run` path (`crates/v3-cli/src/lib.rs:180-196`), and the spec's Fixed design table records the `TickSampleEvent` instrument as "the only telemetry added" — a deliberate scoping choice, not an oversight. And the report is not literally silent on size: `drift_depth.readings[].mean_total_nodes` and `mutational_neighborhood...mesh_execution.total_node_count` are stored. Neither rescues the claim: they are mesh node counts, the spec explicitly rejected per-node pricing because junk also lives inside nodes, and both are taken on a no-energy drift walk or on sampled genomes rather than on a population under selection.

title: Predation counters exist in SimStats and reach neither report half, so nobody knows if creature-to-creature energy transfer happens at all
missing: predation_actions_attempted_total, predation_actions_transferred_total, predation_actions_rejected_total, predation_kills_total and predation_actions_by_result in PerSeed. They are counted at runtime and dropped at the report boundary.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:300-305 declares all five; crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:57-58, 100-101, 125-131 increments them on every attempt, transfer and kill; crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1935-1948 PerSeed copies only seven work counters and does not read any predation field; the string 'predation' occurs zero times in docs/progress/features/t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability-goal.json AND zero times in the gate half t13-f01-module-recruitment-observability.json. The channel is live in production: crates/v3-core/src/runtime/action_decode.rs:20 decodes action code 4 to WorldAction::StealEnergy, so any mutated genome emitting that code steals; the attacker pays steal_cost_rate * requested_amount (predation.rs:62-67) and receives min(request, victim energy) (predation.rs:100-101).
why: Predation is the second energy inflow to a creature and the only one that is not from the world, and its cost is charged on the ATTEMPTED amount whether or not a victim exists, so it is a live energy sink even when it never transfers. Because none of the five counters is stored, the goal report cannot answer whether predation fired even once in a closure run — which also means an energy decomposition built on eating alone could be silently incomplete. T05.F03 is planned as frequency-dependent interaction telemetry, but this is not new instrumentation: it is five existing counters that stop at the report boundary.
criterion: NONE
proposal: Copy the four u64 predation counters into bench.rs PerSeed beside births (and the per_creature_tick ratio block if the rates are wanted). No core change, no runtime cost, no new run time.
refutations:
Lens 2 hit: an existing open feature already owns this telemetry — **T05.F03 "Frequency-Dependent Interaction Telemetry"** (docs/roadmaps/t05-biotic-interactions-and-coevolution.md:30), whose goal is "Record interaction outcomes by lineage so frequency-dependent dynamics are visible in the goal profile; observation only." The goal profile is exactly layer (b), and predation attempted/transferred/rejected/killed are interaction outcomes. Two track notes close the obvious escape hatch that T05.F03 only covers a post-T05.F01 reworked system: :41 claims the *existing* accounting outright — "Extend the existing `StealEnergy` interaction and predation accounting only where they provide sound primitives; do not treat kill counts as proof of coevolution" — and :39 requires "Report applied interactions, including absence," a near-verbatim match for the finder's "cannot answer whether predation fired even once."

OWNER IS UNSCHEDULED, so this is a WEAK refutation, stated explicitly: no T05 ID appears anywhere in the priority order for new starts at docs/roadmap.md:45; T05.F03 is also not in the deferred-proof list at docs/roadmap.md:54 (which names T05.F04/F05/F07 but not F03). It is therefore open, planned, and in neither queue. Its dependency T05.F01 is likewise unscheduled and itself depends on T03.F01 (in-progress), putting the planned owner two unscheduled hops away, while the finder's proposal is a four-field copy into bench.rs PerSeed at crates/v3-cli/src/bench.rs:1935-1948 with zero runtime cost and zero added run time.

title: The energy a parent hands each offspring is creature-chosen and never summed
missing: A cumulative sum of the reproduction energy transfer. births (reproduction_actions_spawned_total) is stored; the per-birth transfer, which the genome chooses and which is clamped to default_offspring_energy (100.0 by default), is summed nowhere.
evidence: crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:177-195: transfer = min(energy_transfer_request, default_offspring_energy) taken from the VM's action parameter, then sim.creatures[parent_id].energy -= transfer; the surrounding stats writes at reproduction.rs:226-240 record mutation events only, never the amount; SimStats (stats.rs:191-348) has no transfer field; the stored report has births at bench.rs:1945 and no energy quantity beyond mean_energy.
why: This is the largest single energy movement in the sim — up to 100 energy against a 0.5 per-tick decay — and it is heterogeneous across the population today because each genome supplies its own energy_transfer. Two populations with identical births can differ by two orders of magnitude in what reproduction actually cost them, and the report cannot tell them apart; combined with the missing intake counter it means the parent-side cost of reproduction is invisible from both directions. When T03.F07's life-history traits are introduced the transfer is precisely the applied cost that criterion asks to be observable, and there is no reading to compare against.
criterion: Every body trait changes applied simulation behavior and has an observable ecological cost or tradeoff.
proposal: Add reproduction_energy_transferred_total: f64 to SimStats, incremented with the realized transfer at reproduction.rs:195 (the value actually deducted, after the clamp and the sufficiency check), and report it in PerSeed beside births so mean investment per birth is a division. One counter, one line at an existing charge site.
corrections: Narrower claim: the gap is real but its justification is prospective, not present-day, and it should ride on an existing feature rather than motivate one. Corrections: (a) the realized deduction is at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:185 (Step 8), not :195, which is the plasticity snapshot; the clamp is :167-173 and the sufficiency check :175-182. (b) The transfer is not a body trait today — it is an action parameter read from a mutable VM constants pool (founder.rs:280-323), so the cited criterion at docs/roadmaps/t03-functional-traits-and-metabolism.md:16 does not bind now; it binds when T03.F07 introduces life-history traits, and T03.F07 (t03 line 35, depends on the in-progress T03.F01) does not appear anywhere in the priority order for new starts at docs/roadmap.md:45. docs/roadmap.md:55 and :57 and t03 line 17 put the obligation to expose a trait's applied cost on the feature that introduces it, so T03.F07 would wire this reading itself; this is not an argument for a standalone telemetry feature. (c) "it is heterogeneous across the population today" is asserted, not measured: the production founder profile is V3Alpha1 (default at config/simulation.rs:1412) whose reproduce-transfer constant is 20.0, so every founder transfers the same 20.0 at tick zero and any spread arises only from later mutation of that constant. The "two orders of magnitude" figure is the clamp range in principle, not an observed spread. The honest framing is that the spread is unknown because nothing counts it, which is the gap — not that a known spread is being hidden.

The absence is real but four particulars are overstated or off. (1) The deduction site is `crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/reproduction.rs:185` ("Step 8: Deduct transfer from parent"), not :195 — line 195 is inside the plasticity snapshot. (2) "Up to 100 energy" is the configured clamp, not an observed magnitude: the five founder profiles emit fixed transfers of 10.0/10.0/15.0/20.0/20.0 (`creature/founder.rs:55-70` and the PROFILES table at 342-348), well under the cap, encoded as `constants[5]` in `node1_vm_decision` (founder.rs:323). The claimed present-day heterogeneity and the "two orders of magnitude" spread are hypotheses that depend on constant mutation and are themselves unmeasured — they are the reason to add the counter, not an established fact the counter would confirm. (3) "The largest single energy movement in the sim" is not established: a predation steal is bounded only by the victim's energy (max_energy default 200), i.e. potentially larger than the 100 reproduction clamp, and its realized amount is equally unsummed — `predation.rs:130,149` increment only a count. If this gap is worth fixing, the same one-line argument applies to the steal amount, and the honest framing is "two uncounted energy transfers," not "the largest one." (4) Layer `runtime-absent` is correct, but note one near-miss so a later reader does not think the gap is closed: `frontend/src/types/trace.ts:140` carries `Reproduce { direction, energy_transfer }` in the per-action inspector trace. That is the pre-clamp REQUESTED value from the decoded action (`runtime/action_decode.rs:18`), for one inspected creature, never aggregated — it is not the realized deduction and does not satisfy the reading.

Four narrowings; the gap and the proposal survive all of them.

1. WRONG SUPERLATIVE. "The largest single energy movement in the sim" is false. `crates/v3-core/src/simulation/actions/predation.rs:97` computes a steal as `min(requested_amount, victim.energy)` with no configured cap — bounded only by `max_energy` (200.0), i.e. twice the reproduction clamp. Corrected: reproduction is the largest *config-capped* per-event movement and the largest one a creature makes on itself.

2. MAGNITUDE OVERSTATED AT BASELINE. The founder does not request anything near 100: `crates/v3-core/src/creature/founder.rs:343-347` fixes `reproduce_transfer_energy` per profile at 20.0 (V3Alpha1 default), 10.0, and 15.0, carried as VM constant index 5 (founder.rs:323). 100.0 is the clamp ceiling, not a typical transfer. "Heterogeneous across the population today" and "two orders of magnitude" are asserted, not measured — and are unmeasurable precisely because of this gap, so they should be stated as the motivation for measuring rather than as findings.

3. CRITERION MISATTRIBUTED. "Every body trait changes applied simulation behavior and has an observable ecological cost or tradeoff" (T03 track criterion, t03:17) does not bind today: `energy_transfer` is a VM/CGP action operand, not a body trait, and T03.F01 has not started. No open criterion is failed by this absence right now. The live justification is `docs/roadmap.md:57` ("Energy is ecological accounting ... Every new capacity must have an applied cost or tradeoff owned by the feature that introduces it") plus the AGENTS.md applied-behavior rule — sufficient, but not criterion-driven until T03.F07.

4. LINE NUMBERS OFF. The deduction is at reproduction.rs:185, not 195 (the proposal's stated insertion point); the mutation stats writes begin at line 218, not 226.

CONFIRMED SUB-CLAIM, worth keeping: the intake half of "invisible from both directions" holds. Eat gain is `food * reward` clamped at `max_energy` (`simulation/actions/mod.rs:75-82`), where `food` is the variable density consumed, so intake energy is NOT derivable from the stored `typed_eats_total` counts.

title: final_energy_sum is structurally always zero — do not transfer it
missing: A creature's energy at death. The field exists and is written, but the value written is always 0.0, so the signal is absent.
evidence: Declared crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:21, accumulated at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:49 from `observation.final_energy`, which is built as `f64::from(creature.energy.max(0.0))` at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/simulation.rs:152. The observation is only built when the creature is removed, and removal is gated on energy <= 0.0 (crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick/helpers.rs:9-15 and crates/v3-core/src/simulation/tick.rs:184-189), so max(0.0) clamps every reading to zero. Confirmed empirically: after 300 ticks with carriers_observed_total = 89,493, final_energy_sum = 0.0 exactly.
why: It is the one field in MutationValueTotals that carries no information, and any transfer of that struct into the stored report (see gap `lifespan-and-death-via-outcome-summary`) would silently add a permanent zero column to every future closure report and to docs/progress.md. Flagging it now is what keeps that transfer honest. The neighbouring mean_lifetime_energy_sum is the field that actually carries lifetime energy (probe: 1,663,078.8) and is the one worth reading.
criterion: NONE
proposal: Exclude final_energy_sum from any bench.rs transfer, and either delete the field or restate its contract as "energy at death, clamped at zero, therefore always zero" in the doc comment at crates/v3-core/src/simulation/stats.rs:21. No report change. Separately noted and deliberately NOT proposed as gaps after checking: hop_cap_hits reads 0 in every goal report since T11.F15 but was 26 and 8 in t11-f14-...-goal.json, so it is a guard correctly reading zero since the single-visit rule landed, not dead weight; temporal_memory_sensitivity.previous_slots reads 0 in 11 of 13 goal reports but was 2 on seed 22 in the T11.F07 and T11.F14 reports, so it moves and is not dead either.
